The first run toward it; the second run about; the third run together; the fourth run ahead. All go to meet Christ. “The crowds,” he says, “meet Him with flowers and palms” [Note: [Col. 0217] Joan. 12.]. The first offer the Lord wise foolishness; the second, victory over enemies; the third, an abundance of charity; [Col. 0218B] the fourth, joy and gladness. On account of the first, when the Lord comes to Jerusalem it is said: “A very great multitude spread their garments in the way” [Note: [Col. 0217] Matth. 21.]; on account of the second, “they bore branches of palms” [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.]; on account of the third, “branches of olive trees” [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.]; on account of the fourth, flowers.

These were prefigured in the Lord’s way. First He comes from Bethany [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.], which is “the house of obedience”; second, He comes to Bethphage [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.], which is said to mean “the house of feasting,” where warriors are refreshed and strengthened; third, He is said to have come to the Mount of Olives [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.]. By this charity is signified; fourth, He comes to Jerusalem, which is “the vision of peace” sought by explorers. For the first, the living creatures of Ezekiel: “When a voice came above the firmament, they stood and lowered their wings” [Note: [Col. 0217] Ezech. 1.]; for the second: “When the living creatures walked, [Col. 0218C] it was like the sound of camps, like the sound of a multitude” [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.]; for the third: “He heard the sound of wings striking one another” [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.]; for the fourth: “Where the impulse was, thither the spirits went” [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.]. Again: “Their faces and their wings were extended above” [Note: [Col. 0217] Ibid.], etc.

To the first it is said: “You obeyed from the heart that form of teaching into which you were delivered” [Note: [Col. 0217] Rom. 6.]. The second, fearing, say: “In this way wherein I walked they hid a snare for me” [Note: [Col. 0217] Psal. 141.]. The third, confident, say: “Many waters cannot quench charity, neither can floods overwhelm it” [Note: [Col. 0217] Cant. 8.]. There are three waters which extinguish charity: the first, of pleasure; the second, of vanity; the third, of malice. The first is the water of the Flood, the second that of Egypt, the third that of the salt sea [Col. 0218D]. We escape the first by imitation of the Passion of the wood of the Cross; the second by humility; the third frequently through the occasion of a grave fall. Concerning the first, Noah was saved in a wooden ark [Note: [Col. 0217] Gen. 6.]; concerning the second, Moses in a basket of rushes [Note: [Col. 0217] Exod. 2.]; concerning the third, Jonah was borne in the belly of the whale to the shores [Note: [Col. 0217] Jonas 2.].

For some, committing lesser crimes, are too secure, as though in shallow waters, and never repent. But when they commit some most grievous crime, they are as though swallowed in the belly of the whale, that is, in the body of the devil. And thus, [Col. 0219A] because they see that they have fallen grievously, they run eagerly to repentance. For the ark made of wood is the wood of the Cross; Moses’ basket made of papyrus is the virtue of humility. The fourth say with Dindimus, king of the Brahmans: “We are not inhabitants of this world, but strangers.”

Behold, the first spread their garments in the way, that is, they humble themselves before God by an honourable manner of life; the second bring forth palms, that is, they give thanks to the Lord because, through His gift, they have triumphed over their enemies; the third bear branches of olive trees, to show that they love God and neighbour; the fourth display flowers, that is, devotions, while they contemplate in heaven violet-coloured confessors, rose-coloured martyrs, and lily-coloured virgins. Therefore, concerning the fourth she says: “Support me with flowers,” that is, “I desire strength from the examples of the saints” [Col. 0219B]; concerning the third: “Surround me,” that I may be encircled with works of charity; concerning the second: “His left hand is under my head” [Note: [Col. 0219] Cant. 2.], that is, may His mercy sustain me, lest I fall in battle; concerning the first: “And His right hand shall embrace me” [Note: [Col. 0219] Ibid.], that is, may His grace protect me from vanity and pride, which descend from above upon the obedient and humbled as stormy winds.

“But woe to you, because the ways are scattered, and the traveller has ceased from the path” [Note: [Col. 0219] Isai 33.]. And therefore, “the ways of Zion mourn, because there are none who come to the festival” [Note: [Col. 0219] Thren. 1.]. The Lord reproaches the first way for its mourning, saying through the prophet: “I called, and you refused; I stretched out my hand, and there was none who looked” [Note: [Col. 0219] Prov. 1.], etc. Concerning the second [Col. 0219C] it is said: “My people have perished because they lacked knowledge” [Note: [Col. 0219] Ose. 4.], namely, knowledge by which they might be prudent in war. “Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knew it not” [Note: [Col. 0219] Ose. 7.]. “Therefore all his enemies have seized him in narrow places” [Note: [Col. 0219] Thren. 1.]. For “the children of Ephraim, bending and shooting the bow, turned back in the day of battle” [Note: [Col. 0219] Psal. 77.]. Concerning the third it is said: “These are they who have forsaken the straight path and walk in ways of darkness; who rejoice when they have done evil and exult in things most wicked” [Note: [Col. 0219] Prov. 2.]. The fourth mourns for those who ought to seek the things above, to set their minds on the things above [Note: [Col. 0219] Coloss. 3.], but set their minds on earthly things [Note: [Col. 0219] Philipp. 3]. Hence they say: “Our soul is humbled in the dust; our belly cleaves to the earth” [Note: [Col. 0219] Psal. 43.]. Hence comes that grief which the Lord says through the prophet that He endures: [Col. 0219D] “O all you who pass by the way, attend and see whether there is any sorrow like unto my sorrow” [Note: [Col. 0219] Thren. 1.].

For He suffered in soul, He suffered in body, He suffered in spirit. In soul—that is, in the animal nature, which is the lower power of the soul—He suffered fear, weariness, and sadness: fear of the future Passion, weariness from prolonged affliction, sadness at the separation of soul and body. Of the first and second it is said: “He began to fear and to be weary” [Note: [Col. 0219] Marc. 14.]. Of the third: “My soul is sorrowful even unto death” [Note: [Col. 0219] Matth. 26.]. In body He suffered the affliction of the Passion. [Col. 0220A] Look, therefore, upon Him fixed with nails, pierced with a lance, crowned with thorns, struck with scourges, smeared with spittle, flowing with sweat, red with blood, and consider His bodily pain. He suffered also in spirit, which is the higher power of the soul, through compassion. Hence at Lazarus’ tomb He groaned in spirit [Note: [Col. 0219] Joan. 11.], and on the Cross: “Bowing His head, He gave up the spirit” [Note: [Col. 0219] Joan. 19.].

Behold, now all who pass by the way see that there is no sorrow like His sorrow [Note: [Col. 0219] Thren. 1.]. But why? Because there are none who come to that heavenly, not lowest, festival [Note: [Col. 0219] Ibid.]. For there is a threefold festival: the festival of sinners, the festival of the righteous, and the festival of the blessed. The first is celebrated outwardly by the flesh, the second by the spirit, the third by angel and glorified man. The first tends toward death, the second ascends [Col. 0220B] through charity, the third possesses blessedness. The first is called *solemnitas*, that is, “worldliness alone”; the second *solemnitas*, that is, “the vanity of consolation”; the third is called *solemnitas*, that is, “the gentleness of the sun.” For then our sun, that is, Christ, will not have the heat of one punishing, but the radiance of one illumining; there, “by day the sun shall not burn thee, nor the moon by night” [Note: [Col. 0219] Psal. 120.].

Of the first festival the Lord says through the prophet: “My soul hates your new moons and your festivals” [Note: [Col. 0219] Isai. 1.]; of the second: “Appoint a solemn day amid the dense throng, even unto the horn of the altar” [Note: [Col. 0219] Psal. 117.]. Likewise: “Blow the trumpet at the new moon, on the distinguished day of your festival” [Note: [Col. 0219] Psal. 80.]; of the third: “On the fourteenth day at evening is the Passover of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0219] Num. 28.], and [Col. 0220C] “On the fifteenth day you shall celebrate a festival to the most high Lord” [Note: [Col. 0219] Num. 29.]. The fourteen days are the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit and the seven virtues; and then there is the Lord’s Passover, that is, the passing over. For, when these have been well completed, we shall pass with Christ from this world; then, after the sevenfold course of this time has been completed, we shall find the fifteenth and enjoy the octave of the resurrection, because fifteen consists of eight and seven. There we shall celebrate the festival to the most high Lord by seeing the festival. But now let us see by what ways one goes to this festival.

There is the way of commandments, the way of justifications, the way of truth, and the way of charity. Of the first: “I ran in the way of thy commandments, when thou didst enlarge my heart” [Note: [Col. 0219] Psal. 118.]; of the second: “Teach me the way of [Col. 0220D] thy justifications, and I shall meditate on thy wonders” [Note: [Col. 0219] Ibid.]. Of the third: “I have chosen the way of truth; I have not forgotten thy judgments” [Note: [Col. 0219] Ibid.]. Of the fourth Paul says: “I show you a still more excellent way” [Note: [Col. 0219] I Cor. 12], speaking of charity. The first leads down, the second leads in, the third leads to, the fourth leads through. The first leads through the field of obedience; the second into the house of conscience; the third to the treasury of wisdom; the fourth to the homeland of glory. The first is hard, the second safe, the third splendid.

Of the first: “Lead me, O Lord, in thy way, and I will walk in thy truth” [Note: [Col. 0219] Psal 85.]. And: “Thou didst lead [Col. 0221A] thy people like sheep by the hand of Moses and Aaron” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 76.], through whom the commandments of God were given. Again: “Lead me in the path of thy commandments, for I have desired it” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 118.]. Hear its hardness: “Because of the words of thy lips I have kept hard ways” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 16.]. The second is that which leads us into all truth, as the Son of God promised [Note: [Col. 0221] Offic. eccles.]. Hear its safety: “Though I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, because thou art with me” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 22.]. Again: “When thou walkest through fire, thou shalt not be burned, and the flame shall not burn in thee” [Note: [Col. 0221] Isai. 43.].

The way of His commandments is the way of the desert [Note: [Col. 0221] Exod. 13.], by which the children of Israel went to the promised land. But the way of righteousness is that by which Tobias went into Rages, accompanied by a dog which foresaw the ambushes of robbers, and by an angel who foresaw his marriage [Note: [Col. 0221] Tob. 6.]. [Col. 0221B] Of the way of truth, which is splendid and brings one to the goal, it is said: “Send forth thy light and thy truth: they have led me and brought me unto thy holy mountain and into thy tabernacles” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 42.]. This is the path of the righteous which, like a shining light, goes forth and increases unto the perfect day. By this way Isaac went toward the south [Note: [Col. 0221] Gen. 24.], until he became exceedingly great. By this way she wished to go who said: “Tell me, thou whom my soul loves, where thou feedest, where thou liest down at noon” [Note: [Col. 0221] Cant. 1.].

Of the way of charity it is said: “And He led them as a flock in the desert” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 77.], in which He left the ninety-nine sheep [Note: [Col. 0221] Luc. 15.]. This is the lofty way. Hence: “I show you a still more excellent way” [Note: [Col. 0221] I Cor. 12.]. This is the way by which Christ, ascending, “led captivity captive on high” [Note: [Col. 0221] Ephes. 4.]; by which the cows drew [Col. 0221C] the ark of the Lord toward Beth-shemesh [Note: [Col. 0221] I Reg. 6.], which is said to mean “house of the sun”; by which Jonathan, crawling on hands and feet, climbed the mountain and overcame the Philistines’ garrison [Note: [Col. 0221] I Reg. 14.]; by which in Solomon’s Temple one ascended by spiral stairs to the upper chamber [Note: [Col. 0221] III Reg. 6.].

“Support me with flowers.”

[CARD.] That is, with the beginnings of good works; and surround me with apples, so that the flowers may pass into ripe fruits and beginnings may attain the completion of perfection. And I cry this because I languish from love, that is, because of love. For I am strong in myself, but languish in you; steadfast in myself, but am made weak in you; when you are scandalized, I burn; healthy in myself, but in you I am wounded in charity. This wound of charity compels me to cry [Col. 0221D] and say: “Support me with flowers; surround me with apples.” For as regards my own person, I am well established, because:

“His left hand is under my head, and His right hand shall embrace me.”

[THO.] Because the Bridegroom saw her so faithful in His absence and so fervent, He could endure her languor no longer, and returned. Thus she bursts forth in thanksgiving, saying: “His left hand is under my head, and His right hand shall embrace me.” For the left hand is the threat of punishment, which is beneath the head, [Col. 0222A] not above it, because she serves not from fear but from love. Hence she rejoices in the promise of the kingdom, which is the right hand. She wishes to be supported by the example of saints who lived well, so that, kindled by their zeal, she may blush at the coldness of her own torpor; blushing, may shudder; shuddering, may conquer it; conquering, may drive it away; and, by their example, may kindle her whole self intensely in the sweetness of divine love and, once kindled, pour it forth again.

Rightly does the Bride glory that she has found rest between the Bridegroom’s hands, “because in His hand are all the ends of the earth” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 94.]. There are four ends which are in His hand. The first is creation; the second, the miserable consummation of creation; the third, the beginning of man’s re-creation; the fourth, the restoration of that same man in glory. Of the first it is said: “O Wisdom, reaching mightily from end to end” [Note: [Col. 0221] Sap. 8.]: from the end, that is, from the beginning of creation, to the end of the final dissolution. Of the second the prophet says: “The end has come; the end has come” [Note: [Col. 0221] Ezech. 7.]. And elsewhere: “The end of all flesh has come” [Note: [Col. 0221] Thren. 4.], that is, of those living carnally. Of the third, a certain philosopher says: “That whose end is good is itself also good.” Of the fourth, David says: “Delights are at thy right hand unto the end” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 15.].

According to the first two ends, left and right may be understood thus: the left hand is the misery of hell. Hence the Judge says to those who shall be on His left: “Depart, ye cursed, into everlasting fire” [Note: [Col. 0221] Matth. 25.]. For there He will place the goats on the left [Note: [Col. 0221] Ibid.]. The right hand, however, is the power of creating and punishing, whether temporally or eternally. Eternally: then in His right hand is a fiery law, namely, one which, if not kept, will be punished with eternal fire. Temporally, Jeremiah says: [Col. 0222C] “He bent His bow as an enemy; He strengthened His right hand as a foe” [Note: [Col. 0221] Thren. 2.]. Again: “Thy right hand, O Lord, is magnified in strength; thy right hand, O Lord, has struck the enemy” [Note: [Col. 0221] Exod. 15.]. Therefore, if I consider hell tormenting beneath me, His left hand is beneath my head; if the Creator who punishes above me, His right hand shall embrace me.

It should be noted that there is the sensual man, the rational man, and the spiritual man. The first entangles himself in pleasures; the second considers the natures of things; the third applies himself to heavenly things. Each of these has his own left and right hands by which he may receive an embrace. The rational man has beneath him the punishment of hell, which he flees; above him, the power of the one who punishes, [Col. 0222D] to which he flees. Hence Abraham, whose name means “exalted father,” namely reason, says to Lot, whose name means “turning aside,” that is, sensuality: “If thou goest to the left, I will take the right” [Note: [Col. 0221] Gen. 13.]. The sensual man has adversity as his left hand and pleasurable prosperity as his right. Hence Abraham continues: “And if thou choosest the right, I will take the left” [Note: [Col. 0221] Ibid.]. Hence David: “Let the devil stand at his right hand” [Note: [Col. 0221] Psal. 108.]. The spiritual man has spiritual goods as the left hand beneath his head, upon which he rests his head—that is, his soul. Above is the right hand: that is, he awaits eternal goods from above.

God’s left hand is placed beneath [Col. 0223A] the fallen, beneath the righteous, and beneath the devout: beneath the fallen, to raise them; beneath the righteous, lest they fail; beneath the devout, that they may sleep and rest together in peace [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 4.]. It raises from the dunghill, prevents failure in labour, and gives rest in the knowledge of heavenly things. Of the first: “Raising the needy from the dust and lifting the poor from the dunghill” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 112.]. Of the second: “Let us not fail in doing good; for in due season we shall reap, if we do not fail” [Note: [Col. 0223] Gal. 6.]. Of the third: “I sleep, and my heart watches” [Note: [Col. 0223] Cant. 5.]. The first says: “When he falls, he shall not be dashed down, because the Lord places His hand beneath him” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 36.]. The second says: “Send forth thy hand from on high; rescue me and deliver me from many waters and from the hand of strange children” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 143.]. The third says: “He has protected me in the shadow of His hand” [Note: [Col. 0223] Isai. 49.].

According to the first, it is called *laeva*, as though *laesis valens*, “strong for the injured”; [Col. 0223B] according to the second, *laeva*, as though *leniens vadentes*, “soothing those who journey”; according to the third, *laeva*, as though *laeta vacantibus*, “joyful for those at rest.” The right hand, moreover, which is placed beneath, does three things: first it touches, second it clasps, third it unites. It touches, that one may love; it clasps, that one may cling inseparably to God; it unites, that one may rejoice together with Him in the kingdom. In the first, God is loved above all things; in the second, one becomes one spirit with Him; in the third, in the kingdom man and Christ will be one head and body. Concerning the first it is said of the vine which He transferred from Egypt: “Perfect it which thy right hand planted” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 79.]. For it is planted in the first, grows in the second, and bears fruit in the third. Of the second it is said: “Indeed thy hand shall lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 138.]. Of the third David says, seeing in spirit as though [Col. 0223C] already fulfilled: “Thy right hand received me” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 62.]. Again: “The queen stood at thy right hand” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 44.]. The first says: “The charity of God has been poured forth in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us” [Note: [Col. 0223] Rom. 5.]. The second says: “My soul clung after thee” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 62.]. The third: “God shall be all in all” [Note: [Col. 0223] I Cor. 15.].

Therefore the soul, thus suspended between this left hand and the left hand [sic], rightly says with the Bride: “His left hand is beneath my head, and His right hand shall embrace me.” Yet it sometimes happens that a person illumined by understanding of heavenly things has, through the violence of love, too little discernment, when he raises himself to the right hand and remains in the left. For the understanding, attracted by the delight of heavenly things, sometimes forgets lower works of mercy; at other times, intent upon works of mercy, [Col. 0223D] it forgets heavenly things. This understanding is Joseph, whose name means “increase”: he placed his firstborn son at his father’s right hand, namely Manasseh, whose name means “forgetfulness,” and Ephraim, whose name means “fruitfulness,” at his left. But Jacob crossed his hands, placing his right hand upon Ephraim and his left upon Manasseh [Note: [Col. 0223] Gen. 48.].

“And lest perhaps the Bride, who was now embraced by the Bridegroom with both [Col. 0224A] hands, should arrogate to herself an occasion for pride from so great a judgment of love, the Apostle admonishes her thus: ‘Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, and He will exalt you in the time of visitation’” [Note: [Col. 0223] I Petr. 5.]. Truly God’s hand is mighty for benefits, mighty for punishments, mighty for rewards: for benefits, by which we may be directed; for punishments, by which we may be corrected; for rewards, to which we may be raised: that we may be directed by the hand of righteousness, corrected from the error of folly, and raised to be possessors of glory. Concerning the first it is said: “The right hand of the Lord has wrought strength” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 117.]. Concerning the third: “The right hand of the Lord has exalted me” [Note: [Col. 0223] Ibid.]. Concerning the second, the same: “The right hand of the Lord has wrought strength” [Note: [Col. 0223] Ibid.].

In the first we are strengthened with God’s mighty hand; in the second we are humbled beneath God’s mighty hand; in the third we rejoice in God’s mighty hand. Concerning the first, it is said of Joseph: [Col. 0224B] “For the hand of the Lord was with him” [Note: [Col. 0223] Gen. 39.]. Concerning the second, here: “Humble yourselves beneath the mighty hand of God” [Note: [Col. 0223] I Petr. 5.]. Concerning the third: “The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and no torment of malice shall touch them” [Note: [Col. 0223] Sap. 3.]. In the first it is said that we may be directed in the way of righteousness. Hence it is said: “According to the blessing of Aaron upon his people, direct us in the way of righteousness” [Note: [Col. 0223] Eccli. 36.]. In the second we are corrected from the error of folly. Hence: “By the strength of thy hand I have failed away. In rebukes, because of iniquity thou hast corrected man” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 38.]. Of the third it is said that it will lead to possession of glory. Hence: “Raising the needy from the dust, and lifting the poor from the dunghill, that he may sit with princes and possess a throne of glory” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psal. 112.].

The hand mighty for benefits does three things: [Col. 0224C] it commands the soul now to devotion, now to contrition; the tongue, to praise and confession; the hands, to action. Concerning the first: “My beloved put his hand through the opening, and my belly trembled at his touch” [Note: [Col. 0223] Cant. 5.]. Of contrition it is said: “Son of man, dig through the wall; and I dug, and behold four-footed beasts, creeping things, and birds” [Note: [Col. 0223] Ezech. 8.]. These animals are sometimes conceived from without through the exterior senses and sent inward; sometimes they are first conceived inwardly and conveyed outward. Of the first: “Do not carry our burdens on the Sabbath day, nor bring them in through the gates of Jerusalem” [Note: [Col. 0223] Jerem. 17.]. Of the second it is said in the same place: “And do not cast our burdens out of the city on the Sabbath day” [Note: [Col. 0223] Ibid.]. Of the first Job says: “I made a covenant with my eyes [Col. 0224D] that I would not think upon a virgin” [Note: [Col. 0223] Job 31.]. Of the second: “If my eye has followed my heart, and a stain has clung to my hands” [Note: [Col. 0223] Ibid.].

It commands the tongue to praise and confession. Hence: “The Lord put forth His hand and touched my mouth” [Note: [Col. 0223] Jerem. 1]. Of action: “Thou hast held my right hand, and according to thy will thou hast led me” [Note: [Col. 0223] Psalm. 72.]. And lest one conceive vain glory from works, it adds: “He protected me in the shadow of His hand” [Note: [Col. 0223] Isai. 49.]. Of this hand [Col. 0225A] it is said: “The Spirit of the Lord adorned the heavens, and by His travailing hand the twisting serpent was brought forth” [Note: [Col. 0225] Job 26.].

Behold, you have been strengthened beneath the mighty hand of God, which is mighty for benefits. It follows that “you humble yourselves beneath the mighty hand of God” [Note: [Col. 0225] I Petr. 5.] for punishments: “For whom the Lord loves He corrects; and He scourges every son whom He receives” [Note: [Col. 0225] Hebr. 12.]. Or the grace of the Lord is mighty in the reprobate: “For He wounds and heals; He strikes, and His hands make whole” [Note: [Col. 0225] Job 5.]. Why did “a living man murmur, a man for his sins” [Note: [Col. 0225] Thren. 3.]? Now that murmuring, which profits nothing, has ceased, spare your tongue from detraction. “For an idle word shall not go empty, and a lying mouth kills the soul” [Note: [Col. 0225] Sap. 1.]. “Neither murmur,” says the Apostle, “as some of them murmured and perished by the destroyer” [Col. 0225B] [Note: [Col. 0225] I Cor. 10.]. “O man, who art thou that thou shouldst answer God?” [Note: [Col. 0225] Rom. 9.]. Does the clay say to the potter, “Why hast thou made me thus?” [Note: [Col. 0225] Isai. 45.]? If thou desirest to contend with Him, thou canst not answer Him one thing for a thousand, for He is wise in heart and mighty in strength. Who has resisted Him and had peace? [Note: [Col. 0225] Job 9.]

What, then, will you say at the Lord’s judgment, if you have not been humbled like a little child? “I called and you refused; I stretched out my hand and there was none who looked. Therefore, because you despised my counsel and neglected my rebukes, I also will laugh at your destruction” [Note: [Col. 0225] Prov. 1.]. Let us therefore humble ourselves under the mighty hand of God [Note: [Col. 0225] I Petr. 5.]. “For he who humbles himself shall be exalted,” says the Lord [Note: [Col. 0225] Luc. 14.]. “Unless you become like little children, you shall not enter the kingdom of heaven” [Note: [Col. 0225] Matth. 18.].—“For upon whom shall [Col. 0225C] my Spirit rest, save upon the humble and quiet man, who trembles at my words?” [Note: [Col. 0225] Isai. 66.] Hear the reward of this humility: “That He may exalt you in the day of visitation” [Note: [Col. 0225] I Petr. 5.].

There are four visitations. A person visits himself; a neighbour visits; a teacher visits; God visits: a person through self-examination, a neighbour through admonition, a teacher through exhortation, God through inspiration. The first takes counsel concerning his own salvation; the second rejoices because he benefits his brother; the third assails the disciple’s vices; the fourth exalts the one visited in His grace. In self-examination, the first must take care how to remove iniquity so as to preserve purity of conscience, and how to maintain steadfastness against temptations. Then let him transfer his heart to heavenly charity. Hence [Col. 0225D] in Job: “If thou removest the iniquity that is in thy hand, and injustice is not in thy tabernacle” [Note: [Col. 0225] Job 11]: behold the first. “Then thou shalt be able to lift up thy face without stain” [Note: [Col. 0225] Job 11]: behold the second. “And thou shalt be steadfast” [Note: [Col. 0225] Ibid.]: behold the third. “And thou shalt not fear; thou shalt also forget misery” [Note: [Col. 0225] Ibid.]: behold the fourth.

This man says: “One thing have I asked of the Lord, this will I seek: that I may dwell in the house of the Lord, that I may behold the will of the Lord and visit His temple” [Note: [Col. 0225] Psal. 26.].—“For the temple of God is holy, which temple you are” [Note: [Col. 0225] I Cor. 3.]: this is the first visitation. [Col. 0226A]

The neighbour performs the second visitation, inviting one to humility, meekness, charity, and patience. Hence the Apostle: “I beseech you to walk worthily of the calling wherewith you were called, with humility”: behold the first; “and meekness”: behold the second; “with patience”: this is the third; “bearing with one another in charity” [Note: [Col. 0225] Ephes. 4.]: this is the fourth. Hence: “Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their tribulations” [Note: [Col. 0225] Jac. 1.]. The first takes counsel thus: “I shall be spotless with Him and shall keep myself from my iniquity” [Note: [Col. 0225] Psal. 17.]. The second rejoices because he benefits his neighbour, saying with the Apostle: “Thanks be to God that you were once slaves of sin, but have obeyed from the heart that same form of teaching into which you were delivered” [Col. 0226B] [Note: [Col. 0225] Rom. 6.].

The third visits by assailing vices, according to: “Reprove, entreat, rebuke” [Note: [Col. 0225] II Tim. 4.]. Reprove the ignorant; entreat the well-disposed; rebuke the obstinate. Because he is a teacher, he assails vices in the words of Isaiah: “Woe to the sinful nation, a people burdened with iniquity, an evil seed, wicked children!” [Note: [Col. 0225] Isai. 1.] Of these it is said: “The kite from heaven knew its coming, etc.; but Israel did not know me” [Note: [Col. 0225] Jer. 8.]. And it is added: “Because they did not keep the time of their visitation” [Note: [Col. 0225] Luc. 19.]. For they had visitors, namely the patriarchs, prophets, and holy fathers. The visitation of God follows.

Thus he visits: first, he chastises, that he may call back from sin; second, he permits temptation, that he may test; third, he pours in grace, that he may preserve; fourth, he removes [Col. 0226C] from this life, that he may exalt. Of the first: “I will visit their iniquities with the rod, and their sins with scourges. But I will not destroy my mercy from him” [Note: [Col. 0225] Ps. 88]. “Lord, when you are angry, you will remember mercy” [Note: [Col. 0225] Tob. 3]. Of the second: “You visit him at dawn and suddenly test him” [Note: [Col. 0225] Job 7]. Of the third: “Your visitation has preserved my spirit” [Note: [Col. 0225] Job 10]. Of the fourth, here: “That he may exalt you on the day of visitation” [Note: [Col. 0225] 1 Pet. 5].

Therefore do not be, in the first case, Ish-bosheth, who made the girl a gatekeeper [Note: [Col. 0225] 2 Kings 4]. Do not say, in the second: “Am I my brother’s keeper?” [Note: [Col. 0225] Gen. 4]. Do not be, in the third, Eli, who did not rebuke his sons [Note: [Col. 0225] 1 Kings 3]. See to it, I say, that you are not that rich man who was clothed in purple and fine linen [Note: [Col. 0225] Luke 16]. The day of the Lord’s visitation will be at judgment [Note: [Col. 0225] Judith 1]. There he will exalt those who humbled themselves [Col. 0226D] under the mighty hand of God [Note: [Col. 0225] 1 Pet. 5].

To that exaltation he thus invites the good: “Arise, hasten, my beloved. For now winter has passed; the rain has gone and withdrawn” [Note: [Col. 0225] Song 2]. Likewise: Come, my chosen one, and I will set my throne upon you. Likewise: “Come from Lebanon, bride; come, you shall be crowned” [Note: [Col. 0225] Song 4].—“Come from Lebanon,” through the first visitation; “come,” through the second; “come,” through the third; “in the fourth you shall be crowned.” Therefore let a person visit himself; let him visit his neighbour; let a prelate visit him; otherwise their soul shall be required from their hand.

Let us therefore cast all care [Col. 0227A] upon him. There is concern for temporal things, concern for spiritual things, and concern for heavenly things. We may have the first for bodily necessity, not for excess; the second for the holiness of the soul, not for boastful vanity; the third for the happiness of the whole person, not for philosophical curiosity. Of the first: “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things” [Note: [Col. 0227] Luke 10]. Of excess he says in the Gospel: “Do not be anxious, saying: What shall we eat? or What shall we drink? and why are you anxious about clothing?” [Note: [Col. 0227] Matt. 6]. Of the second it is said: “Not slothful in diligence” [Note: [Col. 0227] Rom. 12]. Likewise the Apostle: “Be diligent to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace” [Note: [Col. 0227] Eph. 4]. Of the third: “O man, I will show you what the Lord [Col. 0227B] requires of you” [Note: [Col. 0227] Mic. 6]. Therefore love mercy and do judgment [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 32], and walk diligently with your God, until he exalts you to that glory in which he lives and is glorified with the Father and the Holy Spirit unto all ages of ages. Amen.

> His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.

[CARD.] By the left hand are understood all the goods, virtues, and graces bestowed on the way, so that one may come to the right hand of eternal blessedness. Therefore she says: *His left hand is under my head, and his right hand shall embrace me.* As if she said: So that my head—that is, my mind—may rest sweetly, the Lord has made for me a pillow out of all spiritual goods, which are bestowed especially on the way by the left hand; and his right hand, [Col. 0227C] in which are delights, shall embrace me singularly, so that, held more tightly, I may be more closely joined to him in his goods. There follows, in the person of the Son addressing the young women, the saying:

> I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and stags of the fields, that you do not rouse or awaken my beloved until she herself wills it.

[THO.] The young women, whom he calls daughters of Jerusalem, are forbidden to disturb the bride, who had fallen asleep between the bridegroom’s left and right hands. Although weak, they nevertheless cling to her in hope of advancing and of journeying to Jerusalem; and because here they cannot do so by themselves, they need her aid. But they are forbidden to awaken even her except according to her own will. That sleep is contemplation.

The stags and gazelles by whom they are adjured are understood to be souls of the good and angels, because of their light leaps. Likewise, the gazelle sees keenly, delights in high and remote places, runs swiftly, and by rapid flight avoids human gaze. He saw keenly who said: “But we, with unveiled face, behold the glory of God and are transformed into the same image from glory to glory” [Note: [Col. 0227] 2 Cor. 3]. He was on high who said: “I have become like a solitary sparrow upon the roof” [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 101]. David ran swiftly when he said: “I ran the way of your commandments when you enlarged [Col. 0228A] my heart” [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 118]. He had fled to safe places who said: “Behold, I fled far away and remained in solitude” [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 54].

Stags walk together, carrying one another’s chin. These are those who are a consolation to each other, as the Apostle says: “Bear one another’s burdens” [Note: [Col. 0227] Gal. 6]. They kill serpents whose eyes are dim. Thus David: “In the morning I slew all the sinners of the land, that I might destroy from the city of the Lord all workers of iniquity” [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 100]. Thirsting, they run to the fountain and thus receive light. Hence: “With you is the fountain of life, and in your light we shall see light” [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 35]. They put off old age, saying: “Behold, we have left all things and followed you” [Note: [Col. 0227] Matt. 19].

Likewise, two kinds of contemplation are shown here: namely, the sight of one’s own circumspection, represented by the stag which devours serpents and receives sight [Col. 0228B]. This occurs in the fields either of the heart or of conduct. But the gazelle ascends mountains and sees keenly. This is the soul which, as though climbing to the high ground, contemplates God. Isaiah was in this state when he said: “I saw the Lord seated upon a throne high and lifted up” [Note: [Col. 0227] Isa. 6].

This throne is threefold: the first high, the second exalted, the third lifted up. The first is consideration of the fabric of the world; the second, contemplation of the heavenly homeland; the third, contemplation of the divine majesty. In the first God is seen as praiseworthy because of his works; in the second, lovable because of his rewards; in the third, wonderful in incomparable power. Of the first: “Praise him, sun and moon” [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 148]. Of the second: “What eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man, the things which he has prepared for those who love [Col. 0228C] him” [Note: [Col. 0227] 1 Cor. 2]. Of the third: “God is glorious in his saints, wonderful in his majesty” [Note: [Col. 0227] Ps. 69].

In the first are creation, re-creation, and restoration: creation of every existing thing; re-creation of the sinner; restoration from corruption. Of the first: “In the beginning God created heaven and earth” [Note: [Col. 0227] Gen. 1]. Of the second: “Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world” [Note: [Col. 0227] John 1]. Likewise: “Come, Lord, and do not delay” [Note: [Col. 0227] Office of the Church, for Advent], etc. Of the third: “He will reform the body of our lowliness, conformed to the body of his glory” [Note: [Col. 0227] Phil. 3].

In the second throne, that is, the exalted one, there are three lovable things: the brightness of the kingdom, the fellowship of angels, and the security of those who dwell there. Of the first: “That city has no need of sun or moon to shine in it, because the glory of God will illumine it, and the Lamb will be its lamp” [Note: [Col. 0227] Rev. 21]. Of the second: “We [Col. 0228D] shall not be strangers and foreigners, but citizens with the saints and members of God’s household” [Note: [Col. 0227] Eph. 2]. Of the third: “All shall feed and lie down, and there shall be none to terrify them” [Note: [Col. 0227] Zeph. 3].

In the third throne there are four things to consider. First, we see his incorruptible nature and grieve over our own weakness. Hence Abraham: “I will speak to my Lord, though I am dust and ashes” [Note: [Col. 0227] Gen. 18]. Second, we see his purity and mercy, and blush for our fault. Hence Isaiah: “Woe is me, because I am a man of unclean lips, for I have seen the Lord with [Col. 0229A] my eyes” [Note: [Col. 0229] Isa. 6]. And Job: “I heard of you by the hearing of the ear; but now my eye sees you. Therefore I rebuke myself, and do penance in dust and ashes” [Note: [Col. 0229] Job 6]. Third, we see his riches and groan over our poverty. Hence Daniel, seeing the angel, said: “I fell upon the ground, and no spirit remained in me, nor had I any strength” [Note: [Col. 0229] Dan. 10]. Fourth, we see his glory and see in him our salvation. Hence Jacob, seeing him, said: “I saw the Lord face to face, and my soul was saved” [Note: [Col. 0229] Gen. 32].

Thus the Church sings devoutly, seeing and desiring the salvation in which are the joys of the saints, saying: “The souls of the saints rejoice in heaven,” not with temporal joy, nor now with spiritual joy, but with heavenly joy.

For there is temporal joy, spiritual joy, and [Col. 0229B] heavenly joy. First, the souls of the wicked rejoice on earth; second, the souls of the righteous rejoice in gifts; third, the souls of the blessed rejoice in heaven. The first are deceived by the world’s falsehood; the second are imbued with God’s grace; the third have followed Christ’s footsteps. The first, because they have laboured for love of the world, will therefore be tormented with the devil in hell. The second, because they despise the kingdom of the world, therefore merit eternal punishment. The third, because they have poured out their blood for Christ’s love, will therefore reign with Christ eternally.

The first rejoice with a threefold joy: first because they misuse temporal goods; second in the glory of their name; third “because they rejoice when they have done evil and exult in the worst things” [Note: [Col. 0229] Prov. 2]. These are Solomon’s three difficult things: the way of a ship in the sea, the way of an eagle flying [Col. 0229C] in the sky, and the way of a serpent upon a rock. The first “trust in their own strength and glory in the multitude of their riches” [Note: [Col. 0229] Ps. 48]. Hence the poet [Note: [Col. 0229] Ovid, *Remedies for Love* 746]:

> Riches have ruined ages by shameful luxury.  
> Luxurious love is nourished by wealth.

Such people say: “Come, let us intoxicate ourselves with wine and costly ointments” [Note: [Col. 0229] Wis. 2], etc. But Job shows what these things will require: “They take up the tambourine and harp; they rejoice at the sound of the organ. They spend their days in prosperity, and in a moment descend into hell” [Note: [Col. 0229] Job 21]. So that rich man who feasted splendidly every day was buried in hell [Note: [Col. 0229] Luke 16].

The second “have called their lands by their own names” [Note: [Col. 0229] Ps. 48]. Hence James: “Now you exult in your boastings; every such exultation is evil” [Col. 0229D] [Note: [Col. 0229] Jas. 4]. And the Lord: “Do not rejoice in this, that demons are subject to you” [Note: [Col. 0229] Luke 10]. But these things have an end. Hence Job: “I know from the beginning that the praise of the wicked is brief and the joy of the hypocrite lasts but a moment” [Note: [Col. 0229] Job 20]. And Nebuchadnezzar: “Is not this Babylon which I have established for the glory and splendour of my kingdom?” [Note: [Col. 0229] Dan. 4]. And he heard: “To you it is spoken, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom is taken from you” [Note: [Col. 0229] ibid.].

To the third it is said: “Why do you glory in wickedness, you who are mighty in iniquity?” [Note: [Col. 0229] Ps. 51]. [Col. 0230A] These rejoice when they have done evil and exult in the worst things [Note: [Col. 0229] Prov. 2]. Hence the poet:

> Therefore some men can sleep in no other way:  
> Quarrelling brings sleep to them.

And Job: “If my heart rejoiced secretly, and I was glad at the downfall of him who hated me” [Note: [Col. 0229] Job 31]. Hence it is written: “They made the king glad in their wickedness” [Note: [Col. 0229] Hos. 7]. Such were Nero and Herod. Of all these it is said: “Woe to you who laugh now, for you also shall mourn” [Note: [Col. 0229] Luke 6]. And Solomon: “Laughter is mingled with sorrow, and mourning occupies the end of joy” [Note: [Col. 0229] Prov. 14]. Likewise: “I accounted laughter an error, and said to joy: Why are you vainly deceived?” [Note: [Col. 0229] Eccl. 2]. And Tobias: “What joy shall I have, I who sit in darkness and cannot see the light of heaven?” [Note: [Col. 0229] Tob. 5].

Conversely it is said: “Blessed are those who [Col. 0230B] mourn, for they shall be comforted” [Note: [Col. 0229] Matt. 5]. But these men shall be tormented with the devil in hell. And James: “Your laughter will be turned into mourning, and your joy into the cries of weeping” [Note: [Col. 0229] Jas. 4].

Spiritual joy is threefold. First, we rejoice in avoiding an evil; second, in attaining a good; third, in hope of the kingdom to come. Of the first: “Rejoice, Jerusalem” [Note: [Col. 0229] Office of the Church]; of the second: “And celebrate a feast-day, all you who love her” [Note: [Col. 0229] ibid.]; of the third: “Rejoice with great joy” [Note: [Col. 0229] ibid.]. The first belongs to beginners, the second to the virtuous, the third to the perfect. The first sing upon the harp, the second upon the psaltery, the third in jubilation. For the first sounds from below, the second from above, and the third serves love. The first offer God honour for sins forgiven; [Col. 0230C] the second thanksgiving for goods bestowed; the third devotion for goods to come.

In the first, a person rejoices, his neighbour rejoices, an angel rejoices, and God rejoices. Of the first, Paul says: “I was formerly a blasphemer, persecutor, and insolent man, but I obtained mercy” [Note: [Col. 0229] 1 Tim. 1]. “By the grace of God I am what I am” [Note: [Col. 0229] 1 Cor. 15]. Of the second, that good father says: “Son, it was fitting to rejoice and feast, because my son was dead and has come to life; he was lost and has been found” [Note: [Col. 0229] Luke 15]. Of the third: “That good shepherd placed the hundredth sheep upon his shoulders with joy, and brought it back to the flock” [Note: [Col. 0229] ibid.].

“All discipline for the present seems not to be a matter of joy but of sorrow” [Note: [Col. 0229] Heb. 12]. Likewise: “A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers [Col. 0230D] the anguish, because a human being has been born into the world” [Note: [Col. 0229] John 16].

Concerning the attainment of good, that is, of virtues, the Apostle says: “The kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit” [Note: [Col. 0229] Rom. 14]. Likewise: “Rejoice always in the Lord with your heart. Again I say: rejoice with your body” [Note: [Col. 0229] Phil. 4]. “If you loved me, you would indeed rejoice,” he says [Note: [Col. 0229] John 14]. Likewise: “I shall come to you, and your heart shall rejoice” [Note: [Col. 0229] John 16], namely because of the goods of the Holy Spirit. And Zacchaeus received the Lord joyfully into his house [Note: [Col. 0229] Luke 19], namely in the reception [Col. 0231A] of gifts.

They rejoice in hope of the kingdom, as Job says: “As those digging for treasure, and they rejoice exceedingly when they find the grave” [Note: [Col. 0231] Job 3].—“Glorious things have been spoken of you, city of God” [Note: [Col. 0231] Ps. 86], because “the dwelling-place of all who rejoice is in you” [Note: [Col. 0231] ibid.]. Therefore, “I rejoiced in the things said to me: We shall go into the house of the Lord” [Note: [Col. 0231] Ps. 121]. The first are nourished with milk; the second are comforted from the breasts of her consolation; the third feast at the entrance of the glory of the nations. To these it is said: “Rejoice and exult, because your reward is abundant in heaven” [Note: [Col. 0231] Matt. 5]. Nor is this surprising, because “in their land they shall possess double; everlasting joy shall be theirs” [Note: [Col. 0231] Isa. 61]. For they will rejoice in the good things of their Lord: grain, wine, and oil. With such joy rejoice in heaven the souls of the saints who have followed Christ’s footsteps [Col. 0231B].

For they have followed Christ’s footsteps in three things: religious conduct, the purity of chastity, and the suffering of martyrdom. These three were prefigured in the tabernacle of Moses. For conduct there were goat-hair cloths; for the second, violet-blue skins; for the third, ram-skins dyed red. Of conduct: “They went about in sheepskins and goatskins, needy, distressed, afflicted, of whom the world was not worthy” [Note: [Col. 0231] Heb. 11]. Of these the reprobate will say at the end: “Are not these those whom we once held in derision and as a likeness of reproach? We fools considered their life madness and their end without honour. [Col. 0231C] Behold how they have been numbered among the children of God” [Note: [Col. 0231] Wis. 5].

> These are they at whom the world that held them recoiled:  
> for with its barren bloom through the dry waste  
> it utterly despised them; yet they followed you,  
> good King Christ, from heaven.

Therefore the martyrs have followed Christ’s footsteps. For “they were stoned, sawn asunder, and died by the slaughter of the sword” [Note: [Col. 0231] Heb. 11].

> For they trampled the furies and fierce violence  
> of men, and savage blows;  
> the tearing claw gave way before them bravely  
> and did not rend their inmost parts.

Likewise:

> They were struck by swords like sheep;  
> no murmuring sounds, no complaint;  
> but with silent heart, a mind rightly conscious  
> preserves patience. [Col. 0231D]

But hear the reward:

> What voice, what tongue can recount  
> the gifts that you prepare for your martyrs? etc.

Likewise, to them it is said: “Count it all joy when you fall into various temptations” [Note: [Col. 0231] Jas. 1]. You indeed shall have tribulation in the world. “But the world shall rejoice, while you shall be sorrowful. Yet your sorrow shall be turned into joy” [Note: [Col. 0231] John 16]. These look to Jesus, the author and finisher of faith [Note: [Col. 0231] Heb. 12], who, for the joy set before him, endured the cross, despising confession, and sits at God’s right hand.

The first are the goat-hair cloths [Col. 0232A]; these, however, are the ram-skins dyed red; the third are the violet-blue skins, which have the colour of heaven. For chastity is a heavenly life. To live in the flesh beyond the flesh is not a human but an angelic life. The first deny themselves, the second take up their cross, the third follow Christ. For “virgins, clothed in a white robe, follow the Lamb wherever he goes” [Note: [Col. 0231] Rev. 14]. In every other respect confessors and martyrs follow Christ, except when he proceeds in the beauty of virginity. For in these the bridegroom delights, “who feeds among the lilies” [Note: [Col. 0231] Song 6], surrounded by companies of virgins.

The first, fleeing Jezebel—that is, the vain flux of this world—go with Elijah to Horeb, the mountain of God, resting under the shade of the juniper [Note: [Col. 0231] 3 Kings 19]. The second [Col. 0232B], with Stephen, have come out of great tribulation and washed their robes in the blood of the Lamb [Note: [Col. 0231] Office of the Church]. The third, with the wise virgins, purify their lamps. When these are lit, they await the coming of the Bridegroom [Note: [Col. 0231] Matt. 25]. All these have sown in tears and therefore shall reap in exultation. For “going they went and wept, casting their seed; but coming they shall come with exultation, carrying their sheaves” [Note: [Col. 0231] Ps. 125]. “They rejoice before you,” he says, “as they rejoice at harvest; and as victors exult when prey has been captured, when they divide the spoils” [Note: [Col. 0231] Isa. 9]. When “the holy angels shall exult; they shall rejoice in their resting-places” [Note: [Col. 0231] Office of the Church]. Behold, in heaven rejoice the souls of the saints who have followed Christ’s footsteps.

The first joy is triumphant, the second exultant, [Col. 0232C] the third exalting: the first arises from the world’s error, the second from God’s love, the third in the honour of the kingdom. Of the first: “I accounted laughter an error, and said to joy: Why are you vainly deceived?” [Note: [Col. 0231] Eccl. 2]. Of the second: “If you loved me, you would indeed rejoice” [Note: [Col. 0231] John 14]. Of the third: “Because they have poured out their blood for love of Christ, therefore they shall reign with Christ eternally” [Note: [Col. 0231] Office of the Church].

Here it should be noted that there is a kingdom of power, a kingdom of wisdom, and a kingdom of joy. The glory of this threefold kingdom is threefold: the first strengthens the saints with every power of virtue; the second illumines them with the brightness of truth; the third makes them blessed in heaven by the sweetness of divine delight. Hence we ask in the Lord’s Prayer: “May your kingdom come” [Note: [Col. 0231] Matt. 6]. Let the kingdom of power therefore come, to strengthen us who are weak; let [Col. 0232D] the kingdom of wisdom come, to enlighten us who are blind; let the kingdom of joy come, to gladden and console us who are sad.

Of the first: “His power is an everlasting power” [Note: [Col. 0231] Dan. 4]. Of the second: “If I cast out demons by the finger of God, then surely the kingdom of God has come upon you” [Note: [Col. 0231] Luke 12], that is, the understanding of wisdom reigns in us. Hence Wisdom herself says: “Through me kings reign” [Note: [Col. 0231] Prov. 8]. Of the third: “O how glorious is the kingdom in which all the saints reign—or rejoice—with Christ; but they shall reign with Christ eternally” [Note: [Col. 0231] Office of the Church].

It belongs to one who reigns to trample adversities; it belongs to one who rejoices to delight in blessings [Col. 0233A] obtained. Therefore they shall reign because they have trampled the snares of sin, the corruption of this misery, and the punishment of Gehenna. Hence David: “I will exalt you, Lord, because you have received me” [Note: [Col. 0233] Ps. 29], etc. “Lord my God, I cried to you, and you healed me” [Note: [Col. 0233] ibid.]. From the misery of corruption: “Lord, you brought my soul up from hell; you saved me from those descending into the pit” [Note: [Col. 0233] ibid.], lest the torture of Gehenna’s fire afflict me. Behold, these reign.

And they rejoice in three things: because they have angels as companions, whom here they had as patrons; because they shall understand God’s secrets, which here they saw obscurely; and because they shall see God face to face, whom here they loved in longing. Of the first: “They shall neither marry nor be given in marriage, but shall be as the angels of God” [Note: [Col. 0233] Matt. 22]. Of the second: “They shall all be taught by God” [Note: [Col. 0233] John 6]. Of the third: “The glory [Col. 0233B] of the Lord shall be revealed” [Note: [Col. 0233] Isa. 62], “and all flesh shall see the salvation of our God” [Note: [Col. 0233] Luke 3]. And Job: “In my flesh I shall see God, my saviour” [Note: [Col. 0233] Job 19], to whom be honour and glory for ever and ever [Note: [Col. 0233] Rom. 16].

Because of this glory it follows: “And all the earth was full of his mercy” [Note: [Col. 0233] Ps. 32]. The world is called earth. Hence: “On earth peace to people of good will” [Note: [Col. 0233] Luke 2]. The human heart is called earth. Hence: “Our land is desolate” [Note: [Col. 0233] Isa.]. The womb of the Blessed Virgin is called earth. Hence: “And your land shall be inhabited” [Note: [Col. 0233] Isa. 62]. The Church is called earth. Hence: “You have blessed your land, O Lord” [Note: [Col. 0233] Ps. 84]. The heavenly homeland is called earth. Hence: “I believe that I shall see the good things of the Lord in the land of the living” [Note: [Col. 0233] Office of the Church].

The first is full of his majesty through the variety of works; the second because we were made in his image and [Col. 0233C] likeness; the third through the Incarnation; the fourth through the working of miracles; the fifth through the fullness of glory. In the first the wisdom of majesty shines forth; in the second, benevolence; in the third, grace; in the fourth, power; in the fifth, the most exalted mighty deeds of God.

The Seraphim standing over that throne are said to cover his feet with two wings, that is, our humanity. These are temporal goods by which we are covered—that is, protected. And they are wisdom by which we moderate ourselves in these things, and they are said to cover his face [Note: [Col. 0233] Isa. 6]. These are love of eternal goods and the sweetness of his love, because the more we investigate his eternity, the more incomprehensible we find it. Hence: “Let a man approach the deep heart, and God shall be exalted” [Note: [Col. 0233] Ps. 63]. It is the same with sweetness: the more he is loved, the more lovable he is found. And with two they flew: namely, with spiritual goods and strength; for by spiritual goods we are lifted up, and by strength we are sustained lest we fall. These matters have been discussed more fully above.

> I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and stags of the fields, that you do not rouse or awaken my beloved until she herself wills it.

[CARD.] Christ, and likewise the Blessed Virgin, seem to many as though asleep when they do not at once gird themselves for vengeance against the undevout, and do not at once rise in mercy toward the devout. Habakkuk awakened Christ so sleeping, saying: “Why do you not look upon those acting wickedly, and keep silent while the impious devours one more righteous than himself?” [Note: [Col. 0233] Hab. 1]. And Malachi: “Therefore now we call the arrogant blessed; indeed, those who do impiety have been built up” [Note: [Col. 0233] Mal. 3]. And: “What profit is there because we have kept the commandment of the Lord and walked as mourners before the Lord?” [Note: [Col. 0233] ibid.].

Therefore Christ says: Do not rouse or awaken my beloved, but wait patiently until she herself wills it. For she herself will will both to ask mercy for the devout and to awaken vengeance against the undevout, as her countless miracles show. Nor does the Son discourage the devout mind from crying to his mother; rather, he forbids it to murmur impatiently against her, to insult her, or to find fault with her.

He adjures the daughters of Jerusalem by the gazelles and stags [Col. 0234B] of the fields—that is, by the virtues figured in these animals, to which faithful souls ought to be conformed. For as the goat has keen sight, so we ought to contemplate keenly that punishment is not inflicted upon the wicked without cause, and that grace is sometimes delayed even for the elect; and as stags, let us devour the serpent of pride. For pride makes a person devoid of long-suffering and patience, because, presuming upon himself, he believes himself worthy of prosperity and unworthy of adversity.

But because the Son had said these things concerning the awakening of his mother, when she herself wishes to be roused and awakened, the Son is roused and awakens. The mother shows that the Son, although he seems to delay, does not delay, but hastens to help and show mercy. Therefore she says to the young women:

> [Col. 0234C] 45 The voice of my beloved.

[THO.] Seeing the modesty and fear of the young women, by which they are troubled, the bride declares this to have happened by God’s dispensation, as though excusing herself. Hence she says: *The voice of my beloved*, perceiving this—the beloved, I say, who after the voice will shortly come; hence follows: “Behold, he comes, leaping upon the mountains.”

For four reasons we joyfully receive the voice of God: because by reason we penetrate the secrets of his will; because by inward grace we are pierced from knowledge into love of him; because by knowledge of the Scriptures we contemplate his will more abundantly; and because through the example of the elect he strengthens our slothfulness toward earnest virtue.

But many things, and especially three, hinder us from inwardly hearing this voice of the beloved, from following when we hear, and from attaining when we follow: the voice of the flesh, the voice of the world, and the voice of the devil. The voice of the flesh works through desires of pleasures; the voice of the world through the appetite for rank, honours, glory, and riches; the voice of the devil through envy of our brothers’ progress. Thus the flesh suggests lustful things, the world pompous things, the devil poisonous things. The flesh makes men lax through sensual things, the world swollen through ambitious things, and the devil sickly through poisonous things.

This is the voice of the beloved: calling to inward joys, inviting to hard things, exhorting to the firm things of humility, and pouring in the oil of charity. But he who is beloved rebukes the one who errs, strengthens the one who fights, and praises the one who triumphs. [Col. 0235A] There is a threatening voice, an admonishing voice, and a summoning voice. The first reproves the erring person; the second strengthens one subject in obedience; the third soothes the devout person. The first is so that he may come to his senses; the second, that he may grow strong; the third, that “in peace he may sleep and rest in the same” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 4].

Of the first: “The voice of the Lord is upon the waters; the God of majesty has thundered” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 28]. Of the second: “The voice of the Lord is in power” [Note: [Col. 0235] ibid.]. Of the third: “The voice of the Lord is in magnificence upon the waters” [Note: [Col. 0235] ibid.]: that the sinner may be converted; that one working in power may be strengthened; that the devout person may be kindled in magnificence. The first is “breaking the cedars” [Note: [Col. 0235] ibid.], that is, the proud, that repentance may be done; the second is “cutting through the flame of fire” [Note: [Col. 0235] ibid.], that lustful temptation may be interrupted, and “shaking the wilderness” [Note: [Col. 0235] ibid.], [Col. 0235B] that the distress of tribulation may be weakened; the third is “preparing the stags” [Note: [Col. 0235] ibid.], so that, leaping over the thorns of anxieties, they may seek flourishing and most fertile pastures.

Of the first: “The Lord thundered from heaven, and the Most High gave his voice” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 17]. “I heard your voice in paradise,” says Adam, “and I was afraid” [Note: [Col. 0235] Gen. 3]. Therefore, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 94]. Of the second: “My sheep hear my voice” [Note: [Col. 0235] John 10].—“The friend of the bridegroom stands and hears, and rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom’s voice” [Note: [Col. 0235] John 3].

There is a threefold voice pertaining to the beloved: the prophetic voice, the angelic voice, and the evangelical voice. The first was the voice of prophets to an unbelieving people; the second, Gabriel’s voice to the Virgin; the third, the beloved’s voice to an untaught people, because of the newness of faith. The first announced long beforehand that he would come; [Col. 0235C] the second that he was already near; the third taught what a righteous person ought to ask from God. Of the first: “The Lord will ascend upon a light cloud and enter Egypt” [Note: [Col. 0235] Isa. 19]. Of the second: “Behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son” [Note: [Col. 0235] Luke 1]. Of the third: “Thus shall you pray: Our Father who are in heaven, hallowed be your name” [Note: [Col. 0235] Matt. 6].

What you ought to ask was taught by that righteous man when he instructed his people thus: “May the Lord open your heart in his law and in his commandments, and make peace, and not forsake you in the evil time” [Note: [Col. 0235] 2 Macc. 1]. Behold, three things which the righteous person ought to ask for: the opening of the heart, the establishment of peace, and consolation in pilgrimage. The first is for receiving the infusion of charity; the second for tranquillity of life; [Col. 0235D] the third for safety on the way: the first, that we may love more ardently; the second, that we may be freer for God; the third, that we may walk more safely.

Of the first: “The charity of God is poured out in our hearts through the Holy Spirit who has been given to us” [Note: [Col. 0235] Rom. 5]. Of the second: “I sleep, and my heart watches” [Note: [Col. 0235] Song 5]; and: “In peace I shall sleep and rest in the same” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 4]. Of the third: “If I should walk in the midst of the shadow of death, I will not fear, because you are with me” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 137]; and: “Deliver me, [Col. 0236A] O Lord, and set me beside you, and let the hand of anyone whatsoever fight against me” [Note: [Col. 0235] Job 17].

Of the first the bride says: “Your name is poured-out oil” [Note: [Col. 0235] Song 1]. Of the second: “Our little bed is flowering” [Note: [Col. 0235] ibid.]. Of the third: “I held him and shall not let him go until I bring him into my house” [Note: [Col. 0235] Song 3].

It should be noted that the heart of sinners first perishes, second is dispersed, third is covered by the devil, and fourth is opened by the Lord. It perishes when the soul dies within and has no remembrance of God; it is dispersed—that is, perishes into diverse parts—when by the body it works out the wickedness conceived within; the devil covers it when he brings it to the hardness of obstinacy; God opens it when he gives the grace to do good.

Of the first: “Their memory has perished with a sound, and they have perished because of their iniquity [Col. 0236B]” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 9]. And the prophet: “The holy one has perished from the earth, and there is no righteous one among men; all lie in wait for blood; each hunts his brother unto death” [Note: [Col. 0235] Mic. 7]. Of the second: “They perished in Endor and became like the dung of the earth” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 82]. For *Endor* is said to mean “fountain of generation.” This is the body, which begets and is begotten; “they became like the dung of the earth,” namely foul-smelling. Of the third: “They are covered with their iniquity and impiety” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ps. 72]. And the prophet: “For behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gloom the peoples” [Note: [Col. 0235] Isa. 60]. Of the fourth: “May the Lord open your heart in his law and in his commandments” [Note: [Col. 0235] 2 Macc. 1].

The first are the girl dead in her mother’s chamber [Note: [Col. 0235] Matt. 9], that is, the soul inwardly. This is the jar in which impiety sits, which two [Col. 0236C] women carry into the land of Shinar [Note: [Col. 0235] Dan. 1]. The second are the young man dead already outside the gate of the city [Note: [Col. 0235] Luke 7]. Hence Ezekiel: “A great eagle with great wings, with long sweep of limbs, having feathers and much variegation, came to Lebanon, took the marrow of the cedar, and carried it into the land of Shinar” [Note: [Col. 0235] Ezek. 17]. The third are Lazarus, four days dead in the tomb [Note: [Col. 0235] John 11]. To these it is said through the prophet: “What is it, Israel, that you are in the land of enemies?” [Note: [Col. 0235] Bar. 3]. The fourth are those for whom the Lord opens the tomb and raises them with Lazarus.

Note that both we ourselves open, and the Lord opens, in three ways: first, to the teacher; second, to God; third, to one’s neighbour: first by confession, second by devotion, third by edification. [Col. 0236D] The first bestows purity upon you; the second, delight in the Lord; the third, healing upon your neighbour. Of the first the Lord says: “Ephphatha,” that is, “Be opened” [Note: [Col. 0235] Mark 7]. Of the second: “Open to me, my sister, my bride” [Note: [Col. 0235] Song 5]. Likewise: “Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone opens to me, I shall enter in to him, and dine with him, and he with me” [Note: [Col. 0235] Rev. 3]. Of the third: “Open, Lebanon, your forests” [Note: [Col. 0235] Zech. 11]. Lebanon is said to mean “whiteness.” Those open its forests who show their neighbour the flowers of virtues. [Col. 0237A] “That strong woman opened her hand to the needy” [Note: [Col. 0237] Prov. 31].

Likewise, there are three openings by the Lord. For he opens our heart, opens his secret, and opens the kingdom. The first is for understanding the commandments and for the infusion of charity; the second, for wonder; the third, for glorious reception. Of the first: “May the Lord open your heart in his law” [Note: [Col. 0237] II Macc. 1]. Likewise: “Drop down dew, O heavens, from above, and let the clouds rain the Just One; let the earth be opened and bring forth the Saviour” [Note: [Col. 0237] Isa. 45], so that knowledge of charity may grow in us. Of the second: “Behold, I John saw a door opened in heaven” [Note: [Col. 0237] Rev. 4]. Likewise: “Heaven was opened and the ark of God was seen in it” [Note: [Col. 0237] Rev. 11]. And: “Stephen saw heaven opened” [Note: [Col. 0237] Acts 7]. And concerning Christ: “The heavens were opened over him” [Note: [Col. 0237] Matt. 3]. Of the third: “The foolish virgins: ‘Lord, [Col. 0237B] Lord, open to us’” [Note: [Col. 0237] Matt. 25]. And concerning blessed Mary: “Through you the gates of Paradise have been opened to us.” And: “The Lord was lifted up into heaven, and a cloud received him” [Note: [Col. 0237] Acts 5]; he will open Paradise, etc., etc. Behold the opening for the infusion of grace. Peace for leisure with God follows.

Note that through peace some become dissolute, some lax, some devout. The first are slaves, the second hirelings, the third sons. For a slave always acts badly unless he is whipped. A hireling does good better if he is stirred up. A son acts all the better the more he is left to his freedom. Of the first: “The land was silent for many years, and the children of Israel added to doing evil.” But through the scourge, “Their heart was humbled in labours, and they were weakened, and there was none to [Col. 0237C] help. And they cried to the Lord when they were afflicted, and he delivered them from their necessities” [Note: [Col. 0237] Ps. 106], so that they might say: “Your rod and your staff, they have comforted me” [Note: [Col. 0237] Ps. 22]. And the poet:

> You see how every comfort corrupts the idle body,  
> And waters acquire a defect unless they are moved.

And the prophet: “I shall go and return to my former husband, because it was better for me then than now” [Note: [Col. 0237] Hos. 2]. Of the second: “For a moment I deserted you; for a little while I abandoned you” [Note: [Col. 0237] Isa. 54]. And the poet [Note: [Col. 0237] Ovid, *Art of Love*, II, 732]:

> It does no harm to put the spur to a horse once admitted.

Therefore Job was scourged [Note: [Col. 0237] Job 9], and Tobias blinded [Note: [Col. 0237] Tob. 2]. Of the third, the bride in the Song: “On my bed I sought by night him whom my soul loves; I sought him and did not [Col. 0237D] find him” [Note: [Col. 0237] Song 3]. “A little while after I had passed on” [Note: [Col. 0237] ibid.], namely, the night of tribulation, “I found him whom my soul loves” [Note: [Col. 0237] ibid.], namely, in devout peace. And thus: “In peace, in the selfsame, I shall sleep and rest” [Note: [Col. 0237] Ps. 4]. And the Apostle: “And may the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, keep your hearts and your minds,” etc. [lacuna] [Note: [Col. 0237] Phil. 4]. Behold: from peace to leisure with God.

There follows: “Nor may he forsake you in the evil time, for security” [Note: [Col. 0237] II Macc. 5]. “Evil time” is understood in three ways. For this wretched [Col. 0238A] exile is called an evil time; an imminent danger is called an evil time; the final judgment is called an evil time. Of the first, Job says: “Man born of woman, living for a short time, is filled with many miseries” [Note: [Col. 0237] Job 14]; of the second, the Apostle: “In the last days perilous times shall be at hand” [Note: [Col. 0237] II Tim. 3]; of the third: “That day, a day of wrath, calamity, and misery” [Note: [Col. 0237] Zeph. 1]. Therefore the Lord must not “forsake us” in the first “evil time,” so that in enduring this exile we may have patience; nor in the second, lest through the danger of temptation we fall into sin; nor in the third, lest we fall into Gehenna. On account of the first he says: “In this way in which you shall walk, I shall fix my eyes upon you” [Note: [Col. 0237] Ps. 31]. On account of the second he says: “When you walk through fire, you shall not be burned, and the flame of temptation, namely, shall not burn [Col. 0238B] in you, because I am the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Saviour” [Note: [Col. 0237] Isa. 43]. On account of the third: “You shall call upon me and I shall hear you, and I shall restore your captivity from all places” [Note: [Col. 0237] Jer. 29]. Likewise: “Show your face, and we shall be saved” [Note: [Col. 0237] Ps. 79]. Likewise: “From whatever tribulation they cry to me, I shall hear them” [Note: [Col. 0237] Exod. 22], “and I shall be their Lord for ever” [Note: [Col. 0237] Jer. 11]. For this is the voice of the beloved, concerning which the bride says to us: “The voice of my beloved.”

The voice of my beloved, for me.

[CARD.] Such is he, as you have heard; and I tell you concerning him that he hastens to help and powerfully tramples demons underfoot. For:

> Behold, he comes, leaping upon the mountains and bounding over the hills.

[Col. 0238C] [THO.] It was not by chance that hearing is placed before sight. For this is the order in Job: “By the hearing of the ear I heard you, but now my eye sees you” [Note: [Col. 0237] Job 42]. “And suddenly there came from heaven a sound of a mighty rushing spirit” [Note: [Col. 0237] Acts 2]. After this: “There appeared to them divided tongues as of fire” [Note: [Col. 0237] ibid.]. And David: “Hear, daughter, and see” [Note: [Col. 0237] Ps. 44]. The mountains are the higher angels, the hills the lower. Hence the prophet: “Mountains and hills shall sing praise before God” [Note: [Col. 0237] Isa. 55]. The human race is the plain. Therefore he leapt upon the mountains, that is, upon those heavenly spirits, revealing to them the mystery hidden from the ages. But from them he descended as far as the lower angels, that is, the hills, and passed beyond them also. “For he did not take hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham” [Col. 0238D] [Note: [Col. 0237] Heb. 2]; and thus, descending to human beings, “he was made a little lower than the angels” [Note: [Col. 0237] ibid.]. Yet he also made himself lower than men, namely, being subject to his parents [Note: [Col. 0237] Luke 2], and became the angel of great counsel. He leapt upon the mountains after the likeness of the angels, ministering to us. He is a good father who supplied his flesh as food, his blood as drink, and his soul as a price. He passed Gabriel by, preceding him to the Virgin Mary [Note: [Col. 0237] Luke 1].

He also leapt upon the mountains, that is, the angels, appearing in them to the [Col. 0239A] ancient fathers; and he bounded over the hills, that is, the patriarchs, and descended even to sinners. This beloved is said to have sat, or walked, or stood, or, as here, made devout leaps. He sits in those in whom, vices having been eliminated, he sweetly rests through the desirable tranquillity of the mind. Hence: “We shall come to him and make our dwelling with him” [Note: [Col. 0239] John 14]. He stands in those whom he makes strong in battle; he walks in those whom he causes to advance toward what is better; he leaps in those whom he raises in contemplation.

We have three comings of the Saviour at hand. The first is in the flesh, the second in the heart, the third in majesty. In the first he came to redeem. Hence: “The Lord redeems Jacob” [Note: [Col. 0239] Jer. 31]. In the second, to heal: “For he sent his word and healed them” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 106]. [Col. 0239B] In the third, to save: “For we await the Saviour, our Lord Jesus Christ” [Note: [Col. 0239] Church Office, On Advent]. On account of the joy of this coming, the Church sings: “As it were the voice of the beloved, which has been heard in our land. People of Zion, behold, the Lord shall come to save the nations, and he shall make the voice of his praise heard” [Note: [Col. 0239] Church Office]. In the first he made heard the mercy of his voice; in the second, the grace of his voice; in the third, the glory of his voice. We receive the first in the purity of our body; the second in the righteousness of our body; the third in the joy of our body. The first was enfolded in flesh, the second hidden in the heart, the third shall be manifest in majesty. The first was humble, the second lovable, the third terrible. In the first he came to us; in the second, into us; in the third, [Col. 0239C] for us. To us with purple and sackcloth; into us with parchment and pen; for us with fire and sword. With the purple of divinity and the sackcloth of humanity; with the parchment of good will and the pen of divine inspiration; with the sword of separation: “Go, you accursed, into eternal fire” [Note: [Col. 0239] Matt. 25]; and: “The fire of vengeance—the fire shall devour your enemies” [Note: [Col. 0239] Isa. 26]. In this purple Mordecai went out from the king’s presence [Note: [Col. 0239] Esth. 8]. Of the sackcloth: “You tore my sackcloth and girded me” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 29], etc. With parchment and pen, because there was a man who had a writer’s inkhorn at his loins [Note: [Col. 0239] Ezek. 9], so that our heart may be tablets of the covenant written by God’s finger [Note: [Col. 0239] Exod. 31]. Of the sword: “Unless you are converted, he has brandished his sword” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 7]. Of the fire: [Col. 0239D] “Go, you accursed, into eternal fire” [Note: [Col. 0239] Matt. 25].

In the first he “performed my judgment and my cause” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 9]; in the second he instructs us in the discipline of religion [Note: [Col. 0239] Prov. 3]; in the third he shall perform judgment and righteousness [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 118]. In a figure of this threefold coming, the responsory *I Looked from Afar* [Note: [Col. 0239] Church Office] ends in a threefold verse: the first belongs to the first coming, the second to the second, and the third to the third. In the first he came to redeem: “For the Lord sent redemption to his people” [Note: [Col. 0239] ibid.]. Truly, with the Lord there is [Col. 0240A] mercy, and with him abundant redemption [Note: [Col. 0239] ibid.]. He redeemed us from death, from the power of the devil, and from the old manner of life. Of the first: “Who redeems your life from destruction, from the old manner of life” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 102]; of the second: “He saved them from the hand of those who hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 105]; of the third: “You were not redeemed with corruptible gold or silver from your vain manner of life handed down by your fathers, but with the blood, as of an uncontaminated and spotless Lamb, Christ” [Note: [Col. 0239] I Pet. 1].

He came humble, because “he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, made in the likeness of men, and found in appearance as a man” [Note: [Col. 0239] Eph. 2]. O wondrous exchange! The Creator of the human race, taking an animate body, deigned to be born of a virgin; and, coming forth as a man without seed, bestowed upon us [Col. 0240B] his divinity [Note: [Col. 0239] Church Office]. Though heavenly, he became earthly; though Son of God, he became son of man; though rich, for our sake he became poor [Note: [Col. 0239] II Cor. 8], namely in the flesh, in which this man appeared most gentle among his people. Therefore, “both earthborn men and sons of men, together, rich and poor” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 48]. Go out to meet him. He came with the purple of divinity. In what did he “perform my judgment”? In the sackcloth of humanity, in what did he perform my cause? “You tore,” he says, “my sackcloth and girded me with joy” [Note: [Col. 0239] Ps. 29].

There is a threefold judgment: the first between God and the devil; the second between the devil and man; the third between God and man. The first took place in the beginning, namely when the angel fell “from heaven” [Note: [Col. 0239] Isa. 14], because “the prince of this world has already [Col. 0240C] been judged” [Note: [Col. 0239] John 16]. Christ came to effect the second, and he shall effect the third. The devil deceived man by fraud, oppressed him violently, and held him unjustly. First he led him into sin; second, he brought on the punishment of hell; third, he excluded the way to the kingdom. The first was through envy, the second through power, the third through malice.
