- Albinus, bishop of Albano, from 2 May 1191 to 12 July 1196.
- Octavianus, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, from 2 May 1191 to 10 September 1197.
- Peter, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina, from 2 May 1191 to 10 September 1197.
- John, bishop of Palestrina, from 2 May 1191 to 9 February 1196.
- John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement and bishop of Tusculum, from 3 June 1191 to 27 July 1197.
- Romanus, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Anastasia, from 3 June 1191 to 14 July 1194.
- Pandulfus, cardinal-priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles, from 2 May 1191 to 13 February 1196.
- Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Cecilia, from 2 May 1191 to 28 May 1197.
- Melior, cardinal-priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius, from 27 December 1191 to 26 January 1197.
- Cinthius, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina, from 8 June 1191 to 28 May 1197.

# LETTERS AND PRIVILEGES OF CELESTINE III, ROMAN PONTIFF, ARRANGED IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER

For the books consulted, see the bibliographical index prefixed to volume CLXXIX.

## [GENUINE.]

## YEAR 1191

[Col. 0867A]

### I. He affirms for the Church of Porto the concession made by the abbot of Saint John at Ravenna.

*(Lateran, 19 April.)*

[Fantuzzi, *Monuments of the Church of Ravenna*, VI, 56.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the prior and convent of the Church of Porto: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more fervently, with the Lord’s favour, you labour in regular observance, the more sincerely we love your community; and, where we can do so with God, we ought and wish to provide more diligently for your advancement and welfare. Therefore, in response to your just petitions, [Col. 0867B] we confirm by apostolic authority the grant which our beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Saint John the Evangelist of Ravenna, prudently and equitably made to you concerning possessions acquired and to be acquired which belong by right to them, as is contained in their authentic document; and we fortify it with the protection of this present writing. We decree that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let that person know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of May [19 April], in the first year of our pontificate.

### II. He receives the Church of Saint John at Rastorf under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges.

*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 2 May.)*

[Schannat, *Diocese of Fulda*, p. 266.]

[Col. 0867C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons CONRAD, provost of the church of Saint John, and the brethren at Ratesdorf, both present and future, who shall be canonically appointed in perpetuity.

To grant effect to just petitioners is required both by the force of equity and by the order of reason, especially when the petitioners’ will and piety support it and [Col. 0868A] truth does not leave it unsupported. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions. Following the example of Pope Clement, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own, and fortify by the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid church of Saint John the Baptist and Saint Cecilia at Radesdorf, in which you are dedicated to divine service. We decree that whatever goods and possessions the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future obtain, with the Lord’s aid, through grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify these in their own names:

[Col. 0868B] The place itself on which the aforesaid church stands, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Lawrence at Ussine, with the village itself and all its appurtenances; Daftaha, Ingumarestat, and Sulaha, with their dependencies; Geintistat, Issileibes, and Negilstete, with their appurtenances; Melre and Clettistete, with all their appurtenances; Keistreiche and Nenderich, with their appurtenances; Datinbeche, Scherlinges, Gozoldesdorp, and Hasalahe, with the other villages and appurtenances of all the aforesaid villages.

Further, we uphold the liberties and immunities of your manorial and cloistral courts, as also the ancient and reasonable customs granted to your church and observed hitherto; and we decree that they remain unimpaired in future times. Moreover, by apostolic authority we prohibit your advocate, whoever he may be at the time, from presuming to burden the place itself or its appurtenances, or to harass them with any undue exactions, whether in the forests and woods or in the newly cleared lands of your church; rather, he is to be content with what has been granted him from ancient times and belongs to his jurisdiction.

[Col. 0868C] We also decree, as is known to have been established by an authentic document of Otto, emperor of illustrious memory, that it shall not be lawful for anyone, even the abbot of the monastery of Fulda, [Col. 0869A] rashly to take away or diminish any of its possessions, or to grant any of them as a benefice. Nor shall it be lawful for that abbot to impose upon you or the goods of your church the compulsory service of exaction or claim, saving the ancient canonical due specifically owed to that abbot, his brethren, or his canons.

We therefore decree that no one at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved intact, wholly serving the use and benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. If in the future any ecclesiastical person knowingly and rashly attempts to contravene this page of our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, [Col. 0869B] unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find with the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavianus, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. [Col. 0869C] I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Pandulfus, cardinal-priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Peter, cardinal-priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Jordanus, cardinal-priest of Saint Pudentiana, title of Pastor. I, Gratianus, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerardus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Gofredus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. [Col. 0869D] I, Gregory, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church, acting chancellor, on the sixth day before the Nones of May [2 May], indiction IX, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

### III. He announces to archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and the other prelates of churches that Peter, formerly archbishop of Tarentaise, has been enrolled among the saints.

*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 10 May.)*

[*Acta Sanctorum*, May, vol. II, p. 347.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0870A] brothers, archbishops and bishops, and beloved sons, abbots, priors, and the other prelates of churches: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The invisible Creator of all manifests, teaches, and confirms by certain visible signs, as it were by flashes of lightning or thunder, through diverse but not contrary—rather harmonious—testimonies of Holy Scripture, the glory of divine praise concerning the most sacred memory of the saints, marvellous to all mortals and to be extolled by continual praises both individually and collectively, but especially on memorial days or festal solemnities. Thus it is proclaimed concerning him who is praiseworthy without end and wonderful in all his works, in David’s voice [Col. 0870B]: “Praise the Lord in his saints” (Ps. 50:1). And elsewhere: “God is wonderful in his saints” (Ps. 87:36). And concerning the saints themselves, the prophetic saying asks with a certain wonder: “Who are these that fly like clouds?” etc. (Isa. 60:8).

Since he is himself supremely good and infinite, willing to have innumerable persons through whom he may be praised, he gathers and joins saints to saints, as he ordained from eternity according to the riches of his power. This is understood to overflow into the abundance of his praise when he says: “Praise him according to the multitude of his greatness” (Ps. 150:2). That he displays himself as praiseworthy in a special manner in the saints, and is found wonderful in them by granting miracles in their fruitful teaching and saving activity and by increasing their number, is known beyond doubt to concern our salvation, if we are willing to attend carefully. And we ought to acknowledge with so much greater devotion what almighty God works in his servants for the increase of our salvation—as our Fathers are known commendably and devoutly to have done in similar cases—as greater fruit is unquestionably believed to be forthcoming.

[Col. 0870C] Indeed, from a certain rescript of Pope Lucius, our predecessor of happy memory, we have learned that two abbots of the Cistercian Order, prudent and discerning men, had humbly and urgently requested on behalf of that Order that he should canonize Peter of blessed memory, formerly archbishop of Tarentaise [Col. 0870D]. He would have granted favourable assent to the petition presented to him, had a certain untimeliness of circumstances and affairs not then denied the possibility of performing the requested act. He in no way doubted Peter’s merits; but at that time nothing concerning his miracles and manner of life had been committed to writing. It was fitting to defer the request until the brethren had taken counsel together. He directed that, in the meantime, those things concerning the deeds and life of the aforesaid Father which were certain should be put in writing, so that, when a suitable time had come, the Church of God might have a firm and unquestionable basis on which it could more safely and confidently rely in granting what had been requested.

Therefore, since, in accordance with the aforesaid command of our said predecessor, the deeds performed during his life by that blessed man, [Col. 0871A] radiant in virtues, and the miracles which God worked through him after his death, have been faithfully collected and put into writing—a record which we declare proven on the testimony of many persons—and since we have been duly informed of these matters by great and honourable persons, we grant assent to the aforesaid petition, again addressed to the Roman Church and now to us, though unworthy, seated in the Apostolic See. Not so much out of reverence for the aforesaid Order, to whose pious and just petitions we are willingly disposed to accede, as for the extension of the Lord’s glory, we have canonized the aforesaid memorable man by the common counsel of our brethren. [Col. 0871B] We announce by writings of the Apostolic See to the whole Church of God that he has been canonized. We decree that in all your churches and monasteries the venerable memory of that glorious man, Saint Peter, formerly archbishop of Tarentaise, shall be solemnly celebrated every year on the third Ides of September [11 September], on which his glorious body was raised from the tomb with devout reverence.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the sixth Ides of May [10 May], in the first year of our pontificate, and in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

### IV. He informs the abbot and convent of Belle-Vallée that Peter, formerly archbishop of Tarentaise, has been numbered among the saints.

*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 10 May.)*

[*Acta Sanctorum*, May, vol. II, p. 348.]

[Col. 0871C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Belle-Vallée: greeting and apostolic blessing.

“The invisible Creator of all manifests, teaches, and confirms by certain visible signs … the glory of divine praise concerning the most sacred memory of the saints, marvellous to all mortals,” etc., as above, as far as: “We decree that in your monastery and in all monasteries of your Order the venerable memory of that glorious man, Saint Peter, formerly archbishop of Tarentaise, shall be solemnly celebrated every year on the third Ides of September [11 September], on which his glorious body was raised from the tomb with devout reverence.” [Col. 0871D]

Moreover, since divine mercy has granted you so great a grace that the aforesaid precious body now rests in your monastery, we earnestly admonish and more fervently exhort your whole community to devote yourselves with such unanimity to the solemn celebration of the memory of that precious saint that almighty God may be honoured in your actions and the abundance of eternal reward may be increased for you through imitation of him. Thus, with the Lord as author, it may be clearly recognized how the sap and teaching of that holy root abide and are preserved in the fruit of the branches.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the sixth Ides of May [10 May], in the first year of our pontificate.

### V. He promises Geoffrey, elect of York, that Hugh, bishop of Durham, will be subject to him after he has received consecration.

*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 11 May.)*

[*Monasticon Anglicanum*, III, 148.]

[Col. 0872A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son GEOFFREY, elect of York: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although someone may say that the Roman Church ought to show deference to prelates of churches for various considerations, yet when the mother Church herself wishes, as seems fitting, to turn her attention to conferring the rights that are due, this must in no way be taken amiss but rather endured with equanimity. Accordingly, we have thought fit to inform [Col. 0872B] your diligence by this present writing that, although the Apostolic See has provided for and judged worthy of honouring the person of our venerable brother Hugh, bishop of Durham, as an honourable member, it was nevertheless necessary and proper for us to provide for the right and status of the Church of York. For it seemed exceedingly unfitting that this Church should remain any longer deprived of the support of so great and sole a suffragan in the kingdom of England; nor is anything taken from its right if another’s right is preserved.

We have therefore commanded him, and command you, that, notwithstanding any exemption obtained from the Roman Church on his behalf, he shall attend upon you as his metropolitan both before your consecration and after you have been consecrated. Since, by the common counsel of our brethren, we have decreed that he and his church shall be subject to you and your Church, with metropolitan right wholly preserved, he must not delay in rendering you due obedience and reverence, all obstacle of contradiction or appeal being removed.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the fifth Ides of May [11 May], in the first year of our pontificate.

### VI. He receives the monastery of Saint Mary and Saint John the Evangelist at Lübeck under protection and confirms its goods.

*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 21 May.)*

[Shum, *History of Denmark*, VIII, p. 696.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, [Col. 0872D] to his beloved sons ARNOLD, abbot, and the convent of Saint Mary and Saint John the Evangelist at Lübeck: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When what is just and honourable is requested of us, both the force of equity and the order of reason require that it be brought to its proper effect through the diligence of our office. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, giving favourable assent to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and fortify it by the protection of this present writing. We decree that the canonical order, known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict, shall be inviolably observed there for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in the future obtain by lawful means with the Lord’s provision, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify these in their own names:

[Col. 0873A] Half the village of Rantzivelt; the village of Cleve; half the tithe in Greater Gladeburge and half in Lesser Gladeburge; half the tithe of Stuthestorp; the whole tithe of Eteodenwinde; plots in the city of Lübeck; fields in the territory of that city; one [plot] on the stream Strieneze; saltworks at Todeslo; the village of Tribernerthorph; and, in Oldenbruch, three holdings at Tescaio.

We also decree that the burial-place of that locality shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and last will of [Col. 0873B] those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; without prejudice, however, to the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of deception or by force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or by the counsel of the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict.

No person whatsoever, therefore, may infringe this page of our confirmation, protection, and constitution, or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let that person know that he will incur the indignation [Col. 0873C] of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June [21 May], in the first year of our pontificate.

### VII. He receives the monastery of Saint Mary and Saint John the Evangelist at Cismar under protection and confirms its privileges.

*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 23 May.)*

[Ibid.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ARNOLD, abbot, and the convent of Saint Mary and Saint John the Evangelist at Cismar: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0873D] Whenever something is requested of us which is recognized as befitting religion and honour, it is proper for us readily to grant it and, in accordance with the reasonable will of the petitioners, to bring it to completion in effect, reason supporting the act. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, giving favourable assent to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and fortify it by the protection of this present writing.

You may receive to conversion clerics or laypersons who are free and absolved, fleeing from the secular world, and retain them without any contradiction. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in the same place, from leaving it, except in order to embrace a stricter religious life. No one shall dare retain one who has left [Col. 0874A] without letters of the community guaranteeing his departure. When a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and those under interdict, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice.

No person whatsoever, therefore, may infringe this page of our protection and constitution or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let that person know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the tenth day before the Kalends of June [23 May], in the first year of our pontificate.

### VIII. He orders R[eginald], bishop of Bath, and the abbots of Reading and Waltham to restore whatever Baldwin, archbishop, took from the monks of Canterbury.

*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, 28 May.)*

[Twysden, *Historiae Anglicanae Scriptores*, II, 1572.]

[Col. 0874B]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother R., bishop of Bath, and to his beloved sons, the abbots of Reading and Waltham: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The troubles and injuries which the community of that place suffered at the hands of B., archbishop of Canterbury, of good memory, we do not believe are unknown to your discretion. Since, therefore, the aforesaid archbishop, although he had received the command of our predecessors Urban and Clement, of blessed memory, to restore in full the condition of those brothers, had not yet fully carried out that restoration when he set out upon his pilgrimage, we command and enjoin you by apostolic letters that, setting aside every delay, objection, and appeal, you shall, relying upon our authority, cause the churches, together with the revenues received from them, and the other things which the frequently mentioned archbishop took from them without due legal process, to be restored in their entirety; and, if necessary, do not delay to restrain their possessors by ecclesiastical censure. In every way take care that divine offices shall henceforth not be celebrated in the place condemned by apostolic authority; rather, that the chapel said to have been erected there be utterly destroyed. Further, revoking the establishment of canons, as is known to have been decreed by our Fathers, declare null and keep suspended those who, after the apostolic prohibition, knowingly presumed to celebrate divine offices in that place, until they come to the Apostolic See to be absolved. Also cause those known to have incurred the sentence of Pope Clement, of pious memory, to be more carefully avoided by all, until, having rendered fitting satisfaction to the Church, they deserve to be absolved by us. Those who knowingly communicated with persons of this kind shall make suitable satisfaction at your discretion.

We have judged all these matters to be enjoined upon your discretion all the more strictly because the repeated fruitless issuance of commands appears to redound to the injury of the Apostolic See; and it would ill become your religious profession if you were to execute an apostolic command too sluggishly. Nor could we, without displeasure, tolerate in any degree so great a neglect on your part, notwithstanding any letters which may appear to have been obtained from the Apostolic See and which prejudice their right. If all of you cannot be present for carrying these matters out, let two of you nevertheless execute them.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the fifth day before the Kalends of June, in the first year of our pontificate.

## IX. He restores to the prior and convent of Christ Church, Canterbury, privileges taken away by Baldwin, formerly archbishop.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 28 May.)*

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 0875B]

**Coelestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the prior and convent of Christ Church, Canterbury: greeting and apostolic blessing.**

As it is recognized to belong to the duty of our apostolic office to confer enduring force upon things rightly and properly ordered, so, indeed, we are bound to deprive of force, enfeeble, and invalidate things done otherwise than is fitting. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, since B., formerly archbishop, whether on his own initiative or at another’s instigation, at times afflicted you and your church with many troubles and injuries, and, as is said, procured from the Apostolic See certain documents through false representation to the prejudice of your right—although he ought rather to have laboured for your peace—we, wishing with paternal care to provide henceforth for your tranquillity, by apostolic authority revoke and render void everything done in regard to you through the said archbishop by force or fear. In particular, we annul those acts said to have been done, in the presence and despite the objection of the legate of the Roman Church, against a command of the Apostolic See, as is contained in the authenticated instrument of that legate, namely John of Anagni, formerly cardinal priest, sent into England on your behalf; and we decree that whatever the same archbishop obtained contrary to your right or to the tenor of your privileges shall lack all force. We establish that no person shall ever dare to draw into precedent what he did wrongly, nor may things which he procured from the Apostolic See while concealing the truth ever generate any prejudice to your right or privileges.

Therefore let no one at all presume to infringe this page of our constitution or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the fifth day before the Kalends of June.

## X. He takes the Church of Saint Lawrence at Florence under protection and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 3 June.)*

*[LAMI, Ecclesiastical Monuments of Florence, II, 935.]*

[Col. 0876A]

**Coelestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Hildebrand, prior of Saint Lawrence in the city of Florence, and his brethren, both present and those canonically appointed in future, for ever.**

A pious request should be fulfilled by the effect that follows it, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested benefit may unquestionably acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your requests, and, following the example of Nicholas, Alexander II, Alexander III, Lucius, Clement III, and Paschal II, Roman pontiffs of blessed memory, our predecessors, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church of Saint Lawrence—which appears to have been the head of the Florentine Church—and in which you are dedicated to divine service; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this document. We establish that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter obtain, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 0876C] The parish belonging to your church, as you have held it hitherto; the hospital situated beside the aforesaid church of Blessed Lawrence, with all its appurtenances; the hospital called Cigreti, built in the parish district of Saint Stephen in Pane, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Mark with all its appurtenances; the hill of Saint Lawrence, bounded on one side by the land of Saint John and two running roads, on another by Saint Romulus, on a third by Saint Mary, and on a fourth by the Royal Road, with its tithes and first-fruits; the hill of Conii, bounded on one side by the stream Tersunula, adjoining on another the land of Saint Romulus and on a third that of Saint John, while on a fourth side runs the road called *Subtus*, with its tithes and first-fruits; the *citinas* [uncertain local term] of Saint Lawrence situated nearby, with their tithes and first-fruits; the *abataticum* of the gate of Saint Lawrence, together with that congregation itself; the church of Saint Bartholomew situated at Faltignano, with all its appurtenances and all the possessions which you hold in that estate; and the church of Saint Andrew at Percussina.

We likewise confirm whatever has been granted to you by the aforesaid Roman pontiffs and confirmed to your church by privileges. On solemn days, let no one’s opposition prevent you from making processions in the cloister or church court and from singing Masses at terce; but in every way strive to glorify almighty God and, He granting it, diligently devote yourselves to the salvation of your souls. We further forbid anyone, within the bounds of your parish, to build a new church or oratory without the authority of the diocesan bishop and your consent, saving the privileges of the Roman pontiffs. Moreover, we hold ratified the ancient liberties, immunities, and reasonable customs granted to your church and hitherto observed, and we decree that they shall remain unimpaired for all time. We further establish that your bishop may not pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against you or your church without manifest and reasonable cause.

[Col. 0877A] We further decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken shall be preserved. When you, the present prior of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one may be put in charge there by any cunning of deceit or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall in the fear of God judge to be elected.

We decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the bishop of Florence. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, then, after a second and third warning, unless he corrects his offence by worthy satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

[Col. 0877D] I, Coelestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Peter in Chains, of the title of Eudoxia. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, title of Pastor. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Viterbo. [Col. 0878A] I, Romanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquino. I, Lothair, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere, on the third day before the Nones of June, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1191, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Coelestine III.

## XI. He takes the monastery of Nonantola under protection and confirms its privileges and possessions.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 8 June.)*

*[See TIRABOSCHI, History of Nonantola, II, 288.]*

## XII. He orders Opizo, subdeacon of Parma, and Master John of Bergamo to settle the dispute between the canons of the cathedral church of Reggio and the clerics of Saint Prosper.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 16 June.)*

*[TIRABOSCHI, Memoirs of Modena, III, 119.]*

[Col. 0878C]

**Coelestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Opizo, our subdeacon and canon of Parma, and Master John of Bergamo: greeting and apostolic blessing.**

A complaint has been laid before us on behalf of our beloved sons the provost P., the master of the schools, and the other canons of the church of Reggio: namely, that the provost of Saint Prosper, coming with his clerics to their church, sought on Holy Saturday to celebrate a third part of the office and to hold the pastoral staff while carrying out the office—although they resisted—a right which the aforesaid Master P. maintains belongs to his dignity; and that he inflicted great injuries upon them. For certain clerics of Saint Prosper took the book of epistles from the hand of a priest of the aforesaid provost of Reggio and treated the latter very dishonourably after laying violent hands upon him. Moreover, they rashly tore the alb worn by a deacon who was prepared to announce the Gospel, and presumed to commit other excesses, which can be explained to you more fully.

But he who spoke on behalf of the provost and clerics of Saint Prosper asserted that the aforesaid provost and canons had caused an instrument to be drawn up concerning their rights, and had presumed, in grave injury to them and to the great prejudice of their right, to act concerning the injury involving the candles, the production of common instruments, the appeal entered to us concerning the production of certain witnesses, the pastoral staff to be held by that provost of Saint Prosper on Holy Saturday, and the offices which they were accustomed to perform for a third part. Since, therefore, from such divergent assertions we could not ascertain the full sequence of the matter, with the consent of the envoys of both parties we have thought fit to commit this business to you. By apostolic letters we command your discretion that, summoning the parties before you, you hear what is alleged on either side and impose a due conclusion upon the matter, notwithstanding any objection or appeal. If it is established that any persons have rashly laid violent hands on clerics, declare them to be strictly avoided by all as excommunicated until they make fitting satisfaction to those injured and come with your letters to the Apostolic See to be absolved.

Compel by ecclesiastical censure, without appeal, witnesses whom either party names in support of its assertion, if through fear or favour they withdraw themselves, so that they may bear testimony to the truth.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the fourth day before the Ides of June, in the first year of our pontificate.

## XIII. He takes the Church of Saint Sigismund under protection and confirms its goods and possessions.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 13 June.)*

*[TIRABOSCHI, Memoirs of Modena, IV, p. 3.]*

**Coelestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Albert, priest of the church of Saint Sigismund of Sablon, and to his successors canonically appointed for ever.**

[Col. 0879C] A pious request should be fulfilled by the effect that follows it, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested benefit may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and, following the example of Alexander and Lucius, Roman pontiffs of blessed memory, our predecessors, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church of Saint Sigismund of Sablon, over which, by God’s authority, you are known to preside; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this document. We establish that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter obtain through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God granting, shall remain wholly secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The site on which the aforesaid church stands, with its appurtenances and boundaries, which are marked by these limits: from the road to the vineyard of the lords of Saviola, and from the vineyard of the sons of Madelgisilus to the bottom of the ditch of the Castle. At Guavaseto, one *mansus* above Carrubium, four *bubulcae* of land; on the bank of the Ramo, two *bubulcae*; below Gavageto, three *bubulcae* of meadow; at Fontanili, four *bubulcae* of land; on the road of Porothese, one plot of land; at Carzeto, two *bubulcae* of meadow; at Sabone, in the Braida of Noceto, twenty-two *bubulcae*; at Pirumplatum, four, and nearby one; south of the Ramo, in two plots, three *bubulcae*; at the Runcus of John the priest, seven *bubulcae* and a mill in the same place; at Cloza, one *bubulca*, and nearby at Linarium, beside the road of Ursimadius, two plots; beside the road of Bonizoli, two plots; beside the oak-grove of Malaquistus, one plot; at the Linarium of the priest Angelus, eight *bubulcae*, and in the same place the mill-ford, with two nearby plots; on the bank of Beccadosso, one plot; above the road of Feligaria, one plot; in the demesne enclosure, six *bubulcae*, with one small nearby plot; one half of the mill of Panaro and two shares of spelt; on the banks of the Tresnaria, one plot; in the Braida of the *vicedomini*, one *bubulca*, with one nearby plot; beside Canterelli, a vineyard; at Lammis, one *bubulca* of meadow; on the road of Dosis, one *bubulca*; at Felegaria, the field called Saint Dalmatius; and the *mansus* of Jannulinus, given by Araldus and his wife, consisting of seventeen *bubulcae*.

[Col. 0880B] Further, the tithe of all the demesnes of the eight nobles, namely Guido and Atto, at Sablano and Runcadellis, which is collected from the *cervus* [uncertain term] at the ditch of the Martani, as the road goes to the well of Gurda opposite Tresnaria; and the tithe of the entire demesne of William of Bomissima and the sons of Corradinus; and a part of the tithe of Michael of Bona at Gavaseto; also the tithes which your church has peaceably possessed for forty years and presently possesses. We likewise confirm by apostolic authority the liberties and immunities reasonably granted to that church and hitherto observed. Since tithes are known to have been granted to the ministers of churches by both the Old and New Law, we forbid, under threat of anathema, that any layman presume to demand or extort tithes from you.

Furthermore: the tithe along the road from the castle to the cross of the Araldelli, thence through Cluza and Cumuniola as far as [lacuna], and along the road from the castle to the cross of Pedetus as far as the boundary of Frascaritius, excepting the individual holdings of Spitius of the Araldelli and of the Petrozoli; the tithe from the enclosure of Rainerius Malaractus, as the road goes to the Valescella of the Araldelli and thence to the Tresnaria, excepting the holdings of the *mansus* of Giso, Sigulus, and Stanteis; the tithe of the fief of Brunichus and the sons of Girardus; the tithe of that land which Araldus and Lady Cecilia gave to the church; the tithe of the vineyards of Petrocinus of Rome [lacuna] John Stantis and John Madelgisius; the tithe of those lands which are given to the church; the *bubulca* of land given by Richardus; one at Felegaria; one bought by Master Albert from Foliata beside the Runcus of John the priest; and the mill beside the oak-grove of Malaquistus. We also forbid archbishops, bishops, archdeacons, and other ecclesiastical and secular persons to impose new and unlawful exactions upon you.

[Col. 0881A] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Coelestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Alb[—], bishop of Albano. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, title of Pastor. [Col. 0881C] I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement and bishop of Tuscania. I, Rufinus, cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes and bishop of Rimini. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Soffredo, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, on the Ides of June, in the eighth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1191, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Coelestine III.

## XIV. He takes the monastery of Saint Peter of Pescara under protection and confirms its goods and privileges.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 13 June.)*

*[Anecdota Ughelliana, p. 411.]*

**Coelestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Jobel, abbot of the monastery of Saint Clement on the Island of Pescara, called the Golden House, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.**

[Col. 0882A] The duty of the government entrusted to us, and the order of reason itself, invite us to assent to religious vows and to fulfil them by the performance of deeds. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests, and, following the example of Leo, Calixtus, Adrian, and Alexander, Roman pontiffs of blessed memory, our predecessors, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery, where rests the body of Blessed Clement, pope and martyr. It belongs solely to the jurisdiction of Blessed Peter, and you are dedicated there to divine service. We strengthen it by the privilege of this document, so that it shall be held subject to the Roman Church alone and free from the yoke of all churches and persons.

First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order, known to have been instituted in that monastery according to God and the Rule of Blessed Benedict, shall be observed there inviolate for ever. Therefore, by a decree to endure perpetually, we establish that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now lawfully possesses shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

In the county of Penne: the castle of Insula, Castellione, Vinula, Pesculo, Rocca de Soti, Corvario, Petranica, Bectorito, Alannae Farum, Casale Plano, and Colleduno, with all their churches and appurtenances; the castle called Casale of Saint Desiderius, with the churches of Saint Peter of Panepenna, Saint Martin of Muscufo, and Saint Justa of Tagliano. In the city of Saint Angelo: the cell of Saint Clement; the castle of Saint Maurus with its harbour and appurtenances; the church of Saint Cyricus of Montesilvano; the church of Saint Saviour beside the river Nora, with its harbour and appurtenances; the church of Saint Gervasius with its appurtenances; the estates called by surname Palummani, with their households and appurtenances; the churches of Saint Rusticus of Saliano, Saint Angelo on Monte Apriano, Saint Flavian, Saint Mary at Cap[—], Saint Mary of Colle with the chapel of Rocca and all its appurtenances; and the church of Saint Nicholas at Cornisam with its appurtenances.

[Col. 0882D] In the county of Chieti: Bononisato with all its churches and appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Pesula; the church of Saint Angelo of Casula; the church of Saint Cesidius; and the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Lapidaria with its appurtenances. At Caramanico: the church of the Holy Cross; the church of Saint Nicholas with its cells and other appurtenances; the churches of Saint Martin at Gutta, Saint John at Scaviari, and Saint Sylvester of Oligeto with their appurtenances. In the county of Abruzzo: the castle of Guardia, the castle of Vetulum, Monachiscum, and the castle of Saint George, with all their churches and appurtenances. In the March: the castle of Loro, the castle of Caldarola, the castle of Vestimani, Mount Obtetanus, Rotello, Briccia, Saint Vincent, and Saint Angelo at Favara, with the other churches and appurtenances.

[Col. 0883A] In the county of Valva: the settlement called Holy Trinity, with its cells and appurtenances; in the city of Sulmona, the oratory, house and palace formerly of Simeon, houses, small holdings, and all possessions assigned to your monastery within or outside that city; the church of Saint Maurus of Amiternum with its appurtenances; Mount Tarino with its rocks and woods; and the cell of Saint Clement at Lisina with its appurtenances. We also grant you and your successors all the tithing of the aforesaid estates of your church and a share of the offerings made for the dead.

We further forbid any bishop to dare, in the aforesaid places, to celebrate a synod or exercise any episcopal rights unless summoned by you or your successors. You may receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of your monks or clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders, from whichever bishop you prefer. We also decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict. Whatever, moreover, you may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one may be placed in charge by any cunning of deceit or by force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall in the fear of God and according to the Rule of Blessed Benedict judge to be elected; the person elected shall be consecrated by the Roman pontiff. Wishing also with paternal care to provide henceforth for your peace and tranquillity, we forbid by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosure of your houses to commit theft, set fire, seize or kill a person, or rashly inflict any violence upon you, your goods, or those who flee to you.

[Col. 0883D] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future knowingly attempts rashly to act against this page of our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by worthy satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, our Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good works and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Coelestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Peter in Chains, title of Eudoxia. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, title of Pastor. [Col. 0884B] I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement and bishop of Tuscania. I, John Felix, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Romanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, title of Calixtus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Berard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Goffredo, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. [Col. 0884C] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary the New. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Lothair, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, on the Ides of June, in the ninth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1191, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Coelestine III.

## XV. He grants various privileges to the prior and convent of Canterbury.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 20 June.)*

*[WILKINS, Councils, I, 494.]*

[Col. 0884D]

**Coelestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the prior and convent of Canterbury: greeting and apostolic blessing.**

As it is incumbent upon us by virtue of our office to promote the progress of religious life, so, by that same office, we are likewise compelled to oppose with pastoral solicitude those things which seem to hinder the ordinances of the regular order. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, carefully considering the dignity of your church and judging it unworthy that, while you are bound by the bond of monastic profession, you should be summoned elsewhere than in your own chapter when you commit an offence, we grant you by this present letter that none of your brethren, if he should offend, may be compelled by your archbishop to appear for judgment outside your chapter, especially in matters concerning the Rule of Blessed Benedict and the discipline of your order. Rather, we establish that you all shall be treated by that archbishop regularly and honourably, as the ancient and reasonable custom of your church requires.

[Col. 0885A] We also more strictly forbid the aforesaid archbishop, or any other ecclesiastical or secular person, to extort an oath from you or any one of you, or to place any impediment in your way, so that you cannot freely send some of your members to the Apostolic See on the business of your church. Whenever necessity or advantage requires it, we grant you free authority to send one or more of your brethren to the Roman Church. We also grant that, according to God and for the advancement of the chapter, you may freely and peacefully dispose of your goods and retain your seal without anyone’s objection. Neither the same archbishop nor any other person may dare to interfere in the disposition or administration of your possessions or other property contrary to the privileges granted you by the Apostolic See and contrary to the custom of your church.

We further forbid any one of you to presume to leave the enclosure of that church without first obtaining the permission of the prior and convent. But whenever the archbishop is absent, the prior and convent shall be free, according to the custom of that church, to grant brethren permission to leave when necessity presses or when they must labour in your affairs. By this document we also forbid the archbishop to remove your prior, once installed, from the administration of the priory or suspend him from the exercise of his office, contrary to the statutes of the Lateran Council and the custom of your church, without manifest and reasonable cause.

[Col. 0885D] Therefore let no one at all presume to infringe this page of our constitution or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of July, in the first year of our pontificate.

## XVI. He asserts the parochial right of the church of Saint Margaret to the prior and Camaldolese brethren.  
*(Rome, at St Peter’s, 1 June.)*

*[MITTARELLI, Annals of Camaldoli, Appendix, p. 183.]*

**Coelestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the prior and Camaldolese brethren: greeting and apostolic blessing.**
[Col. 0886A] When what is just and honorable is requested of us, the force of equity and the order of reason require that it be brought, through the diligence of our office, to its due effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, for your devotion, the parochial right which your church of Saint Margaret has held undisturbed for forty years; likewise the donations or grants which patrons or other faithful persons have justly made; and also the tithes and other rights of your church belonging to you, just as you have canonically and without dispute possessed all these things for forty years. Therefore let no one, etc. But if anyone, etc.

[Col. 0886B] Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the Kalends of July, in the first year of our pontificate.

XVII. He takes the monastery of Saint Anastasius at Aquae Salviae under protection and confirms its possessions and goods. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, July 6.)

[RATTI, *History of Genzano*, p. 96.]

XVIII. To the chapter of Narbonne.—He confirms the transfer of Berengar, bishop of Lleida, to the metropolitan see of Narbonne. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, July 22.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXI, 614.]

[Col. 0886C] COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the chapter of Narbonne, greetings and apostolic blessing.

That transfers of bishops may lawfully be made by apostolic authority for reasons of utility or necessity is most plainly attested both by the decrees of the canons and by the ancient examples of the holy Fathers. For Saint Peter, our master and prince, was transferred from Antioch to Rome, that he might achieve greater profit there. Eusebius likewise was transferred to Alexandria, and Felix to Ephesus, by the authority of this venerable see for the same reason. Therefore, prompted by this consideration and by many other examples of transfer, and indeed having regard to the advantage of the Church of Narbonne and to the necessity of the time—when, in your [Col. 0886D] regions, the pursuits of various heresies and sects, and the conflicts of wars, are said to have gained strength beyond their usual measure—and also considering the fitness of the person: although some opponents resisted at first, you nevertheless laudably agreed, by the common counsel of the brethren. We therefore hold valid the election which you made of our venerable brother Berengar, bishop of Lleida; confirming it by apostolic authority, we grant him to you as pastor.

We therefore command and enjoin you henceforth, setting aside appeal, to render him the honor and obedience due to him as your spiritual father, as cheerfully as humbly; and to take care to conduct yourselves toward him in such a way that he himself, as a solicitous father, may deserve commendation for his governance of you, and that you, as devoted sons, may receive worthy praise for the obedience shown to him. For we believe and hope that he who conducted himself usefully and honorably in an abbacy and bishopric will, with the Lord’s help, be able in an archbishopric to accomplish things which will advance your Church in temporal matters and, through divine power working with him, will bring about correction and improvement in spiritual matters.

[Col. 0887A] Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of August, in the first year of our pontificate.

XIX. He takes the monastery of Saint Ghislain under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, July 27.)

[REIFFENBERG, *Monuments*, vol. VIII, p. 409.]

[Col. 0887B] COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot of the monastery of Saint Ghislain and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made to us which is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting for us to grant it willingly and to provide suitable support for the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following the example of our predecessors of happy memory, Alexander and Lucius, Roman pontiffs, take under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery of Saint Ghislain, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree [Col. 0887C] that the monastic order which is known to have been instituted in that monastery according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The site itself on which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; the village of Hornut with all its appurtenances; in the village of [Col. 0887D] Slogia, the demesne manor and a ploughland of arable land, with enclosures and every tithe both of that land itself and of all the fiefs of the same village; the tithes which you possess from the lands of Saint Peter; the tithe from Hugh’s vineyard; the hamlet called Ultramontes, with its appurtenances Harminiacum and Beweniis; the tithe from the manor and lands of Saint Landelin; at Novella, one ploughland of arable land; a fourth part of the village of Blelgiis, with its appurtenances and jurisdiction; the village of Waherias and its demesne manor, free from all advocacy-right and tithe; in the village called Wamia, the allod of Gonter and his son Aegidius, of Cing, and the land of Hugh of Aengien, with other lands, enclosures, rents, meadows, and woods; part of the village of Durni, with [Col. 0888A] the village and jurisdiction; the church which you hold from the church of Saint Gaugeric under an annual rent of one hundred solidi of Cambrai currency; in the village of Chasnen, the demesne manor, with lands, meadows, waters, woods, and enclosures, and a share of the tithe, free of every lordship and divided from the other shares; in the village called Harchies, three *fertons* by the weight of Flanders, which the Church of Aulne owes for the land of Heluidis (or Helvidis); at Resbaco, the demesne manor and three parts of the entire allod, in lands, woods, waters, meadows, and rents, with jurisdiction; at Runcherias, six marks of silver, by the Cologne weight, which the Church of Cambron owes under an annual rent for the lands and altar of that place, together with the chapel of Herieri Bridge; the altar of Cella with its appurtenances [Col. 0888B] Hornut and the quarter-share; the church of Durno with its appurtenances Blelgiis, Hercana, Astices, and Slogio; the church of Villari with its appurtenances Harminiacum and Bewengiis; the church of Wamia with its appurtenances Wamiolo and Resiniis; Basecles with its appurtenances; Altregium with the chapel of the village, together with all its appurtenances, free of every exaction except the bishop’s entertainment-right; at Imbrechies, the manor and demesne lands with meadows and waters, two parts of the common allod, free of every exaction; the altar of Bossut, free from the *personatus* and every exaction, except an annual payment of six solidi for the bishop’s entertainment-right; the altar of Baldurno, with its appurtenance Villeroth, free of every exaction except an annual payment of three [Col. 0888C] solidi for the bishop’s entertainment-right; the altars of Eligenies (Elignies) and Tumaides; the chapel of Ramegnies, free from the *personatus* and every exaction except the bishop’s entertainment-right; Abechias with its appurtenances Belchi, Molembais, Popiola, Pierwez, and its other appurtenances; likewise, the altars granted to you by Nicholas of good memory, formerly bishop of Cambrai, and confirmed by his privileges; Harchies, with its appurtenances the Great Church, Stambrusia, and the chapel of Equicampo; the altar of Blatum, free and without a *personatus*; the chapel of Wierez, free except for a *sonegium* of twelve denarii; the altar of Thulin with its appurtenance Hainin; the altar of Hunchignies; the altar of Herselle; [Col. 0888D] the altar of Rascengien; the altar of Humbergher; the altar of Gog with land and its other appurtenances; the altar of Louvignies with its appurtenances Volziis and the chapel of Squery; the chapel of Velfagt and the chapel of Herieri Bridge, free from every exaction and *personatus*; in the village of Alemans, the demesne manor and the tithe of that manor and of the land belonging to it, in lands, vineyards, meadows, and woods; the manor and demesne lands at Altregium and the shares of the common allod in lands, waters, meadows, woods, and rents, free from every exaction and advocacy-right; the village of Bassecles with all its appurtenances, and the administration of that village granted in alms to your monastery.

Moreover, we also confirm to you whatever land or water lies between [Col. 0889A] Wamia and Hanneton, from the source of their springs as far as the places where they fall into the Haine; the whole fishery of the Roa; and the entire fishery from Cremba-Salice to the village of Saint Ghislain on one side, to Cremba-Salice on the other, and on the other side toward the Roa as far as the place where the Roa, joined to the Hanneton, falls into the Haine—except for one small enclosure known to belong to the noblewoman Beatrice of Boussut—and also whatever right you possess in the sale of timber deposited upon the bank of the Haine nearest the Roa, which is called *Wiltragium*.

Furthermore, let no one presume to demand or extort from you tithes from your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the fodder of your animals. And you may receive clerics or laymen fleeing from the world, free and absolved, for conversion, and retain them without any opposition.

We further prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, from leaving it without the permission of his abbot, except for the purpose of adopting a stricter religious life; and no one shall dare retain one who has left without letters of authorization from the community. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice.

Moreover, we hold valid the liberties and immunities, and the ancient and reasonable customs, granted to your church [Col. 0889C] and observed hitherto; and we decree that they shall remain unimpaired in future times. We further forbid anyone to presume, without manifest and reasonable cause, to pronounce against you or your churches a sentence of excommunication or interdict. We also decree that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have decided to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict—while preserving, nevertheless, the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that house, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of fraud or violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall determine ought to be chosen, according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict.

[Col. 0889D] We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; rather, all things shall be preserved intact and shall be wholly available for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, and know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, and from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, etc. But upon all, etc., [Col. 0890A] so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Tusculum. I, Romanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Mary [Col. 0890B] beyond the Tiber, of the title of Callistus. I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. [Col. 0890C] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, Lothair, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, on the sixth day before the Kalends of August, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

XX. He adjudges the monastery of Baume to the monastery of Cluny. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, July 28.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 95.]

[Col. 0890D]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot of the monastery of Cluny and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for perpetual remembrance.

The glorious and wondrous providence of the divine majesty has established diverse ranks and orders in its Church, so that, while inferiors render the due obedience and reverence to superiors, one union may arise out of diversity and the administration of the respective offices may be carried on in an orderly fashion. But just as sons of obedience ought to be cherished in the bosom of Mother Church by the breasts of gracious consolation, so rebellious and proud persons, who through their disobedience incur, as it were, the sin of divination and the crime of idolatry, must be restrained by stricter disciplines of ecclesiastical severity.

[Col. 0891A] Thus the monastery of Baume, which through the brethren gathered there ought to have shone and flourished through the fragrance of good repute and the beauty of religious life, followed the old man with his deeds and, at the devil’s urging, wasted away in their sins. Consequently it had been grievously diminished in both spiritual and temporal matters. But when it pleased Him who disposed all things from eternity to put an end to such great evils and mercifully call that place back to His service, He willed to fill the faces of those brethren with shame, so that through this they might seek His name and might return, even unwillingly, to the way of uprightness.

[Col. 0891B] Therefore, with this justice leading the way, Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, decreed that the aforesaid monastery of Baume, with its appurtenances, should be possessed in perpetuity by the Church of Cluny, and confirmed this by the protection of his privilege. We therefore, following in the footsteps both of Eugenius himself and of Pope Urban, our predecessors of happy memory, confirm by apostolic authority to you—and through you to your Church—the aforesaid monastery, as it is known to have been justly and reasonably granted to you, together with all that it now justly and canonically possesses or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through lawful means; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 0891C] This is on the condition that the monastic order there shall be inviolably observed in future times according to the institution of the Cluniac brethren, and that, because of the rebellion, contumacy, and offence which the abbot and brethren of the monastery of Baume committed against the holy Roman Church, whoever shall in due course obtain the governance of that place through you shall never bear the name of abbot, but only that of prior.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or burden it with any exactions; but all things shall be preserved intact and wholly available for the benefit of those for whose [Col. 0891D] governance and support they were granted, saving, of course, the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment of the iniquity committed, be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But may all who preserve their rights to that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action [Col. 0892A] and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Tusculum. I, John Felix, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Romanus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Anastasia. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of Saint Martin, title of Equitius. I, Cynthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. [Col. 0892B] I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, on the fifth day before the Kalends of August, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

XXI. Privilege for Henry the Lion and his sons, that they may not be excommunicated by any person except the supreme pontiff or his legate *a latere*. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, August 5.)

[*Origines Guelficae*, III, 563.]

[Col. 0892C]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the nobleman Duke HENRY, greetings and apostolic blessing.

If at any time the Roman Church, mother of all the faithful, grants some favor of prerogative mercy to one of the princes whom she remembers to have always shown pure devotion toward her, she does what becomes her; nor should this seem burdensome or in any way absurd to anyone. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, moved by your just prayers and considering the ardor of devotion which you have hitherto shown toward [Col. 0892D] our predecessors and are especially known to show toward our own person, we grant to your nobility, from the kindness of the Apostolic See, lest anyone indiscriminately be allowed rashly to burden you by an ecclesiastical sentence, that no one may dare to pronounce a sentence of excommunication against your person or those of your sons, except only the Roman pontiff, a legate specially dispatched from his side, or perhaps someone acting under a special mandate from us or our successors—unless, indeed, the offence is such as carries the penalty of excommunication by the act itself. If, however, such a sentence should be rashly pronounced, we decree that it shall have no force, as having been issued in contempt of the Apostolic See.

[Col. 0893A] Therefore let no person whatsoever infringe this page of our grant or, by rash presumption, act against it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let that person know that he has incurred the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed Peter and Paul, His apostles.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the Nones of August, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXII. He takes the monastery of Saint Ragnibert in the Jura under protection and confirms its discipline and possessions. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, August 5.)

[GUICHENON, *History of Bresse and Bugey*, p. 234.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUMBERT, abbot of Saint Ragnibert in the Jura, [Col. 0893B] and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, everlasting greeting.

Whenever a request is made to us which is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is altogether fitting for us to grant it willingly and to provide suitable support for the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and take the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, under the protection of Saint Peter and our own, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been instituted in that monastery according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict [Col. 0893C] shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The site itself on which the said monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances and the adjoining borough; the cell of Chamon; the church of Saint Michael of Mont-Audric; the church of Saint Peter of Villari Lagerio, with all their appurtenances; the cell of Villars Sales; the church [Col. 0893D] of Saint Julian of Mont-Major, with all their appurtenances; the cell of Saint Mary of Graveriis and the church of Saint Peter of Sanciaco; the church of Saint Peter of Asperomonte; the church of Saint Balduf; the church of Manusco, with their appurtenances; the cell of Saint Mary of Lueys; the church of Saint Mary of Janua; the church of Luziaco; the church of Saint Desiderius; the church of Campanieu, with their appurtenances; the church of Saint Peter of Benoncia; the church of Saint Andrew of Tenayo; the church of Saint Maurice of Argit; the church of Saint Martin of Vaugiis; the church of Saint Lawrence of Onciaco; the church of Saint Peter of Aranda; the cell of Saint Michael of Rupae; the church of Saint Maurice of Langiis; the church of Saint Hilary of Torciaco; [Col. 0894A] the church of Saint Martin of Cleysieu; the church of Saint Martin of Varey; the church of Saint Maurice of Ambutriaco; the church of Saint Maurice of Meyri; the church of Saint Andrew of Rigniaco; the cell of Saint Peter of Vilieu; the church of Saint Mary of Hospitalari; the chapel of Saint Mary Magdalene of Loyes; the cell of Saint Christopher of Burgo; the cell of Saint Vincent of Faramans; and the church of Saint Martin of Stingiaco, with their appurtenances.

You may also receive clerics and laymen, free and absolved, fleeing from the world, for conversion, and retain them without any opposition. We further prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, from leaving it without the permission of his abbot, except for the purpose of a stricter religious life.

Desiring also, with paternal solicitude, to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we forbid by apostolic authority anyone within the enclosures of your houses or granges to commit robbery or theft, set fire, seize or kill a person, or rashly exercise any violence. We further decree that no one may presume to build a new church or oratory within your parishes without your permission and that of the diocesan bishop, saving the grants of Roman pontiffs.
