When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. We command that chrism, holy oil, consecrations [Col. 0894C] of altars or churches, and the ordinations of monks who are to be promoted to sacred orders shall be provided for you without any improper condition by the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic and enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved intact and shall be wholly available for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, after a second or third warning, unless that person corrects the offence by worthy satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honor, know himself or herself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and at the last judgment be subject to severe vengeance. But may all who preserve their rights to that place have the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of [Col. 0895A] Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, on the Nones of August, in the ninth indiction, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Tusculum. I, John Felix, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, of the title of Callistus. [Col. 0895B] I, Hugh, cardinal priest of Saint Martin. I, Beraldus, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, John, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin.

XXIII. He confirms the privilege of the provost and brethren of the church of Saint Nicholas at Stendal: if the diocesan bishop refuses to confer ecclesiastical sacraments, they may receive them from any bishop. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, apparently August 7.)

[RIEDEL, *Codex diplomaticus Brandenburgensis*, I, V, 26.—See the privilege granted to them by Clement III, *Patrologia*, vol. CCIV, no. 60.]

[Col. 0895C]

XXIV. 1. He forbids a synod to be held in the church of Saint Nicholas at Stendal against the will of the brethren, and forbids that church to be subjected to interdict.—2. He confirms for the provost and brethren of Saint Nicholas at Stendal the privilege concerning the care of souls granted by Lucius III. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, apparently August 7.)

[See RIEDEL, cited above.]

XXV. He takes the church of Saint Nicholas at Stendal under protection. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, August 9.)

[Same source.]

[Col. 0895D] COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the provost of Saint Nicholas at Stendal and his brethren, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

. . . We graciously assent to your just petitions and, following the example of Pope Clement, our predecessor of pious memory, take the aforesaid church of Saint Nicholas, in which you are devoted to divine service, into the right and property of Saint Peter under the protection of the Apostolic See, and fortify it for the future by pontifical grant, decreeing that whatever possessions, etc.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the fifth day before the Ides of August, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Celestine III.

XXVI. He takes the church of Saint Mary and Saint John the Evangelist at Schwerin under protection and confirms its goods and privileges. (Rome, at Saint Peter’s, October 24.)

[LUNIG, *Spicilegium ecclesiasticum*, II, Appendix, 154.]

[Col. 0896A]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the Church of Schwerin, present and future, canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

It accords with the mercy of apostolic governance to cherish churchmen and to fortify their houses with pious protection. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to uprightness that we, who have been raised to the governance of churches, should protect them from the wickedness of evil men [Col. 0896B] and cherish them under the patronage of the Apostolic See. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, following in the footsteps of Pope Clement, our predecessor of happy memory, take under the protection of Saint Peter and our own the aforesaid Church of Schwerin, dedicated in honor of the Blessed Mary, Mother of God, and Saint John the Evangelist, and endowed by the nobleman Duke II. [name or numeral uncertain], in which you are devoted to divine service; and we fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the Lord’s favor, acquire through grants of pontiffs, gifts of kings or princes, offerings [Col. 0896C] of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these, we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

At Brezne, thirty *mansi*; at Ylowe, four villages: Curiwiz, Mentina, Qvazentin, and Insliz; at Schwerin, one village, Liscowe, which after a change of name is called Alta villa (“High Village”); at Silasne, Rampe; at Sadelbandingen, Borist; beyond the Elbe, Virichim and manors at Todendorp; Nauliz near Lugouve; the naval toll at Plote; the parish at Schwerin with every right; one half of the tithe at Sclazne; one third of the tithe at Mikelenburch; one third of the tithe at Ylowe; one third of the tithe at Zareze; one third of the tithe at Warnowe; one third of the tithe at Mariz; and the whole tithe [Col. 0896D] in your villages throughout the bishopric of Schwerin.

For the deanery of the same church, two marks of denarii from episcopal revenues—one at Mickelenburg and the other at Ylowe—and two large measures of grain, called *wichs kepel*; from the mill situated on the northern side of the city of Schwerin, annually one *brachium* of wheat and another of rye; for the lights of the same church, the new toll at Plone and one third of the revenues at Nauliz.

Furthermore, we confirm to you by apostolic authority free election in choosing deans, provosts, and canons, and free disposition in collecting stipends, as you have possessed hitherto. We decree that, for the funeral, the thirtieth-day observance, and the anniversary; for paying debts; and for rewarding servants [Col. 0897A] of any deceased canon, the stipend which he had in the church while alive shall remain vacant for one year after his death, according to the custom of your Church. We likewise confirm by apostolic authority to that place, through the page of this present writing, the honor and dignity of the pontifical see which the Church of Schwerin is known to have possessed hitherto.

We also confirm with perpetual stability to the oft-mentioned Church the entire endowment assigned for the bishop’s use: namely, the whole land of Butisowe with every utility and appurtenance; six villages in Ylowe—Moytz, Ledarsiz, Gugulvosei, Jastrowe, Pancoviz, Gnesdiz, Liuzchou, and Goderaoc; at Kizin, Wotencha near Dimin, with other villages; one village in Muriz and another in Warnowe; the island adjacent to Schwerin [Col. 0897B] as far as the stream, and another island near Dobin, called Libiz.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but all things shall be preserved intact and shall be wholly available for the benefit of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, anyone in the future, etc.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, on the eighth day before the Kalends of November, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of [Col. 0897C] Lord Pope Celestine III.

XXVII. [To Umberto, archbishop of Arles?] He grants him authority to restrain by ecclesiastical censures the disorders that have arisen in Provence. (At the Lateran, November 5.)

[PAPON, *General History of Provence*, vol. II, p. 27.]

COELESTINE, bishop, etc.

When the Redeemer of humankind came down to earth in order to restore peace between God and humanity, it befits your brotherhood diligently to strive to preserve that peace among your parishioners and to employ pontifical aid toward this end. Since, therefore, we have heard that very many quarrels are arising both in your city and in its borough, [Col. 0897D] and that mutual killings and other injuries between the parties result from them, by the authority of these present letters we grant you leave freely to bind with the bond of malediction and excommunication those of your citizens or burgesses who, contrary to your admonition, refuse to restore peace and concord with their adversaries. You shall also have full power to strike with a sentence of excommunication those who seize or despoil persons suffering shipwreck, or take their property from them; and those who presume to capture pilgrims, merchants, or others travelling along the roads, to plunder their goods, or newly to increase tolls. Moreover, relying on our authority, and without appeal, you may punish heretics; those who receive them or extend favor to them; Aragonese, Brabançons, and those foreign companies which are said to ravage your province; [Col. 0898A] and further those who hire them, receive them in castles, towns, or cities, sell to them or buy from them, or enter into any commercial dealings with them.

Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of November, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXVIII. He confirms an agreement made between the churches of St. Mary and Holy Cross at Étampes. (Lateran, November 7.)

[FLEUREAU, *Les Antiquitez de la ville et du duché d'Estampes*, p. 390.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son ODON CLEMENT, abbot of Saint Mary [Col. 0898B] of Étampes, notary of the letters of our dearest son in Christ Philip, illustrious king of the French, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Cases settled by agreement or judgment ought to be fortified by apostolic authority, lest they relapse and be reopened in the future. Therefore, moved by your prayers, we confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the agreement made by common consent between your church and the church of Holy Cross, as is more fully contained in the written judgment of the delegates of the aforesaid king and of the bishop of Paris—the abbot of Sainte-Geneviève, the dean, cantor, and chancellor of the Church of Paris—and which has been concluded between you without any improper dealing and has hitherto been observed.

[Col. 0898C] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to act contrary to it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, seven days before the Ides of November, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXIX. A bull which first establishes that the Order of St. Benedict shall be observed forever on Mount Cruzenberg; then that its goods shall remain perpetually unimpaired; and, specifically, [concerning] Erctestedt, Saverhausen, Dsthaimb, Bolthaimb, Heit-Zelle, Ingelmarstadt, Rapuldis, the houses of that same [monastery], and other property at Hersfeld, and revenues from salt at Salzungen. Moreover, by a general decree he grants the right to celebrate divine offices subject to the stated conditions, and likewise the right to elect an abbot according to the Rule of St. Benedict. (Lateran, November 12.)

[WENCK, *Hess. Landesg.*, III, charter 87.]

[Col. 0898D]

XXX. Under pain of excommunication, he commands the monks of Cluny to return to the monks of Savilliano their charters, which they have long retained. (Lateran, December 2.)

[*Historiae patriae Monum.*, *Chartae*, I, 970.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and monks of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As you would not wish to be harassed by others, so, as religious men fearing the Lord, you ought more carefully to refrain from injuring others. You are to know that it has come to the hearing of our apostolic office, as the beloved sons the abbot and brethren of Savilliano report, that you retain their privileges at your own discretion and, though repeatedly asked, have hitherto refused to return them. Since, therefore, we do not wish their loss to remain without due correction, we who are bound to exercise special care for them, we command and strictly enjoin you by apostolic letters to return those same privileges to the aforesaid brethren without delay or difficulty. Otherwise, know that we have firmly commanded our venerable brother, the archbishop of Milan, relying on our authority, not to delay compelling you to do this by [Col. 0899B] excommunications and a sentence of interdict.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Nones of December, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXXI. To the prelates of England.—On behalf of William, bishop of Ely. (Lateran, December 2.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXII, 594.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren, the archbishops and bishops established in the kingdom of England, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When our beloved son in Christ Richard, [Col. 0899C] illustrious king of the English, girded himself, having taken up the sign of the cross, to avenge the injury done to the Redeemer, he placed under apostolic protection the care of governing his kingdom—an office which, as a prudent man seeking the Lord, he judged ought to yield to that service. We both wish and ought to preserve the constitution, rights, and honor of his kingdom with greater zeal, inasmuch as, trusting in our protection, he exposed his person and possessions to greater dangers for the exaltation of holy religion, and is known, as his deeds make clear, to show himself more praiseworthily and more fervently in the Creator’s service, the Lord working with him a sign for good.

Since, therefore, we have learned that certain acts have been attempted both against that kingdom itself and against your venerable [Col. 0899D] father [perhaps “brother”], William, bishop of Ely, legate of the apostolic see, to whom he entrusted the government of the kingdom, by John, count of Mortain, and by certain others—acts which contain some grounds for suspicion and, if true, are known to redound to no slight insult against the apostolic see—we have judged that this presumption must be confronted all the more promptly because delay itself might bring graver harm to the said king and to the land of Jerusalem, and greater disgrace to us and to the Roman Church.

[Col. 0900A] Accordingly, by apostolic letters we command your whole body, and in virtue of obedience enjoin you, that if, as has been reported to us, the aforesaid count or anyone else should presume to lay violent hands upon the said bishop, seize him, extort any oath from him by violence, hold him captive, or in any way alter the condition of the kingdom as established by royal authority before the king’s departure, then, laying aside every pretext or quarrel, assemble together and publicly declare the aforesaid count, together with all advisers, instigators, accomplices, and supporters of the aforesaid presumption, to be bound by excommunication, with candles lit and bells rung, setting aside every appeal, excuse, and respect of persons. [Col. 0900A] Cause those thus excommunicated to be more strictly shunned by all; and in their lands and in other lands which they may have invaded, wholly forbid the celebration of divine offices, without impediment of appeal, except for penances and the baptism of infants, [Col. 0900B] until, after the said legate has first been released both from captivity and from the oath, and the kingdom itself restored to the condition established by the aforementioned king before his departure, they come together to the apostolic see to receive absolution, bearing letters of testimony both from that legate and from you.

Know certainly that if you are negligent or remiss in carrying out this our command, then, God granting it, we shall judge that no lesser punishment ought to be inflicted upon you than if the aforesaid injury had been done to our own person or to one of our brethren.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of December, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXXII. He receives the monastery of St. Peter at Savilliano under protection and confirms its possessions. (Lateran, December 5.)

[*Historiae pat. Monum.*, *Chart.*, I, 973.]

[Col. 0900C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WILLIAM, abbot, and the monks of Saint Peter of Savilliano, present and future, professing the regular life, forever.

It is fitting to grant effect to just petitioners, and [lacuna] both equity and the order of reason require it, especially when piety assists the petitioners’ wish and truth does not oppose it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following the example of our predecessor Pope Lucius of blessed memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen with the privilege of this present writing, the aforesaid monastery of Saint Peter of Savilliano, [Col. 0900D] in which you are devoted to divine service, and which is known to belong directly, without any intermediary, to the right and property of blessed Peter. We first establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolably in perpetuity.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the aforesaid monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, acquire through the Lord’s favor, shall remain firm and unimpaired to you [Col. 0901A] and your successors. We have judged that the following should be expressly named:

Whatever you possess in Savilliano, Strepeto Marenae, the town of Maxi, Ricrossae Sarmatario, Duania, Monte Falcone, San Gregorio, Fontana, Cabalario Majore, Cavalario Leone, Solaria, Marchione, Salucia, Centallo, Bosnasio, Gragnasio, Nigella, Crespibulo, Cinglio, Lugia, and Morra Maggiore, both in churches and parishes and their tithes, lands, vineyards, meadows, cultivated and uncultivated fields, streams, and mills.

Furthermore, let no one presume to exact or extort tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands which you till with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the fodder of your animals. You may also receive into conversion free and unencumbered clerics or laymen fleeing the world, and retain them without any contradiction. We further prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in that place, from being permitted to leave it without his abbot’s permission, save by reason of [lacuna]. No one may dare retain one who departs without security provided by your letters.

When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, the ordination of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, [Col. 0901C] and the other ecclesiastical sacraments from whichever bishop you prefer, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the grace and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to provide these to you freely and without [lacuna] of any kind.

We also decree that the burial-place of that monastery shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who choose to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any craft of deception or violence, save one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall determine ought to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

[Col. 0901D] Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away or retain its possessions once taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop in the aforesaid churches. As a sign of this liberty received from the apostolic see, and that the same monastery belongs by right to blessed Peter, you shall pay one Byzantine gold coin each year to us and to our successors.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly, should attempt rashly to contravene this page of our constitution, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offense by fitting satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of the Lord our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen. Fare well.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. [Col. 0902B] I, John, cardinal of the title of St. Clement, bishop of Tusculum. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Conrad, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian. I, Infredus, cardinal of St. Mary in Via Lata. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, Gregory, deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Lothair, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

[Col. 0902C] Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aegidius, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, on the Nones of December, in the tenth indiction, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

XXXIII. He confirms certain possessions to [Hugh], bishop of Coventry. (Lateran, December 5.)

[*Monastic. Anglic.*, III, 232.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop of Coventry, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0902D] When that which is just and honorable is requested of us, the vigor of equity and the order of reason require that it be brought to its due effect through the diligence of our office. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, gladly concurring in your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority and strengthen with the protection of this present writing, for you and for your Church of Lichfield, the churches of Bromley and Alrewas, and the towns of Cannock and Rugeley, with their churches and all their appurtenances, situated in your diocese, just as you and your church possess them by royal grant, rightfully and without dispute.

Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to act contrary to it. But should anyone presume to attempt this, [Col. 0903A] let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of December, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXXIV. He confirms to the clergy of Cardona the church of Liemon. (Lateran, December 16.)

[GUENTHER, *Cod. diplom.*, I, 474.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the clergy of the church of Cardona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When churchmen ask of us something that does not depart from reason, we ought to grant them our assent all the more readily, because their care has been entrusted to us more particularly. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, gladly concurring in your just requests, we confirm by apostolic authority and strengthen with the protection of this present writing, for you and for your church, the church of Liemon, just as your metropolitan has reasonably granted it to you and you possess it peacefully. Let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to act contrary to it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXXV. He confirms to the archbishop of Esztergom the right to crown the king of Hungary and “to bind the heads of the officials of the royal household with the bond of anathema and to judge in spiritual causes.” (Lateran, December 20.)

[FÉJER, *Cod. diplom. Hung.*, II, 276.]

[Col. 0903C]

XXXVI. By letters issued to the archbishop of Esztergom, he confirms the liberty of the church of the Transylvanian Teutons, made a provostship. (Lateran, December 20.)

[Ibid.]

XXXVII. He confirms the goods and privileges of William, lord of Montpellier. (Lateran, December 24.)

[GARIEL, *Series praesulum*, etc., vol. II, p. 240.]

[Col. 0903D]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the nobleman WILLIAM, lord of Montpellier, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Considering, beloved son in the Lord, and more diligently observing how devoted William, your ancestor of illustrious memory, was to the Holy Roman Church and to ourselves when we held a lesser office; and hoping also that your vigor ought to imitate his sincere devotion toward the Roman Church and ourselves, we graciously grant your petitions. We receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen with the protection of this present writing, your person, your son William, and the goods which you now reasonably possess or may hereafter, through the Lord’s favor, acquire by lawful means. [Col. 0904A]

Following the model of the concession granted by our predecessor Alexander of blessed memory to your ancestor, we establish that no person whatsoever, except the Roman pontiff, one to whom he has given a special command, or a legate sent from his side, may bind your person with the bond of excommunication, unless by the very nature of the offense you should incur a sentence of excommunication—for example, by laying hands upon clerics or persons subject to religion, or by setting fire. Likewise, no one may dare place under interdict your chapel at Montpellier or the other chapel in the castle of Palude, so as to prevent divine offices from being celebrated in them for you and your household, excluding excommunicated persons and those expressly interdicted. [Col. 0904B] Yet from each chapel, because both were bestowed upon blessed Peter by your ancestors, one gold coin shall be paid each year to our Lateran palace, as was previously established; provided, however, that the tithes, first-fruits, and all other matters belonging to parochial right remain intact to the Church of Maguelone.

Given at the Lateran, on the ninth day before the Kalends of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

XXXVIII. He confirms to Theobald, bishop of Chiusi, and to his church all their goods and rights. (Lateran, December 27.)

[MURATORI, *Antiq. Ital.*, VI, 421.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to [Col. 0904C] our beloved brother THEOBALD, bishop of Chiusi, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Moved by compassion for the poverty of the Church of Chiusi entrusted to you, and following in the footsteps of our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Honorius, Eugenius, Anastasius, and Adrian, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves that Church over which, with God’s help, you preside, so that its clerical orders, and whatever possessions and goods your Church now possesses or shall possess in the future, may remain firm and unimpaired to you and your successors.

First, the cathedral church of Saint Secundianus; the church of Saint Mustiola; the hospital [Col. 0904D] of Saint Irenaeus; the parish church of Saint Mary of Bagno; the parish church of Saint Donatus of Radicofani; the parish church of Saint John of Queneto; the parish church of Saint Mary of Spino, with the chapel of Saint John and its farmholdings; the parish church of Saint Martin of Fabbrica with all its appurtenances; the parish church of Saint John of Pupille; the parish church of Saint Donatus; the parish church of Saint Martin with the chapel of Saint Quiricus of Castello Algisi; the parish church of Saint Eleutherius; the parish church of Saint Mary of Peretulo; the parish church of Saint Mary of Runcano; the parish church of Saint Donatus; the parish church of Saint Cervasius; the parish church of Saint Severus of Verlano; the parish church of Saint Terentianus of Materno; the parish church of Saint Mary of Figline with its chapels; the parish church of Saint Caesarius; the parish church of Saints Cosmas and Damian; the parish church of Saint Sylvester; the parish church [Col. 0905A] of Saint Victorinus with the chapel of Saint Martin; the parish church of Saint Philip; the Hermitage of Vivo; the parish church of Saint Flora, with all its appurtenances; the parish church of Saint Peter of Auliano with the chapel of Lugnole; and whatever you possess in the church of Saint Leonard of Castello de Plano; the parish church of Saint Mary of Muscia with the chapel of Castellione Ugonis; the parish church of Saint Lawrence.

Likewise, the estates belonging to that bishopric: namely, the estate of Saint Flora of Noceto; the estate of Bugnano with the castle of Potentino and its tower, situated above the River Vivo; the estate of Saint Clement; the chapel of Saint Paul of Moterlo and the parish church of Saint Ansanus; the estate of Montealtulo; the estate of Capitino and of Lojano; Corvaja with its chapel; Mount Torino; the estate of Bruscaja with the castle of Ceculo; [Col. 0905B] the estate of Rasarone with the chapel of Saint Adrian; the monastery of Saint Peter in Campo; the estate of Saint Angel of Cervinaja; the parish church of Saint Mamilian at Cignano, with its appurtenances; the estate of Saint Quiricus of Pulsignano; the chapel of Saint Paul; the estate of Puteolo with the chapel of Saint Peter; the estate of Casa Maggiore with its chapel; the estate of Saint Saviour; the estate of Caliano; the estate of Mugnano; the monastery of Saint Benedict, situated beside the River Tresiani; the church of Saint Paul of Materno; the church of Saint Andrew of Fracta; the chapel of Saint Angel of Rivo; the chapel of Saint Chrysanthus and Tavernelle with Roso; the church of Saint Honorata with all its appurtenances; the estate of Petrognano; Mount Venus; the estate of Raspista; the estate of Campilli; [Col. 0905C] the estate of Saint John of Terninano; the estate of Valcalla; the estate of Martiniano; the estate of Resignano; the estate of Fabbrica; the chapel of Saint Mary of Flojano; the church of Saint Mary of Fortunula; the estate of Tilliano; the estate of Pistulla; the estate of Valliano; the castle of Carriolo with its entire estate; the chapel of Saint Justus with its appurtenances; the estate of Cignano; the church of Saint Peter; the church of Saint Lawrence; Mount Luculi; a fourth part of the castle of Asciano by the testament of Count Manente; the castle of Montolla with its entire district; and half of everything which it possessed from Serra of Sarthiano as far as the River Clanis, excepting what it possessed in Colle Franculi.

Moreover, the church of Saint Peter; the church of Saint [Col. 0905D] Sylvester; the church of Saint Pantaleon; the chapel of Saint Dominic; the church of Saint Sabinus; the church of Saint John of Guerneto; the church of Saint Hilary with all its appurtenances; the estate of Murelle with all its appurtenances. Furthermore, the fisheries which you possess at the Port of Casali, in the Plain of Lignallia, in the Vena of Arrone, above and below the bridge over the Clanis, at Ulma, and at Volatu.

Therefore we decree that no archbishop may presume, without the permission of the bishop of Chiusi, to consecrate churches, make chrism, ordain clerics, or impose public penance in the aforesaid parish. Nor may anyone unreasonably impede the episcopal right of the bishopric of Chiusi—namely, the fourth part of tithes and offerings both of the living and the dead, and other things due to it under the statutes of the sacred canons—nor rashly disturb that church, take away or retain its possessions once taken, diminish them, or harass it in any way with vexations; but all things shall be preserved intact for the benefit both of clerics and of the poor, saving the authority of the apostolic see. If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul. [Col. 0906B] I, John, cardinal of the title of St. Clement, bishop of Tusculum. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of St. M . . ., title of Equitius. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Joffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary Nova.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Aegidius of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, on the sixth day before the Kalends of January, in the eleventh indiction, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

XXXIX. He commands Stenar, bishop of Växjö, not to invade the possessions of C[ol], bishop of Linköping. (Lateran, December 28.)

[LILJEGREN, *Dipl. Suec.*, I, 124.]

[Col. 0906C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother STENAR, bishop of Växjö, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The office imposed upon us admonishes and exhorts us to assist those suffering injustice and to grant them, by the aid of apostolic authority, the assent due for obtaining justice. Accordingly, by apostolic letters we command your devotion not to presume to inflict injuries upon our venerable brother C., bishop of Linköping, concerning what he possesses and what his predecessors possessed peacefully; rather, permit him to enjoy his rights in such a manner that we are not compelled, justice requiring it, to exercise due punishment against you.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

XL. He commands C[inthius], cardinal priest of the title of St. Lawrence in Lucina and legate of the apostolic see, and P[eter], archbishop of Uppsala, and J[erpulf], bishop of Skara, to settle the dispute of C[ol], bishop of Linköping, and S[tenar], bishop of Växjö, over the boundary of their dioceses. (Lateran, December 31.)

[Ibid.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0907A] son C., cardinal priest of Saint Lawrence in Lat[eran], legate of the apostolic see, and to his venerable brethren P., archbishop of Uppsala, and J., bishop of Skara, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have judged that the case pending between our venerable brethren C., bishop of Linköping, and S., bishop of Växjö, concerning the boundaries of their bishoprics, should be entrusted to your experience and brought to its proper conclusion without appeal. By apostolic letters we command that, after summoning the parties into your presence, you carefully hear what is put forward on both sides and settle that case according to justice, without appeal. If all of you cannot take part in carrying this out, nevertheless let two of you execute it.

[Col. 0907B] Given at the Lateran, on the second day before the Kalends of January, in the first year of our pontificate.

XLI. To the monks of St. Augustine at Canterbury, he grants “that they may celebrate divine offices during a general interdict.”

(See the chronicle of W. Thorn, in TWISDEN, *Hist. Angl. Script.*, II, 1839.)

XLII. He confirms the privilege of the monastery of St. Augustine at Canterbury “concerning the blessing of the abbot.”

[See ibid.]

XLIII. To the monastery of St. Augustine at Canterbury, he “confirms the church of Northbourne with its chapels for the use of the almonry.”

[See ibid.]

[Col. 0907C]

XLIV. To the monastery of St. Augustine at Canterbury, he “confirms the prebend of Gustone for the clothing of the monks.”

[See ibid.]

XLV. He commands R[oger], abbot of St. Augustine at Canterbury, to see “that none of the clerics assign to anyone at farm the church entrusted to him.” (Fragment.)

[TWYSDEN, *H. A. Scr.*, II, 1840.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son R., abbot of Saint Augustine, etc.

“We have heard and hear”; and below: “By apostolic authority we forbid any of your clerics to assign at farm to anyone the church entrusted to him. If he does so, you may, by apostolic authority, deprive him of the benefice of that church until he has made suitable satisfaction.”

XLVI. To Roger, abbot of St. Augustine at Canterbury, he permits “that if anyone who has obtained an ecclesiastical benefice from the monastery refuses to render the customary oath of fidelity, he may suspend him from receiving the benefice.” (Fragment.)

[Ibid.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God.

“Since from ancient [custom]”; and below: “By these present letters we grant you leave that, if anyone who has obtained an ecclesiastical benefice from that [Col. 0908A] monastery refuses to render the customary oath of fidelity, you shall suspend him by our authority from receiving the benefice, and shall cause him to remain suspended until he gives the customary security.”

XLVII. He confirms the privileges of the monastery of Saint Augustine at Canterbury.

[Ibid.]

XLVIII. He informs Sueno, bishop of Aarhus, that he has permitted Absalon, archbishop of Lund, “to grant him leave to resign his bishopric.”

[LANGEBEK, *Scriptores rerum Danicarum*, vol. V, p. 255.]

[Col. 0908B] CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother SUENO, bishop of Aarhus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From the letters of our venerable brother Absalon, archbishop of Lund, and from the report of others, we have learned that your brotherhood has hitherto exercised the solicitude of the pontifical office in such a manner that the clergy and people subject to your jurisdiction have, through divine grace favoring you, received increase both spiritually and temporally. But because, on account of the infirmity of old age and the multitude of burdens which necessarily accompany the episcopal office, you have proposed to lay aside the burden you undertook—concerning which our predecessor Urban of pious memory received your petition addressed to him and sent you a letter of indulgence—we have judged these matters should be entrusted to the discretion of the aforesaid archbishop, [Col. 0908C] so that he may grant you leave to resign the bishopric when you request it, provide from the goods of your church, according to its means, what may enable you to be honorably maintained, and cause what he shall establish in this matter to be firmly observed.

[Note: [Col. 0907] It cannot have been issued later than the year 1191, for Sueno the bishop died in that year.]

XLIX. He writes to Absalon, archbishop of Lund, appropriately in accordance with the preceding letter.

(Ibid., p. 256.)

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ABSALON, archbishop of Lund, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have always held such confidence in your integrity that you would not seek to carry out anything by authority of the apostolic see [Col. 0908D] unless you knew it to be supported by equity and honor. Thus we assent all the more confidently to the requests of your brotherhood because we know by surer experience the purity of your conscience.

As your charity informed us by letter, and as we have perceived from the tenor of the letters of our venerable brother Sueno, bishop of Aarhus, Pope Urban, our predecessor of blessed memory, granted the said bishop leave, because the infirmity of old age and excessive pastoral care weighed upon him, freely to resign the bishopric whenever he wished; and he entrusted to your discretion the task of providing for him from the revenues of the bishopric, which he had greatly increased, [Col. 0909A] in such a way that the means of his maintenance would thereafter impose a burden upon no one.

We, therefore, wishing in this respect to accede to both your petition and his, command your brotherhood by apostolic letters, since such is his wish and necessity presses upon him, to grant that bishop authority to resign and to provide, according to the means of his church, what may enable him to be suitably maintained for as long as he lives. What you decide should be done in this matter, we decree shall be held ratified and command to be inviolably observed.

YEAR 1191–1192.

L. He commands certain bishops concerning the wife of R. [Canute], king of the Swedes, to release her from the vow of continence undertaken on account of illness.

[LILJEGREN, *Dipl. Suec.*, I, 682.]

[Col. 0909B]

CELESTINE III.

Our beloved son in Christ, R., the illustrious king of the Swedes, humbly informed our apostolic office by letter and messenger that, when he was a young man and his beloved wife a young woman, binding themselves by mutual faith to the vow of contracting a lawful marriage, they confirmed their mutual consent, with their parents’ approval, by the gift of earnest money. Afterwards, however, when his father N. of illustrious memory had been slain by enemies, and he was hard pressed on every side [by the adversity of wars], [Col. 0909C] and, having engaged his enemies, had been defeated and put to flight, he feared that his betrothed might be violently carried off by his enemies, and that no other woman like her might be found in the kingdom whom he could marry. Therefore, on the advice of his own parents and those of the same betrothed woman, it came about that she received the monastic habit in a convent of nuns, without any intention of retaining it permanently; and she remained there for some years, so that she might suffer no injury from his enemies. When peace had been restored and he had obtained victory over his enemies, he solemnly took her as wife amid great rejoicing, and had children by her; one of them, by the common consent and election of the princes of Sweden, he appointed as his successor in the kingdom. But as time passed, the aforesaid wife was seized by a grave illness; believing that she would depart this life, she was induced by fear of death to vow continence. Since the king himself did not wish to distress her, he consented for a time; but now he declares that he cannot maintain continence, and wishes to return to his wife’s bed, as he believed this could lawfully be done. To restrain the disparagements and reproaches of his rivals, he asked us to command that, by our authority, he might treat his wife with marital affection, notwithstanding the vow of continence rashly made by her and temporarily approved by the same king.

But because we could not fully ascertain the truth concerning these matters, we have thought fit to commit their examination and canonical determination to your Fraternity. By apostolic letters we command you diligently to investigate the truth; and if it is established to you that the aforesaid woman was first received among the nuns through fear of violence and abduction, and that, while she remained among them, she acknowledged that she had intended to marry—especially since afterwards she publicly married the king in the face of the Church and, living with him until these times, bore children by him—you shall declare that she is not bound to the aforesaid monastery. For that act cannot dissolve the marriage contracted, even if perhaps it could have impeded a marriage yet to be contracted. Concerning the other matter, let the discernment of your Fraternity examine it so carefully that, if you find that she vowed continence while oppressed by grave illness, and that her husband consented for a time—especially if that same husband did not likewise vow perpetual continence—you shall cause her to live with her husband, and cause each of them to treat the other with marital affection.

## A.D. 1192

### LI. He confirms the goods of the Liberian basilica at Palestrina. (Lateran, January 4.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, vol. I, col. 200.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God . . . .

. . . . And we have thought fit, by this present instrument, to release you from such assessments, insofar as this has hitherto been observed there. Furthermore, because Pope Clement III, our predecessor of happy memory, while he held a lesser office and presided over the see of Palestrina, caused a palace to be built at his own expense in your church, he forbade the bishop of Palestrina for the time being any opportunity whatsoever of inhabiting it, granting it to another, or demanding anything from you on its account. Nor may any of our successors grant that palace to anyone, or demand anything from you because he caused it to be built at his own expense; rather, you are to possess it freely for common use in perpetuity, just as you possess the other houses. Furthermore . . . . because he had been educated and brought up from childhood in your church, and held that place in the greatest veneration and reverence, Pope Eugene III of happy memory granted three twelfths of the offerings of St. Peter and of the ministries to the church of St. Peter; he himself, with the counsel of his brethren, gave, granted in perpetuity, and confirmed to you, and through you to the aforesaid church, one twelfth from the nine twelfths of those offerings which remained to the apostolic see, deducting nevertheless the customary expenses which must be incurred in proportion to its amount. We, following in his footsteps, hold ratified both the constitution and grant concerning the palace and also the gift of that twelfth; and we decree that it shall remain unimpaired in future times.

Therefore we decree that no person may, etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Giles, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, on the second day before the Nones of January, [Col. 0911A] indiction 10, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I . . . . . . I . . . . . . I, John, of the title of St. John. I . . . . . . cardinal of the title of St. Eusebius . . . . I, Romanus, of the title of St. Anastasia . . . . I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of St. Martin at Equitius. I, John, of the title of St. Stephen on the Coelian Hill, cardinal priest. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico. [Col. 0911B] I, Renaldus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary the New. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin.

### LII. He receives under protection the church of St. Thomas of Halberstadt, founded by Bishop Theoderic and entrusted to Premonstratensian monks. (Rome, St. Peter’s, January 20.)

[JAFFÉ, *Regesta*, 890.]

### LIII. He confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of Marbach. (Rome, St. Peter’s, January 21.)

[WUERDTWEIN, *Nova Subsidia diplomatica*, vol. X, p. 161.]

[Col. 0911C] COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the provost and canons of Marbach, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever a request is made to us which is recognized as befitting religion and honesty, it is fitting for us willingly to grant it and to extend apostolic protection in accordance with the petitioners’ wishes. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, favorably assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the possessions and goods which you now reasonably possess, or may hereafter acquire by lawful means, God being favorable. We further decree that, whenever a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate divine service behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons and with subdued voice. Moreover, we prohibit anyone from unjustly pronouncing against you or your church a sentence of excommunication or interdict. We also decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and last wishes of defenders of your church who lawfully hold that status by succession, should they determine to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict—without prejudice, however, to the rights of those churches from which the bodies are taken.

Therefore let no person at all be permitted to infringe this charter of our protection and constitution, or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty [Col. 0912A] God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February, in the first year of our pontificate.

### LIV. He receives under protection the monastery of St. Mary’s Valley at Helmstedt and confirms its possessions. (Rome, St. Peter’s, January 21.)

[*Origines Guelficae*, III, 564.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of St. Mary’s Valley, professed of the Cistercian order, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When what is just and honorable is requested of us, both the force of equity and the order of reason require that it be brought to its due effect through the care of our office. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your just petitions, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves your monastery, with all that it now reasonably possesses or may hereafter acquire by lawful means under the Lord’s protection. In particular, we confirm to you, and through you to the same monastery, by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the possessions set down below, just as you possess them lawfully and without dispute.

First: the estate of Brandesleve with its appurtenances; the wood adjoining that estate, which you exchanged [Col. 0912C] with the illustrious woman Regilinda and her son Gevehard, acting as guarantor. From the gift of the nobleman Theoderic of Sunnebeke, a field adjoining that estate and its tithe. In the village of Kissellinge, thirteen hides: seven for the use of the brethren and six belonging to the church situated in that village; first by gift of the noble prince Adalbert the count palatine, and then of Wichmann, bishop of Magdeburg. From the gift of Count Frederick and his brothers of Amuordesleve, eight hides: four in Greater Amuordesleve, three in Lesser Amuordesleve, and one in Everinge. From the gift of Countess Luchardis, one and a half hides in the village called Grasleve. From the gift of Conrad of Holdenstidde, half a hide in the village called Crispenrod. In the village called Winienstede, half a hide [Col. 0912D] bought for a price; in the village called Uppenrod, half a hide; from the gift of the noblemen Otto and Frederick of Harbiche, one plot in Rodensleve; from the gift of the noblewoman Willa, one hide in the village called Memenich. In Lesser Rodensleve, one hide offered for Otto of Grinde; for Henry of Drenleve, half a hide in the village called Remkeleve. In Lesser Sigersleve, one hide bought for a price; in the village called Mammendorp, hides and one mill, purchased from Henry of Neyndorp; one woodland tract purchased from Rimo; from the gift of Gertrude of Amuordesleve, half a hide in Brandesleve; from the gift of the nobleman Hilbrand of Schusen, half a hide in Brandesleve; in the village [Col. 0913A] called Hogendorp, eight acres given by Adelrad for his father; in the city of Helmstedt, certain estates and plots acquired both by gift and purchase; in the city of Magdeburg, certain plots acquired both by gift and purchase. Indeed, let no one presume to demand or extort tithes from you on the produce of your own labor.

Therefore let no person at all be permitted to infringe this charter of our protection, confirmation, and constitution, or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the second day before the Kalends of February, in the first year of our pontificate.

### LV. He declares to the chapter of Genoa the authority granted by Archbishop Joscius of Tyre to establish a chapel in the city of Tyre. (Rome, St. Peter’s, February 1.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 877.]

[Col. 0913B]

To his beloved sons O., provost, and the whole chapter of Genoa, etc.

The most holy Roman Church regards devoted and humble sons, etc. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, . . . we confirm by apostolic authority the grant made by our venerable brother, the archbishop of Tyre, concerning the foundation of a chapel in the city of Tyre, as contained in his authentic instrument, etc.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the Kalends of February, in the first year [Col. 0913C] of our pontificate.

### LVI. He declares Ubaldo, archbishop of Pisa, primate of Sardinia. (Fragment.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 409.]

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, through the hand of Giles, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, on the Nones of February, indiction 10, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation.

### LVII. He receives the monastery of Goldbach under protection and confirms its goods and rights. (Rome, St. Peter’s, February 8.)

[SCHOEPFLIN, *Alsatia diplomatica*, I, 296.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 0913D] sons THEOBALD, provost of the church of St. Lawrence at Golpac, and his brethren, greeting and apostolic blessing.

A petition born of pious intention ought to be fulfilled by its effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth commendably and the requested benefit may assuredly gain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of St. Lawrence, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing. First, we decree that the canonical order known to have been established in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine shall be inviolably observed there for all time. [Col. 0914A] Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that church now possesses justly and canonically, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s assistance, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among them we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

In the valley of Golpa, the endowment of relics; in the same valley, tithes both from cultivation and from livestock; fields, meadows, and woods in that same valley. Whatever you hold in Hostheim, Ensiheschim, Bercholz, and Wathewilre; one vineyard at Senene. Whatever you hold in the valley of St. Amarin and in the village of Wilri; whatever you hold at Sulze; whatever you hold at Sulzemata and the exchange [*concambium*] which the monks of Crescent granted you there; whatever you hold at Regin; whatever you hold at Sarmenze. In the village of Gabulwire, the estate in which you live; the estate of Durrebach; two holdings granted to you by the sisters Adeledis and Mathildis; three mills in that village; vineyards, fields, and meadows; and twelve estates. One estate at Behele; whatever you hold at Markense and Ratresei. We likewise confirm the exchange between you and Bertolf, abbot of Marbach, concerning the place formerly called Heupech and now called Gophach, which the aforesaid abbot granted you in exchange for certain vineyards by the lime-kiln which you gave him.

You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen, free and unbound, fleeing the secular world, [Col. 0914C] and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your monastery, from being permitted to leave it, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one may dare retain one who departs without letters of guarantee from the community. When a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. Moreover, wishing with paternal care to provide henceforth for your peace and tranquility, we establish by apostolic authority that you shall not be obliged to receive any woman as a sister while she remains below the years of discretion. By apostolic authority [Col. 0914D] we also prohibit anyone from harassing you or your church with new and unlawful exactions. We further decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may obstruct the devotion and final wishes of those who determine to be buried there, unless perhaps they are excommunicated or under interdict—without prejudice, however, to the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. Upon the death of you, the present provost of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any deceitful contrivance or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the greater and sounder part of the brethren, shall judge fit to elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

Therefore let no person at all be permitted to infringe this charter [Col. 0915A] of our protection and constitution, or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the sixth day before the Ides of February, in the first year of our pontificate.

### LVIII. He grants the patriarch of Grado the tithes of the church of St. Archidian at Constantinople, and permits him to exercise conventual right in the chapels of that church. (Rome, St. Peter’s, February 11.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 1133.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother, the patriarch of Grado, greeting and apostolic [Col. 0915B] blessing.

Whenever our brethren and fellow bishops request from us something that does not depart from the path of reason, it is fitting for us readily to consent to their petition, so that they may apply themselves more steadfastly to the office entrusted to them and remain devoted to us, in proportion as they find themselves more graciously and speedily heard by us. Thus, since you state that you possess the church of St. Archidian at Constantinople, certain of your suffragans persistently demand tithes from the parishioners of that church who frequently transfer their households from your regions to the parish of those same suffragans. They do so on the ground that those parishioners’ fathers, grandfathers, or great-grandfathers once paid those tithes; and, in order to extort those tithes, they do not hesitate . . . . . to send [Col. 0915C] their vicars, without considering that, although those parishioners may once have been theirs, once they have transferred to another parish no one may put his hand into another’s harvest. Therefore, wishing carefully to provide for your indemnity, we grant you by the authority of this present document that you may freely receive and retain tithes from the parishioners of your aforesaid church of St. Archidian, notwithstanding that their forebears paid tithes to the aforesaid suffragans of yours while they remained in those suffragans’ parish. Likewise, you may exercise without anyone’s contradiction, by our authority, the conventual right which is legally yours in the chapels of the aforesaid church.

Therefore let no person at all be permitted to infringe this charter of our grant or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the third day before the Ides of February, in the year of our pontificate:

### LIX. He informs J[ohn], archbishop of Lyons, and his suffragans that he has granted the Cluniac monks “that, if bishops and prelates of churches, after being requested three times by the brethren, do not compel all their wrongdoers and the wrongdoers of their men who are from the province of Lyons to render them suitable satisfaction, it shall be lawful for them to subject such persons, with lighted candles, to sentence of excommunication and interdict.” (Rome, St. Peter’s, February 15.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, 94.]

[Col. 0916A]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brethren J., archbishop of Lyons, and his suffragans, and to his beloved sons, the abbots, deans, and other prelates of churches established throughout the province of Lyons, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although we are bound to foster and love all religious places, we ought nevertheless to devote more attentive care to those which stand under the jurisdiction of blessed Peter and, without any intermediary, belong to our provision and protection. Therefore, wishing to strengthen the monastery of Cluny against unlawful molestations by a special privilege of liberty, we have granted by apostolic authority to the brethren of that monastery that, if their bishops and prelates of churches, after being requested three times by the same brethren, do not compel all their wrongdoers and the wrongdoers of their men who are from the province of Lyons to render them suitable satisfaction, it shall be lawful for the brethren and their successors, with lighted candles, by apostolic authority to subject such persons to a sentence of excommunication and interdict. They shall declare them bound by the bond of excommunication and interdict until they have made adequate satisfaction for the offences committed; [Col. 0916C] and, if the character of the offence requires it, they shall come to the apostolic see to be absolved, bearing testimony in their letters.

Moreover, we have decreed that the liberties and immunities, and the reasonable customs hitherto observed, of that monastery are to remain valid; and we have confirmed them by apostolic authority to the brethren and their successors, strictly forbidding anyone to presume, without the knowledge of the apostolic see—to which it is specially subject—to alienate in any way the possessions, rights, or goods of that monastery, or to violate its ancient and reasonable customs hitherto observed. If anyone does attempt this, we decree that it shall be wholly void. [Col. 0916D] Furthermore, since, as we have heard, parishioners belonging either to those brethren or to their cells, who for manifest offences incur in any way a sentence of ecclesiastical discipline from the aforesaid brethren, sometimes transfer themselves elsewhere in order thus to evade the brethren’s sentence and justice, we strictly command and enjoin that, whenever you are requested, you shall cause those who have thus deemed ecclesiastical correction contemptible, and the other wrongdoers of the same brethren who have been bound by the bond of excommunication or interdict by you, by the brethren themselves, or by others, to be avoided by everyone throughout your parishes as excommunicated and interdicted persons, without regard to appeal, until those wrongdoers are compelled to make satisfaction. And, if [Col. 0917A] the character of the offence requires it, let them come to the apostolic see to be absolved with testimony in letters of the abbot or chapter. We also strictly forbid you to relax by your own authority any sentence passed by those brethren against wrongdoers of themselves or of their men.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the first year of our pontificate.

### LX. At the request of Bishop Bentivolus, he confirms the possessions of the Church of Gubbio. (Lateran, February 25.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, I, 641.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother BENTIVOLUS, bishop of Gubbio, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Whenever it is asked of us, etc., to grant, etc. Therefore, venerable brother bishop, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and, following the example of Alexander, Roman pontiff, our predecessor of happy memory, strengthen by the charter of this present writing the Church of Gubbio, over which by God’s authority you are known to preside, together with all that belongs to it. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, God being favorable, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among them we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The possession of Cerri and Cragnani; the church of St. Cyprian; the castle of Albaneti with its appurtenances; the castle of Anea with its appurtenances; the castle of St. Mary; the castle of Salicia; the castle on the Mount; two parts of the castle of Anagni; the castle of the hill of Casale; the castle of Tertiani; the castle of Ildebrand’s Castiglione; the castle of Martiaula’s Castiglione; the castle of Carbonana; the fortified place beyond Serra; the fortified place of Sasallera; the castle of Burani, one half together with the adjoining public lands; the castle of Arsenii, the portion given to the bishopric by Theobald together with half of all his possessions; the fortified place of Albaneti; the fortified place of Majula; the fortified place of Seuctiani; [Col. 0917D] the portion with the village of Decimi; the fortified place of Scattioli and the church of St. Clement with its appurtenances, one half; the fortified places of Monte Calvo; the fortified place of Agellionis; the estate of Campelliones; the church of St. Donatus with its appurtenances; the canonry of St. Secundus, situated near the said city, with all its appurtenances; the church of St. Lawrence and the church of St. Martin with all their appurtenances; the land of St. Marianus, held by the sons of Carbo; and the church of St. Mary at Merta with its appurtenances. Furthermore, let it be your concern to distribute firstfruits, tithes, and offerings, both of the living and of the dead, according to canonical ordinances.

Therefore we decree, etc.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0918A] I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Pandulphus, cardinal priest of the Basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title . . . . par . . . . I, Romanus, cardinal priest of the title of St. Anastasia. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Coelian Hill. I, Gratianus, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St. Adrian. I, Rofredus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary Inviolata. I, John, cardinal deacon of St. Theodore. I, Bernard, cardinal deacon of St. Mary the New. I, Lothair, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 0918B] I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Cosmedin.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Giles, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in Carcere Tulliano, on the fifth day before the Kalends of March, indiction 10, in the year 1191 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Celestine III.

### LXI. He confirms certain churches to the monastery of Cluny. (Lateran, February 27.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, p. 94.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and monks of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily assent to the pious desires of petitioners and bring to effect the vows which do not depart from the straight path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, favorably assenting to your just petitions, we confirm to you, and through you to your monastery, by apostolic authority, the church of St. Mary of Mont-Meruti near Belleville de Sollenat, the churches of St. Desiderius in the archbishopric of Lyons, and the church of Hermes in the bishopric of Belley, just as you possess them lawfully and peaceably.

Let no person at all be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 0918D] Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Kalends of March, in the first year of our pontificate.

### LXII. To [Bentivolus], bishop, and the clergy and people of Gubbio—On the canonization of St. Ubaldus. (Lateran, March 4.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXII, 596.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother B., bishop, and to his beloved sons B., prior, and the clergy and people of Gubbio, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Blessed is God in His gifts, and holy in all His works. According to the multitude of His mercies, He grants to those who were by nature children of wrath the spirit of adoption, in which we cry, “Abba, Father”; and in His goodness He assumes men formed of clay into the fellowship of angels and glory. So it came to pass in our own time with Ubaldus, your bishop of holy memory. Though, while he lived in the flesh, he was deemed pious and just, after his passing he deserved to be regarded as a saint by those near and far, because of the miracles which God worked through his merits. In him was fulfilled what the Prophet said in the Psalm: “Sons are born to you in place of your fathers; you shall make them princes over all the earth. They shall remember your name, O Lord” (Psalm 44). But you, brother bishop, being present at the apostolic see, persisted humbly, as was fitting, both opportunely and importunately, asking [Col. 0919B] that we should canonize the memory of the aforesaid bishop and inscribe him in the catalogue of saints by apostolic authority, in view of his religious life and the many miracles which, after he departed from this world, the Almighty has deigned to work through him. Yet, perceiving that this matter exceeds our understanding and intelligence, because it pertains rather to divine judgment than human judgment, since He alone fully knows those who are His, we suspended your request for some time, so that the grace of the Holy Spirit might reveal to us and to our brethren what ought rather to be done. Finally, induced by your devout supplication and moved by the testimonies of many bishops and others, trusting chiefly not in our own merits but in the mercy [Col. 0919C] of the Creator, with the common counsel of the brethren we have assented to your desires. Canonizing the aforesaid saint by the authority of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul, which we exercise though unworthy, we decree that the feast of his death shall be perpetually observed among you as that of a most blessed confessor.

Therefore we admonish and exhort you all in the Lord not to receive this grace in vain, but to be renewed in the spirit of your mind after the example of the blessed man; to be more fervent than usual in reverence toward God, the aforesaid saint, and all the other saints; and diligently to ensure that his feast be celebrated joyfully every year on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of June, so that [read: *ita quod*, “so that”] your devotion to divine worship may deservedly seem to have increased, others may indeed take an example from your conduct, and he, moved by your prayers, may intercede with Almighty God for the state of the whole Church.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Nones of March, in the first year of our pontificate.

### LXIII. He receives the Church of Scala under protection and confirms its goods. (Lateran, March 13.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, VII, 328.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother ALEXANDER, bishop of Scala, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Set, by the Lord’s disposition, on the watchtower of the apostolic see, we ought to love our brother bishops, whether near or far, with steadfast charity and to grant prompt effect to their petitions. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, assenting to your prayers, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the Church of Scala, over which you are known to preside by God’s authority, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that Church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, with God’s help, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among them we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 0920B] Greater Scala with its appurtenances as far as the river which separates Scala from Ravello; on the northern side, as far as the marsh of Cicini, and thence to St. Angelus of Petralene, where the boundary between Scala and Ravello lies; on the western side, the whole mountain of Candirecti as far as Pietra Palumbara, as it runs along the plain; and Mount Cerbellani with its appurtenances. The church of St. Julian with its appurtenances as far as Lactaria; from the south, from Planello, which lies below St. Helena, as far as the river of Camneti, and along Tabernata, Mount Scanni, and the arch of Patalarum, returning to the same Cerbellani; whatever you hold in the city of Amalfi; the church of St. Barbara with its dependent chapels and all its appurtenances; two shops and another cell [Col. 0920C] with its appurtenances. Upon the death of you, the present bishop of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be elected bishop of that Church except one whom the canons of that Church, or their sounder part, shall judge fit to elect according to God.

Therefore we decree that no person at all may rashly disturb the aforesaid church; take away, retain, diminish, or harass with any vexations its possessions; but that all things shall be preserved whole and undiminished for you and your successors, for whose governance and support they have been granted for their beneficial use, without prejudice to the authority of the apostolic see and the due reverence owed to your metropolitan. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, attempts rashly to act against it, after a second and third warning, unless he makes amends for his offence by due satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and let him be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 0921A] I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Tusculum. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of Saint Adrian. I, Sifred, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, John, deacon-cardinal of Saint Theodore. I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saint Mary in Aquiro.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Moses, subdeacon of the Holy Roman Church and canon of the Lateran, on the third Ides of March, indiction 10, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 0921B] 1191, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Celestine III.

LXIV. To William, king of the Scots.—He confirms the liberties of the Scottish Church. (Lateran, March 13.)

[MANSI, Councils, XXII, 613.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest son in Christ WILLIAM, illustrious king of the Scots, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although all who are subject to Christ’s yoke ought to find protection and favour at the Apostolic See, it is especially fitting that those whose faith and devotion it has often [Col. 0921C] experienced should be cherished under the safeguard of advancement; so that they may be drawn all the more fully to the favour of its love, and submit themselves with more devoted affection to its reverence, in proportion as they know that they have more certainly obtained a pledge of its goodwill and grace.
