On the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any trickery of surreptitious procurement [Col. 1057C] or by violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or that part of the brethren of sounder counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. Desiring also to provide henceforth with paternal solicitude for your peace and tranquility, we forbid by apostolic authority, under threat of anathema, anyone within the enclosures of your places to commit robbery or theft, set fire, seize or kill persons, or dare perpetrate any violence.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain property taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, [Col. 1057D] let all things remain intact for the use and benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support they were granted by pious generosity, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. As a sign of this liberty received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay to us and our successors one gold coin every year. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowingly acting against this charter of our enactment, should rashly attempt to violate it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his office and honor; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer [Col. 1058A]; and at the Last Judgment let him be subject to strict vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good action and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Cecilia. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Viterbo and Tusculum. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Martin at Equitius. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill [Col. 1058B]. I, Soffredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of Saint Peter in Chains, of the title of Eudoxia. I, Fidantius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, John, cardinal priest of the church of Saint Prisca. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Saint Rufina. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of [Col. 1058C] Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of December, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1194, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

## CLXXI. He commands the bishop of Lincoln not to obstruct the monks of Saint Neot in their possession of the churches of Esnebiria and Torneia.  
*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, November 19.)*

*[Monasticon Anglicanum, I, 370.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop of Lincoln: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The most holy Roman Church has customarily loved its devout and humble [Col. 1058D] sons more ardently, in accordance with the duty of its customary compassion; and, lest they be troubled by the unlawful oppressions of wicked men, it is accustomed, like a loving mother, to cherish them with the protection of its defense. Therefore, since we are bound to grant apostolic protection to each person who cries out to us, out of regard for pity and mercy we confirm by the present charter to the prior and convent of Saint Neot the churches of Esnebiria and Torneia, from which they have already received an annual pension. For the aforesaid prior and convent, being situated upon a route of travel and a much-frequented road, provide food and drink, for the mercy of God, to all passers-by who ask for them; and they declare that they spend the income of the aforesaid churches upon the needs of guests.

[Col. 1059A] Therefore, by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood that, for reverence toward the blessed apostles Peter and Paul and toward us, you shall permit the aforesaid prior and convent to possess the said churches in peace, as they possess them justly and reasonably and are secured by the testimony of the present charter; setting aside appeal and notwithstanding any letters to the contrary, you shall defend them—fortified by the authority of blessed Peter and by ours—from the insolence of deans, archdeacons, and all officials of men. If anyone should presume to oppose such confirmation and the aforesaid prior and convent in this matter, you shall publicly declare him excommunicated by our authority.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends [Col. 1059B] of December, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

## CLXXII. He receives under protection the Scottish monastery of Saint James at Regensburg and confirms its possessions and rights.  
*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, November 22.)*

*[RIED, Codex diplomaticus Ratisponensis, I, 279.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PATRICK, abbot of the monastery of Blessed James at Regensburg, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

(The remainder of the text agrees word for word with the protection charter granted to the same monastery by Pope Lucius III on 10 April 1185. See *Patrologia*, vol. CCI.)

[Col. 1059C] I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church.

There follows the subscription of sixteen cardinals.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, on the tenth day before the Kalends of December, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1194, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

Lead seal: **CELESTINE POPE III.**

## CLXXIII. He commands the bishop of Foropopoli to ensure that the church of Saint Mary of the Port remains in possession of the church of Saint John in Marmorato, donated by the canons of Ravenna.  
*(Lateran, December 10.)*

*[FANTUZZI, Monumenti Ravennati, vol. VI, p. 58.]*

[Col. 1059D]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop of Foropopoli: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Appearing in our presence, the beloved son G . . . . , prior of the Church of Saint Mary of the Port, showed us by his statement that, when the beloved sons . . . . . . . . , archdeacon of the church of Ravenna, and his brethren had granted to him and to the church of the Port, with the archbishop’s consent, the church of Saint John in Marmorato together with its appurtenances, and had accordingly drawn up a public instrument, the priests and parishioners of that church, seeking to evade the donation, have not ceased to trouble that prior and his church concerning it. Therefore [Col. 1060A] by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood that, if what is alleged is true, you shall urgently admonish the said disturbers and induce them wholly to desist from troubling the prior and the church of the Port; otherwise, setting aside appeal, you shall compel them to do so by ecclesiastical censure, as shall be just.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Ides of December, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

## CLXXIV. He takes the church of Saint Reparata at Lucca under protection and confirms its goods and privileges.  
*(Lateran, December 17.)*

*[MURATORI, Antiquitates Italicae, VI, 443.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MARTIN, prior of the church of Saint Reparata, [Col. 1060B] and his brethren, present and future, to be canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

A petition of pious intent ought to be fulfilled in its effect, so that the sincerity of devotion may shine forth praiseworthily and the requested advantage may undoubtedly gain force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and, following in the footsteps of our predecessors of faithful memory—Eugenius, Anastasius, Adrian, Alexander, Urban, and Clement, Roman pontiffs—we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Saint Reparata, which in the city of Lucca bears the designation of a *plebs* church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of the present document. We decree that whatever [Col. 1060C] possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s aid, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

We confirm to you by authority of the Apostolic See every right you possess in the church of Saint Cassian and in the church of Saint Justus at the Arch; likewise your whole parish, parishioners, and tithes which you hold justly. Furthermore, we confirm to you every right which you possess in the church of Saint Lawrence of Picciorano [Col. 1060D], as it is known to have been adjudged to you by the judgment of Roland, provost of Saint George, and Guy, prior of Saint Donatus, judges delegated by the Apostolic See; as is contained in their authentic written instrument; and as you possess it without dispute. We likewise confirm the celebration of the high Mass on the feast of Saint Lawrence, and the other things which you have hitherto reasonably held in the aforesaid church. We also prohibit anyone from imposing penances upon your parishioners without consulting you, unless they are perhaps in such urgent necessity that they cannot have recourse to you. Nor may anyone receive any of your parishioners for burial unless the canonical right of your church is preserved. Neither the bishop [Col. 1061A] nor anyone else may introduce into that church, against your will, new and less canonical customs or impose unlawful exactions. We likewise confirm to you and, through you, to your church the baptismal rite which the bishop and canons of Saint Martin customarily perform in your church on Holy Saturday, as well as the ancient processions and stations and the high Masses which those canons customarily celebrate in that same church on appointed days. Furthermore, if the chaplains of your city whom you summon to baptize children at the solemn baptism should, as has hitherto been observed, refuse to come through obstinacy, they shall be compelled by your bishop through ecclesiastical censure, without impediment of appeal. We decree [Col. 1061B] that on those Sundays and principal feasts on which the canons of the principal church customarily come in procession to the aforesaid church, if perhaps led by some abuse or malice they refuse to come to that place as ancient custom requires, you yourselves shall solemnly celebrate by apostolic authority the high Masses, Vespers, and the other divine offices which they ought to have celebrated.

Moreover, you may receive as brethren, without anyone’s contradiction and with the consent of your bishop, learned and honorable clerics, from wherever they may come, provided that, if unknown, they bring letters of recommendation from their bishops. But if the bishop himself should maliciously oppose you and refuse to allege a reasonable ground, you may nevertheless receive those clerics [Col. 1061C]. We further add that neither the bishop nor the canons may subject your place or clerics dwelling there to interdict or excommunication without reasonable and manifest cause. We also decree that burial in your church shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the right of the mother church is nevertheless preserved. On the death of you, the present prior of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any trickery of surreptitious procurement or by violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the greater part of the brethren by sounder counsel, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God [Col. 1061D]. The person elected shall then, in the customary manner, be presented to the bishop and canons of the principal church for confirmation.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, etc.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, etc.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, [Col. 1062A] on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1194, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

The lead seal is missing.

## CLXXV. He receives the monastery of Saint Prosper of Reggio under the protection of the Holy Roman Church and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(Lateran, December 24.)*

*[MARGARINI, Bullarium Casinense, II, 223.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the brethren of the monastery of Saint Prosper situated below the city of Reggio, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1062B] Whenever a request is made of us that is recognized as fitting religion and uprightness, it becomes us to grant it willingly and to furnish appropriate support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint Prosper, which is known to belong to the Roman Church and in which you are devoted to divine service, following the example of our predecessor Alexander of happy memory; and we strengthen it by the privilege of the present document. First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in the same monastery according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. [Col. 1062C] Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through grants of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, through the Lord’s aid, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its tenements and appurtenances and with its cemetery; nine *iugera* of land with the chapel of Saint Nazarius, which the abbot then in office received from the above-mentioned church of Saint Prosper, situated within the castle of that city [Col. 1062D], through a lawfully concluded exchange; and all the land at Corticella surrounding that monastery, which has been given to the said monastery by bishops, canons, or any of the faithful. Further, twelve holdings at Fossulae, four at Palude, four at Campagnola, three at Quingenta, one at Curte Nova, one at Gurgo, one at Fossudunde, five at Bagnolo, and the chapel of Saint Mustiola with its appurtenances; one holding at Crustulo Vetere; one in the village of Sbragato; one at Magno Casale, and the chapel of Saint Sylvester, with the demesne of that same village of Magno Casale; three holdings in Reggio and the duchy of Reggio; the king’s *braida* [enclosed estate] and all the land of the aforesaid monastery situated around that city; [Col. 1063A] three holdings at Rodano, three at Marmirolo, one at Aliano, one at Bibiano, one at Riano, one at Mulazano, one at Planzo, one in the castle of Oleriani, and the estate of Vasseto with Lama Fraularia, a field, and the stream of Vasseto, which are known to have been granted to the Church of Reggio by charter of the most pious King Charles, according to the boundaries there designated; and the land given by Roland, son of Eribert. At Motilena, four holdings with a chapel and a certain part of the castle. At Albinea, four holdings and the chapel of Saint Mary at Pisignam with the adjoining Oliveto. At Vergniano, two holdings, and eight holdings given by Adicio, son of Atho, son of Gandulf; and the chapel of Saint Dalmatius at Medule, given by Count Albert [Col. 1063B] with all its appurtenances. At Speciano, one holding; one at Floriano; one on Mount Baranzonis; a certain share in the chapel of Saint Martin at Revere; two shares in the church of Saint Mary; one in Saint Florentinus; one in Saint Lawrence; two holdings at Pulianello; and whatever it justly possesses, or ought by right to possess, within the Italian kingdom.

Moreover, let no one presume to demand or exact tithes from you on your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. You may also receive into conversion in your monastery clerics or [Col. 1063C] laymen, free and released from secular life, and retain them without any contradiction. Furthermore, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in the same monastery, from leaving that place unless for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one may dare retain a departing brother without an assurance in letters from the community. On the death of the abbot then in office, or of any of his successors, no one shall be set over it by any trickery of surreptitious procurement or by violence, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the greater part of the brethren by sounder counsel, shall provide to be elected according to God and the Rule of Saint Benedict. Also, out of reverence for Saint Prosper, confessor of the Lord, we decree by the present authority that the abbot and brethren of that monastery whom [Col. 1063D] the same abbot appoints, provided that they exercise the office of priest, may solemnly celebrate the solemnities of Mass upon his sacred relics for people from everywhere who visit the thresholds of that most holy confessor, or for inhabitants of his territory who assemble at the same church; may suitably refresh them with the bread of God’s word; and may make them participants, for a period, in your prayers and in the other good works continually performed in that monastery. We also command that no bishop of that city, nor indeed any primate or metropolitan, nor any great or small ecclesiastical or secular person, may dare overturn any of the things set forth above; celebrate public Masses there upon any pretext; perform any ordination, however slight, [Col. 1064A] without the consent of the abbot and brethren; pronounce excommunication against them; or oppose any office. Nor may anyone presume to exercise any power or jurisdiction against that venerable monastery. Furthermore, we decree that burial in that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken are nevertheless preserved.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain property taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; rather, [Col. 1064B] let all things remain intact for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See. As a sign of this liberty received from the Apostolic See, you shall pay one Byzantine coin every year to us and our successors. If, therefore, in the future, etc.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Peter, bishop of Porto, of the title of Saint Rufina. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. [Col. 1064C] I, Frederick, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Angel. I, B., cardinal deacon of the title of Saint Theodore. I, Peter, of the title of Saint Mary in Via Lata.

Given at the Lateran through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, on the ninth day before the Kalends of January, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1194, in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

## CLXXVI. He replies to Gilbert, bishop of Clermont, that “an interdict imposed upon a church by one or more of its canons without his consent ought in no way to be observed.”

*(Augustine of Tarragona, Works, IV, 387.)*

[Col. 1064D]

## THE YEAR 1195

## CLXXVII. He permits Bernard, bishop of Faenza, to restore the monastery of Gamundio, subjected on his order by its prior to the monastery of Acereta, to its former condition.  
*(Lateran, January 3.)*

*[TONDUZZI, History of Faenza, p. 230.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 1065A] brother BERNARD, bishop of Faenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Just as the union of bishoprics and their subjection to another’s authority is recognized as belonging to the supreme pontiff, so the union and subjection of churches in their own diocese concerns bishops. Therefore, since, as has become known to us, the prior of Gamundio subjected or united his monastery, which is in your diocese and ought to be regulated with your consent, to the monastery of Acereta without seeking your consent, we grant your brotherhood by the present charter that you may, by apostolic authority, annul as justice requires what he has done in this matter without consulting you. The consent or confirmation which the metropolitan may have given shall not stand in the way, since he ought not to attempt anything of this sort, contrary to canonical enactments, within the diocese of his suffragan [Col. 1065B] without that suffragan’s consent. We also decree that this act, as stated above, is to be annulled, establishing that no person whatsoever may, etc. But if anyone, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the third day before the Nones of January, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

## CLXXVIII. He confirms certain possessions of the canons of Maurienne.  
*(Rome, at Saint Peter’s, January 6.)*

*[CIBRARIO and PROMIS, Documents, p. 103.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of the principal church of Maurienne: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1065C] It is fitting that we readily grant consent to the just wishes of petitioners and bring to effect the requests that do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, concurring favorably in your just requests, we confirm to you and, through you, to your church by apostolic authority the possessions which the nobleman Thomas, count of Maurienne, and his predecessors are known to have bestowed upon you and your church, as you possess them justly and without dispute; and we strengthen them by the protection of the present document. Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation [Col. 1065D] of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the eighth day before the Ides of January, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

## CLXXIX. He confirms the agreement made between the abbot of Saint Benedict at Piacenza and Martin, abbot of Saint Mary of Vallombrosa, concerning the right and establishment of the monastery of Saint James at Turin.  
*(Lateran, January 21.)*

*[LAMI, Deliciae eruditorum, 1737, p. 226.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Saint Benedict at Piacenza: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily [Col. 1066A] grant consent to the just wishes of petitioners and bring to effect the requests that do not depart from the path of reason. Since a controversy had arisen between you, son abbot, on behalf of your monastery, and our beloved son Martin, abbot of Saint Mary of Vallombrosa, concerning the right and establishment of the monastery of Saint James at Turin, that dispute was at length settled by an amicable agreement; the terms of that agreement are more fully set out in the public instrument made concerning it. Therefore, in order that the agreement may henceforth be observed unshaken and not be broken by anyone’s malice, we confirm it by apostolic authority and strengthen it by the protection of the present document, as it was prudently and without abuse made, received, and hitherto observed, and as it is fully contained in that same instrument.

[Col. 1066B] Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation and enactment or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

## CLXXX. He commands the bishop of Castello (Venice) to grant the church of Saint Bartholomew to the canons of Saint Saviour.  
*(Lateran, January 27.)*

*[CORNELII, Churches of Venice, XIV, 121.]*

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 1066C] brother the bishop of Castello: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The care of the office entrusted to us and the obligation of charity urge us to provide for peace and tranquility in religious places and to preserve their rights intact. Since, therefore, scandal has sometimes arisen between the beloved sons . . . . , prior and canons of Saint Saviour at Rialto, and . . . . , parish priest of Saint Bartholomew, because the neighbors of the aforesaid church of Saint Saviour and of the church of Saint Bartholomew render parochial dues, the said canons long ago obtained letters from you or your predecessor so that they might obtain that church by episcopal generosity, with all the rights of the church of Castello preserved. Since this [Col. 1066D] has not been carried out until now, and since we have hope in your devotion that you would willingly promote the advantage of those brethren even without our speaking, we exhort your brotherhood in the Lord and command by apostolic letters that, out of regard for God and reverence for blessed Peter and ourselves, you shall grant the aforesaid church of Saint Bartholomew, by pious generosity, to the said canons for peaceful possession, saving to you and your successors episcopal right and the other dues which you customarily receive from it. Thus those canons may be more devoted to you on that account, and we may commend your devotion in the Lord for divine works.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Kalends of February, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

## CLXXXI. He grants Peter, archbishop of Compostela, that “since human law provides that no prescription has force in tribute and public obligations, and since the offerings which King Ramiro ordained to be paid every year to God and Blessed James in Spain are like tributes, no prescription alleged against them shall have force or validity.”  
*(Lateran, January 31.)*

*[FERRER, History of the Apostle of Jesus Christ Saint James, Madrid, 1610, folio, p. 279b.]*

[Col. 1067A]

## CLXXXII. He grants the chapter of Bremen authority to deprive beneficiary brethren of their benefices if they do not pay the dues owed to the chapter at the appointed time.  
*(Lateran, February 8.)*

*[LAPPENBERG, Hamburg Documents, I, 266.]*

[Col. 1067B]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons F[REDERICK], provost major, R[UDOLF], dean, and the chapter of Bremen: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Know that it has come to our hearing that certain among you sometimes withhold the dues owed for the brethren’s stipends, and sometimes delay their payment too long, failing to supply them at the proper time. As a result, the brethren are often given occasion to complain, to withdraw themselves from divine service, and even to resist the discipline of their superiors when they are rebuked for lukewarmness, negligence, or other offenses. Therefore, that the presumption of such persons [Col. 1067C] may be corrected in due fashion, we have thought fit by this present charter to grant you that, if in future any persons maliciously withhold beyond the fixed term a payment or due owed toward the common stipends, and after three warnings fail to correct this at your command, you shall have free authority by apostolic power, without impediment of appeal, to take away from them, by common counsel or by that of the greater and sounder part, the benefices from which those dues ought to be paid.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of February, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

## CLXXXIII. He commands [Hermann], bishop of Münster, and [Gerhard], bishop of Osnabrück, to anathematize certain ministerials of the Church of Bremen if they do not restore goods unjustly taken from that church.  
*(Lateran, February.)*

*[Ibid.]*

[Col. 1067D]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren, the bishops of Münster and Osnabrück, and to his beloved son, the abbot of Raderstad: greeting and apostolic blessing.

As has been represented to our hearing, the beloved sons Alard, Henry, Otto, and Frederick, ministerials of the Church of Bremen, do not hesitate, at peril to their souls, to retain very many revenues and other goods belonging to that Church and to our venerable brother Hartwig, its archbishop [Col. 1068A]. In retaining them, they offend their Creator all the more because they are more able to assist those persons advantageously and are more bound to furnish them stronger aid and protection against the violence of any persons whatsoever. Therefore, we have commanded them and strictly enjoined them under threat of anathema to restore without delay or difficulty those revenues and goods to the same archbishop and his church, and to permit them to receive and hold them without disturbance. Accordingly, by apostolic letters we command and strictly enjoin your discretion that, if these aforementioned ministerials delay or neglect to fulfill our command, you shall proceed to the city of Bremen and, notwithstanding any contradiction or appeal, shall not delay binding them with the bond of anathema [Col. 1068B] and subjecting their lands to interdict. By our authority you shall publicly announce, and cause to be announced, that both sentences are to be observed inviolably until suitable satisfaction is made; you shall inflict the due penalty upon any who rashly presume to violate either sentence. No letters shall stand in the way, if any should appear to have been obtained from the Apostolic See without mention of these matters. If all of you cannot be present to carry this out, nevertheless let two of you execute it.

Given at the Lateran, 10 February, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CLXXXIV. He grants the chapter of Bremen that the security concerning indemnity of the church, furnished by Archbishop Hartwig “at the time of the settlement,” shall remain inviolate. (Lateran, 15 February.)

[Ibid., p. 267.]

[Col. 1068C]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Frederick, provost major, Rudolf, dean, and the chapter of Bremen: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant consent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to effect, by the ensuing accomplishment, requests which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, gladly concurring in your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority, and fortify with the protection of this present writing, the security which our venerable brother Hartwig, archbishop of your church, furnished concerning the indemnity of that church at the time of the settlement concluded between himself and you; and, since it was made and received prudently and without impropriety, it ought to remain unshaken. Let no person therefore whatsoever be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CLXXXV. He confirms to the church of St Donatian at Bruges the legacy established in the will of Margaret, formerly countess of Flanders. (Lateran, 15 February.)

[Miraeus, *Opera diplomatica*, II, 1331.]

[Col. 1069A]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Gerard and the canons of St Donatian of Bruges: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When what is just and honorable is requested of us, both the force of equity and the order of reason require that it be brought to its due effect through the diligence of our office. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority, and fortify with the protection of this present writing, for you and your church, one hundred solidi which Margaret, formerly countess of Flanders, bequeathed in her will to your church for distribution on the day of her anniversary; together with fifteen pounds to be assigned, without any diminution, to the daily distribution among the canons; and thirty pounds for the support of three prebends, which are to be conferred in your church only upon priests serving there continually—as you possess these things justly and peacefully.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may infringe this charter of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CLXXXVI. At the request of Sifred, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes, he grants privileges concerning the church of St Praxedes. (Lateran, 28 February.)

[Lami, *Deliciae eruditorum*, 1737, p. 227.]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Sifred, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes: greeting and apostolic blessing.

By reason of the office of the apostolate entrusted to us, although unworthy, we are bound to exercise care for all churches. Yet we are especially obliged to extend the eyes of paternal provision toward those which, being situated in the city, are known to pertain more particularly to us and, as is fitting, look to no other for the provision of our care and concern, while by a certain special prerogative they have awaited, and await, the aid of favorable support.

Accordingly, since the church of St Praxedes had formerly been entrusted by our predecessor Anastasius, of good memory, to the prior and brethren of St Mary of the Rhine, to be ordered and governed by them so that canonical order might be preserved therein inviolate for all time; and since in the end religious fervor there had declined, while usurious debts had grown enormously through the wrong done by the brethren who served there, you have repeatedly and urgently requested us to apply paternal concern to repairing that church and to provide more cautiously, lest, brought to complete destitution, it should be compelled to await every kind of ruin.

[Col. 1069D–1070A]

Therefore, yielding as we ought to your most urgent petitions, we sent our brethren down to the aforesaid church. Having recognized that it was necessary to act against the excessive decline from which it was said to suffer, we warned by our letters the aforesaid prior and brethren of St Mary of the Rhine to appear before us and answer concerning the matters stated above. Since, after being awaited for about a year, they took no care to apply any remedy of correction to the enormities committed by their people, we—unwilling, as indeed we ought not, that the often-mentioned church should utterly fail, exhausted both spiritually and temporally—by the common counsel of all our brethren withdrew it from every care, ordering, subjection, and obedience owed to the oft-mentioned brethren and to the church of St Mary of the Rhine.

We decree that both the privileges and all writings concerning that church of St Praxedes, granted to those brethren by the Roman Church, and every arrangement made therein, shall henceforth be wholly devoid of legal force. By apostolic authority we grant that church freely to you and your successors, with power to dispose and order it in temporal as well as spiritual matters.

We decree, therefore, that no person may infringe this charter of our constitution and grant or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, the second day before the Kalends of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CLXXXVII. He writes to [Adolf], archbishop, and to the dean of the cathedral church and the provost of St Andrew at Cologne concerning the dispute between Adolf, count of Schauenburg, and Hartwig, archbishop of Hamburg. One of them, having seized the castle of Stade and the county of Stade, had constructed the castle of Harburg to the great detriment of the church of Hamburg; the other is said earlier to have invaded the territories of the count while the latter was travelling to Jerusalem. The bishops of Münster and Osnabrück have been ordered to excommunicate the count unless he makes good the damages inflicted upon the archbishop. If they do not obey this command, the recipients are to declare both the count excommunicated and the bishops removed from their offices. (Lateran, 3 March.)

[Lappenberg, *Hamburgische Urkunden*, I, 268.]

[Col. 1070D]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the archbishop, and to his beloved sons, the dean of the greater church and the provost of St Andrew at Cologne: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When our beloved sons R[udolf], dean, and B[urchard], canon of the church of Bremen, came to the apostolic see, they presented to us letters of that church and of our venerable brother H., its archbishop. These set forth the many grievances which the nobleman Adolf, count of Schauenburg (so written), had violently inflicted upon them.

For, as they indicated both by their own assertion and by the contents of the letters they brought, that count unjustly held for some time, and still persists in holding unlawfully, at peril to his own salvation, a certain castle of that archbishop and his church, named Stade, together with the county of Stade. He also built a new castle upon property of that church, near the place called Horebruch, to the great injury of the same church, while the archbishop’s and the church’s envoys were being sent to the apostolic see concerning the injuries which the said count continually inflicted upon them. Furthermore, the count frequently forbids the archbishop’s clerics to attend his synod, does not permit his ministerials to render their due service to him, and does not fear to inflict many other injuries upon him and his church.

On behalf of the aforesaid count, however, our beloved son Master Bruno appeared in opposition to the said dean and his companion, having been sent to our hearing in the count’s name with his letters. He asserted that, while the count was on pilgrimage to Jerusalem, the archbishop invaded his lands and inflicted serious damages upon him and his men. For this reason, after his return the count brought a case concerning these matters before our beloved son Cencio, cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina, then legate of the apostolic see, as he was returning from the regions of Denmark. Cencio delegated judges to both parties. When the archbishop had been summoned by them, he promised that he would make a settlement with the count and would give him appropriate satisfaction in all these matters. Thus, while making such promises, he neither appeared before their tribunal nor took any care whatsoever to fulfil what he had promised.

Moreover, when the often-mentioned archbishop wished to summon that same count in certain other disputes and intended to subject him to excommunication, the count, regarding him as suspect in such a matter, appealed to the apostolic see and fixed the feast of the blessed apostle Thomas most recently past as the term for his appeal. In pursuit of that appeal he took care to send the aforesaid envoy to us.

Since, however, we must regard the grievances of that archbishop and his church, by which they are continually oppressed, as our own, we strictly commanded the aforesaid count, under threat of divine judgment, to restore without difficulty or delay all the things which he is alleged to hold to the prejudice of that archbishop and his church, insofar as these belong to them by right; to make suitable satisfaction for the damages and injuries inflicted; and henceforth to desist altogether from burdening or harassing them.

Once restitution has been made and suitable satisfaction, as stated, rendered for the injuries and damages inflicted by him upon that archbishop and the church entrusted to him, should the count think fit to bring any claim against the archbishop or his church concerning the aforementioned articles or other matters, he shall bring it before our venerable brethren the bishops of Münster and Osnabrück and our beloved son, the abbot of Hersuithehusen, according to the form of law.

For we have strictly commanded these judges, under obedience, that if the aforesaid count neglects to fulfil our command, they shall proceed together to the city of Bremen and, notwithstanding any contradiction or appeal, bind the count and his supporters in this presumption with the bond of excommunication, and subject the whole land under his power to ecclesiastical interdict. They shall publicly announce, and cause to be announced, each sentence on every Sunday and feast day, to be inviolably observed until he humbly submits to the command of the aforesaid archbishop and his church, fulfils all the aforesaid requirements, and furnishes firm security that he will not grievously burden the archbishop and his church in these or other matters.

But if the aforesaid count, after full restitution has been made and suitable satisfaction rendered for the inflicted injuries and damages, wishes to bring any claim against the archbishop and his church, they shall hear the case and decide it with justice as their guide, causing by our authority, through ecclesiastical censure, whatever they decree to be inviolably observed.

Therefore, by these apostolic writings, we command and strictly direct your discretion that, if the mentioned judges should prove lukewarm or remiss in carrying these matters out—which we do not believe—you shall, setting aside every contradiction and appeal, take care to execute what we have stated. And if the said judges do not come to the Roman Church by the forthcoming feast of St Michael in September, in order to make satisfaction for their contempt of the apostolic command, you shall suspend them from their offices by apostolic authority, notwithstanding any letters which may appear to have been obtained from the apostolic see without mention of these letters. If all of you cannot be present for carrying these matters out, nevertheless let two of you carry them out.

Given at the Lateran, the fifth day before the Nones of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CLXXXVIII. He confirms the chapel of Ceidlarn to the monastery of Raitenhaslach. (Lateran, the Ides of March.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, VI, 360.]

[Col. 1072D]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Ricceric, abbot, and the convent of Reidenhasla: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The most holy Roman Church is accustomed, by the office of its habitual compassion, to love more earnestly devoted and humble sons, and, lest they be troubled by the vexations of wicked men, to cherish them, like a loving mother, beneath the safeguard of its protection. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, considering the devotion which you are known to have toward blessed Peter and ourselves, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own protection your persons and monastery, together with all that you now reasonably possess or may, God favoring, acquire in the future by just means.

In particular, we confirm for you and, through you, for your monastery, and fortify with the protection of this present writing, the chapel of Cidelare with all its appurtenances, as our beloved son Frederick, advocate of Berge, is known to have granted it with the assent and will of our venerable brother Albert, archbishop of Salzburg, and as you possess it justly and without dispute. We further establish that, should you find yourselves oppressed in any matter, you may appeal to the apostolic see.

Let no person whatsoever therefore be permitted rashly to disturb your persons or the monastery entrusted to you, or to infringe this charter of our protection and confirmation, or rashly oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of March, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CLXXXIX. He takes under protection the monastery of St Zeno of Reichenhall and confirms its possessions and rights. (Lateran, 16 March.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, III, 552.]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Wichmann, provost of the church of St Zeno at Hall, and his brethren, present and future, professing the religious life, in perpetuity.

Whenever something is requested of us which is recognized as suitable to religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford appropriate support to the desires of petitioners. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of St Zeno, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it with the privilege of this present writing; first establishing, indeed, that, etc. Moreover, whatever possessions, etc.

Concerning, moreover, your newly cultivated lands, etc.

It shall also be lawful for you to receive for conversion clerics and laypeople, free and absolved persons fleeing the world, and to retain them without any contradiction.

[Col. 1073D]

Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your church, from leaving that place without the permission of his provost, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one shall dare retain a departing brother without letters of authorization from the community. We also hold valid the ancient liberties and immunities, and the reasonable customs granted to your church and hitherto observed in the chapels situated in your parish, and decree that they shall remain unimpaired in perpetuity.

Furthermore, we forbid anyone within the bounds of your parish, without the assent of the diocesan bishop and of yourselves, to dare build anew a chapel or oratory, saving the privileges of the Roman pontiffs. When a general interdict of the land has been imposed, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a low voice. We will that chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of your clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders shall be provided to you freely and without any impropriety by the diocesan bishop, if he is Catholic and enjoys the favor and communion of the apostolic see. Furthermore, the burial-place of that place, etc. On the death of you, the present provost of that place, etc.

Wishing also to provide henceforth with paternal concern for your peace and tranquillity, we prohibit by apostolic authority anyone within the boundaries of your properties from daring to commit robbery or theft, set fire, shed blood, seize or kill a person rashly, or exercise any violence rashly.

We decree, therefore, etc.

If anyone, therefore, etc.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Cencio, cardinal deacon of St Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the Roman curia, the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April, in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1194, and in the fourth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III.

### CXC. To Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury.—He entrusts to him the legation of the apostolic see. (Lateran, 18 March.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXII, 601.]

[Col. 1074C]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the apostolic see: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The sincerity of customary devotion and faith which the English Church has always maintained toward the most holy Roman Church has, as we confidently trust, flowered anew in your prudence and strength, and has received an acceptable increase of gentle ardor [variant: “sacrament”]. For such a reputation of your brotherhood has reached the Roman Church as refreshes us with the fragrance of your integrity and strengthens us with the vigor of the constancy which you possess, so that we may now make more openly manifest in our action the confidence which we have conceived in your worth.

Accordingly, at the request of our dearest son in Christ Richard, illustrious king of the English, and of all the suffragans of the church of Canterbury, that the English Church might obtain a legate of the apostolic see for the advancement of its own affairs and those of the realm, we have granted assent and favor to their requests: both because of the devotion which we have toward the church of Canterbury on account of the merits of that glorious martyr, and in view of your integrity and uprightness; especially because we strongly believe that it will benefit the church and kingdom if that realm receives in the aforesaid office a person such as the urgency of the said king and of those petitioners commends on account of the excellence of his manner of life and the devotion of his faith.

Therefore, for the honor of God, the welfare of the church of Canterbury, and peace throughout the kingdom of England, notwithstanding any exception or privilege granted to our venerable brother Geoffrey, archbishop of York, or to his church or to anyone else, we grant you the office of legate. By these apostolic writings we command that you receive it with the humility of brotherly obedience and, according to the authority granted you from heaven, apply the hand of due diligence by the authority of that legation to correcting what needs correction and establishing what ought to be established. In all things, indeed, preserve with ready devotion the reverence due to your mother, the Roman Church, so that through your deeds you may render her still more joyful concerning the success of the ministry which she gladly entrusts to you.

[Col. 1075B]

Given at the Lateran, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCI. To all the bishops of England.—Concerning the reverence to be shown to Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the apostolic see. (Lateran, 18 March.)

[Ibid., 602.]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren in Christ, the archbishop of York, all bishops, and his beloved sons, abbots and priors and other prelates of churches established throughout the kingdom of England: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The unsearchable height of divine wisdom established the most holy Church throughout the breadth of this world, and willed its governance and direction to be ordered by its incomparable providence in such a way that many should be taken into a share of its solicitude for its healthful administration, although the Roman Church has received fullness of power for the strengthening of ecclesiastical unity. For God willed that, as he addresses the Church in the Prophet, sons should be born in place of her fathers, men established as princes over all the earth, who by the merits of virtue and by the word of teaching should instruct the unlearned and those advanced in faith toward righteousness.

Accordingly, the most holy Roman Church, to which the Lord granted authority over the other churches, has from the beginning made a loving, maternal provision for the others, and has hitherto preserved the praiseworthy custom of choosing prudent men from diverse parts of the world for the fulfilment of their ministry. Under the direction of the Roman pontiff, their authority and teaching administer to distant churches what he himself cannot administer in person.

Therefore we, although established through insufficient merits in the lofty watchtower of that same Church, following in the footsteps of our fathers, intend with God’s help to exercise the ministry entrusted to us toward nearby churches in such a way that suitable provision shall not be lacking for those from whom we are distant even in location. At present, therefore, looking with the gaze of paternal consideration especially upon the English Church, we decree for its welfare and its special advancement in Christ, by the common counsel of our brethren, that our venerable brother Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury—whose merits and strength, wisdom and teaching, gladden the universal Church—having received the ministry of the legation, shall freely exercise our authority throughout the kingdom of England for the honor of the Church and the welfare and peace of the whole kingdom, notwithstanding any exception or privilege granted to you, brother archbishop, or to your church, or to anyone else.

By the authority of these presents, therefore, we command all of you by apostolic writing to show him due reverence and honor as legate of the apostolic see; humbly receive and observe his salutary admonitions and commands; and firmly observe whatever he, exercising the authority of the legation which he holds under the Lord, judges should be established.

Given at the Lateran, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCII. He commands the bishop of Foligno [Anselm] to recall the abbot of St Silvester of Ospello to obedience to the prior of Camaldoli. (Lateran, 20 March.)

[Mittarelli, *Annales Camaldulenses*, IV, Appendix, p. 193.]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the bishop of Foligno: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The beloved son, the prior of Camaldoli, has shown us in his complaint that the abbot of St Silvester of Ospello refuses at his own discretion to render the obedience and reverence which his predecessors are known to have shown to the said prior and his predecessors. Therefore, wishing through paternal concern to provide for the security of that prior and his church, we command your brotherhood by apostolic writings to inquire more carefully into the truth of the foregoing. If you establish that the matter is so, compel the said abbot through ecclesiastical censure to render the due obedience and reverence to the said prior.

Given at the Lateran, the thirteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCIII. He commends Adalbert, archbishop of Salzburg, “because, at the death of Leopold, formerly duke of Austria, he compelled Leopold’s son, together with the leading men of the land, to swear that satisfaction would be made for the offences and that what his father had wrongly taken for the ransom of the illustrious king of England would be restored in full.” (Lateran, 22 March.)

[Hansiz, *Germania sacra*, vol. II, p. 955.]

[Col. 1076D]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable A., archbishop of Salzburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The greater the authority bestowed upon us and you by the Creator of all, and the more persons whom, by God’s gift, we govern—persons who take examples from our acts—the more we must take care to conduct ourselves in the office of administration which we have undertaken in such a way that we instruct the peoples subject to us both by word and example, and can double and triple the talents entrusted to us.

For the testimony of Holy Scripture clearly and emphatically warns that, as gifts increase, the reckoning required for those gifts also increases: from him to whom more is entrusted, we read that more is required. Moreover, since both your archiepiscopal dignity and your depth of learning render your person more distinguished, you must labor with all your strength so that you may be found faithful in these things and deserve to be set by the Lord over many things; and you must protect and defend the devoted sons of the Church subject to your authority in such a manner as powerfully to oppose those who are disobedient and rebellious toward the apostolic see and ecclesiastical discipline.

We especially commend your brotherhood because, at the death of L., formerly duke of Austria—whose offences and contumacy offended the ears of all the faithful subject to the Christian name—you conducted yourself in accordance with the duty of your pontifical office in such a manner that, because the duke’s life was despaired of, you compelled his son, together with the leading men of his land, to swear that he would make satisfaction for his father’s offences and restore in full what his father had wrongly received as ransom for the illustrious king of England. You denied the father ecclesiastical burial unless he confirmed by sworn security that he would make full satisfaction concerning the aforesaid matters.

Therefore, since what you have reasonably done is exceedingly welcome and pleasing to us and our brethren, and since we do not wish it to be revoked on any ground, we command your brotherhood by apostolic writings diligently to admonish and induce the said F., the former duke’s son, to keep his oath and restore without diminution anything that he has retained of the things which he is bound by sworn security to surrender; and, if necessary, to compel him by ecclesiastical censure, with appeal set aside.

Given at the Lateran, the eleventh day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCIV. He takes the church of St Mary in Uznam under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Lateran, 23 March.)

[Hasselbach, *Codex diplomaticus Pomeraniae*, I, 175.]

### CXCV. To the canons of Urgell.—Concerning the election of a bishop. (Lateran, 27 March.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXII, 615.]

[Col. 1077D]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the canons of Urgell: greeting and apostolic blessing.

From letters of . . . your late bishop, of our beloved son the noble count of Urgell, and from your own letters, we have learned that your bishop, because of great physical weakness and old age, has resigned the episcopate and intends to dedicate the remainder of his time to his Creator in some religious house. We therefore, sympathizing with him and wishing to provide appropriately for your church, admit and ratify his resignation. By apostolic writings we command you, after invoking the grace of the Holy Spirit, to endeavor in accordance with the sacred canons to appoint over yourselves as pastor a person through whom the spiritual and temporal affairs of the Church may receive welcome growth.

But if, which God forbid, the enemy man should sow tares among you and a unanimous, canonical election cannot be held, know that we command our venerable brethren, the archbishop of Tarragona and the bishop of Lleida, that both, or either one of them, notwithstanding any contradiction or appeal, shall appoint over you a suitable person as pastor.

Given at the Lateran, the sixth day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCVI. He informs the archpriest and primicerius of Lucca that free burial has been granted to the monastery of St Peter at Puteoli. (Lateran, 27 March.)

[Mittarelli, *Annales Camaldulenses*, IV, Appendix, p. 194.]

[Col. 1078B]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the archpriest and . . . primicerius of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Considering the devotion which the beloved sons, the abbot and monks of St Peter of Puteoli in the diocese of Lucca, are known to have toward us and the Roman Church, we have granted their church free burial, in accordance with ecclesiastical custom. Therefore, by apostolic writings we command you that neither you yourselves shall harass that church contrary to the charter of our grant, nor permit it to be troubled by others; restraining any opponents who may appear from such presumption through ecclesiastical censure, appeal set aside.

Given at the Lateran, the sixth day before the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCVII. He commands P., abbot of St Peter, and Master Rudolf, dean of Salzburg, to compel Rapoto of Steine and Count Eberhard of Dornbach—who, while serving under the duke of Austria, devastated the monastery of Baumburg by fire and plunder—to make good the damage. (Lateran, 1 April.)

[*Monumenta Boica*, II, 194.]

[Col. 1078D]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons P., abbot of St Peter, and Master Rudolf, dean of Salzburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The beloved sons . . . O . . . provost and brethren of the church of Baumburg have sent us a complaint: Rapoto of Steine, when formerly providing his aid and support to the duke of Austria in a certain war, devastated the cloister of their church by fire. The said duke had promised to make good the loss caused by that fire, had he not died so suddenly. Furthermore, Count Eberhard of Dornbach, supporting the said duke, plundered their people; and, carrying some of them off as captives, extorted from them an intolerable ransom.

Therefore, unwilling—as indeed we ought not—to pass over such offences with dissimulation, we command you by the authority of these presents that, if what is alleged is true, you shall cause those wrongdoers to remain under the bond of excommunication until they obey the command of the Church concerning all the aforesaid matters.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCVIII. He confirms to the monastery of Baumburg the estate of Anegatterperg, donated by Elizabeth of Ortenberg and her sons Rapoto and Henry. (Lateran, 5 April.)

[Ibid.]

[Col. 1079B]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the provost and chapter of St Margaret at Baumburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant consent to the just desires of petitioners and bring to effect requests which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, gladly concurring in your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority, and fortify with the protection of this present writing, for you and, through you, for your church, the estate called Anegatterperge and the vineyards which the beloved daughter in Christ Elizabeth of Ortenberg, with her sons Rapoto and Henry giving their assent and support in this matter, is known freely to have bestowed upon you for the remedy of her soul, as you possess them justly and peacefully.

Let no person whatsoever be permitted, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CXCIX. He grants “free burial” to the monastery of St Peter at Puteoli, “so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict.” (Lateran, 5 April.)

[Mittarelli, *Annales Camaldulenses*, IV, Appendix, p. 191.]

[Col. 1079D]

Celestine, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and monks of St Peter of Puteoli, situated in the diocese of Lucca: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The duty of our pontifical office requires us to give an effective hearing to those who seek what is just, especially where their prayers and piety support them and the established truth of the law leaves no doubt. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, assenting to your just requests, we grant that the burial-place of your monastery shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; while nevertheless preserving the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. It shall also be lawful for you to receive for conversion clerics and laypeople, free and absolved persons fleeing the world, and retain them without any contradiction.

We decree, therefore, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the Nones of April, in the fourth year of our pontificate.

### CC. He takes the monastery of the Scots at Würzburg under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. (Lateran, 7 April.)

[Ludewig, *Geschichtschreiber von Wirtzbourg*, 997.]

CCI. To Walter, Bishop of Autun, and Garnier, Bishop of Troyes—On dissolving the marriage of Gaucher of Salins and Lady M., lady of Bourbon. (Lateran, April 14.)

*[Gallia Christiana nova*, IV, Instr., 93.]

[Col. 1080B]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers G., bishop of Autun, G., bishop of Troyes, and his beloved son . . . . abbot of the monastery in Argonne: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since, by reason of the office of universal governance which we have assumed, we are bound to exercise every care for the welfare of the flock entrusted to our concern, it is especially fitting that we be cautious and solicitous concerning marriages, inasmuch as greater dangers to souls arise from them if they are entered into without discernment: namely, if those whom God has joined are unreasonably separated by man, or if those whom it is clear have been joined by man contrary to God are allowed to live together.

You are to know that the relatives of our beloved daughter in Christ, the noblewoman M., lady of Bourbon, have represented to us that the nobleman Gaucher of Salins, her said husband, is related to her within a degree of consanguinity within which, according to the ordinances of the sacred canons, neither may a marriage be contracted nor one already contracted remain valid. Since, therefore, the substance of the truth has not been established before us, by these apostolic letters we command your discretion that, having summoned before you those who ought to be summoned and having more diligently inquired into the truth concerning the foregoing matters, you shall determine what is canonical. Notwithstanding any obstacle of objection or appeal concerning either the principal or an incidental question, you shall cause whatever you judge should be determined in this matter to be firmly observed through ecclesiastical censure. You shall take careful care to assist that woman favourably, so that she may suffer no prejudice in her legal right.

But because she, as we have learned, was once placed under strict guard by the same G., and, fearing on that account for danger to her own person, having been released, she fled again to her relatives, we will, and by the authority of these presents command and firmly enjoin, that, lest she again incur the same danger while the suit is pending, you shall, setting aside every objection and appeal, without delay or difficulty commit her, by apostolic authority, to the protection of our venerable brother William, archbishop of Reims, cardinal of Santa Sabina and legate of the Apostolic See; nor shall you in any manner permit her to be restored to the aforesaid man until the case has been concluded by a canonical judgment.

If either party, having been lawfully cited, should refuse to appear before you or obey your judgment, you shall nevertheless proceed in the same cause, appeal having ceased, as reason dictates. Moreover, since, as has been reported to us, our venerable brother Henry, archbishop of Bourges, has pronounced upon her a sentence of excommunication, we will that, after sufficient security has been received from her in the form required by the Church that she will obey the law before you, you shall absolve her by our authority, any remedy of appeal being removed.

And if, after the agents in this affair have undertaken a journey to us, anything has rashly been attempted or altered against the aforesaid woman before the commencement of the suit, you shall restore matters to their former state, appeal being set aside. Those who have been named to bear witness to the truth, should they withdraw through favour, hatred, or fear, you shall compel thereto by ecclesiastical coercion, appeal being removed; nor shall any letters stand in the way, if any appear which were obtained from the Apostolic See without disclosure of the tenor of these letters. If all of you cannot be present for carrying these things out, nonetheless two of you shall carry them out.

Given at the Lateran, 18 Kalends of May [April 14], in the fifth year of our pontificate.

CCII. He receives the monastery of Saint Alexander at Parma under protection and confirms its goods. (Lateran, April 17.)

*[AFFO, Storia di Parma*, III, 305.]

[Col. 1081C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, GUILLA, abbess of the monastery of Saint Alexander, situated in the city of Parma, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life: greeting and apostolic blessing for ever.

Although by the office entrusted to us we ought to exercise care for all churches and religious places, it is fitting that we be especially diligent for those known particularly to adhere to blessed Peter and to belong to his jurisdiction. Therefore, beloved daughter in the Lord, Abbess Guilla, we graciously assent to the reasonable petitions of you and your sisters, and receive under the guardianship and protection of the Apostolic See, and strengthen by the patronage of the Apostolic See, the monastery of Saint Alexander, in which you are devoted to divine service and which indeed belongs to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain firm and unimpaired in perpetuity to you, to those succeeding you, and through you to the same monastery. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1082A] Within the city of Parma, the church of Blessed Bartholomew with all its appurtenances; at Fabrorio, the church of Saint Andrew with everything belonging to it and with its demesne; the lands or possessions which you hold at Faligaria; at Fodico, the church of Blessed James with its appurtenances; at Belena, the church of Blessed Lawrence with all its appurtenances; likewise, whatever you possess in lands, vineyards, and houses at Melajano and Colorno; near the same city of Parma, whatever you possess at Meletato, Baganzola, Valeria, and Vicogibuli, in lands, vineyards, houses, and demesnes. At Vigorcolo, one enclosed vineyard with other lands and tenants; moreover, whatever you possess at Juliniano and Purpurano, in lands and vineyards, as well as in tenant-houses and other things; and what you possess at Vigattuti, Morturani, or at the basilica of Nola, at Moliola, Castello Nuovo, Feline, Vigodemeri, Traversedula, Puvilio, Berotto, Cadecomazi, and Noceto, in lands, vineyards, and other things, we confirm to you by this present writing.

No one shall presume to demand from you tithes of the produce which you cultivate at your own expense. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics who are to be promoted to sacred orders from the diocesan bishop, provided he is Catholic, enjoys the favour of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper exaction. Otherwise, you may approach whatever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested.

Upon the death of you, the present abbess of that place, or of any sister who succeeds you in the governance of the abbey, no person shall be placed over it through any deceitful contrivance or violence, except one whom the sisters of that place, or the sounder part of them, shall elect according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict. Moreover, we decree that the burial-place of that establishment shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who determine to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated.

Therefore let no person whatsoever rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, seize its possessions, retain what has been seized, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted. As a sign of the liberty received from the Roman Church, and of the fact that the same monastery belongs to the jurisdiction of blessed Peter, you shall pay one Byzantine coin each year to us and our successors.

If anyone therefore in the future, etc.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia. I, Albinus, bishop of Albano. I, John, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 1083A] I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Viterbo and Tusculum. I, Guy, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Callistus in Santa Maria in Trastevere. I, Hugh, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Martin . . . . . I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cinthius, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Soffredus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Bernard, priest-cardinal of Saint Peter in Chains, of the title of Eudoxia. [Col. 1083B] I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of Saint Adrian. I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Santa Maria in Aquiro. I, Lothair, deacon-cardinal of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Nicholas, deacon-cardinal of Santa Maria in Cosmedin. I, Gregory, deacon-cardinal of Saint Angelo. I, Bobo, deacon-cardinal of Saint Theodore. I, Peter, deacon-cardinal of Santa Maria in Via Lata.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Cinthius, deacon-cardinal of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, on the 15th day before the Kalends of May [April 17], in the thirteenth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1195, and in the fifth year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Celestine III. [Col. 1083C]

CCIII. He grants to the abbot of the monastery of Saint-Denis that he may correct his monks and lay brothers notwithstanding their appeals. (Lateran, April 18.)

*[DOUBLET, Hist. de Saint-Denys*, p. 526.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the abbot of the monastery of Saint-Denis, situated in the diocese of Paris: greeting and apostolic blessing.

You have caused it to be reported to us that, when you wish to undertake the correction of your subjects and instruct your monks in regular discipline, they raise to us the voice of appeal, and thus usurp for the defence of wrongdoing what is known to have been instituted for the protection of the innocent. Therefore, that such malpractices may be checked, we have thought fit to grant you, by apostolic authority, that, notwithstanding such vexatious appeals, you may correct the offences of your monks according to the Rule, and compel to regular life those whom you see conducting themselves insufficiently religiously.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may, etc.

Given at the Lateran, 14 Kalends of May [April 18], in the fifth year of our pontificate.

CCIV. He confirms to the monastery of Saint Alexander at Parma the church of Saint Cecilia. (Lateran, April 19.)

*[AFFO, Storia di Parma*, III, 305.]

[Col. 1084A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter in Christ, the abbess of Saint Alexander at Parma: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We wish, with paternal solicitude, to prevent measures reasonably established by our venerable brethren discharging the office of legation from being called into doubt in the course of time through anyone’s rashness, and to strengthen their enactments with letters of apostolic confirmation. Therefore, beloved daughter in Christ, favourably assenting to your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the ordinance which our beloved son Peter, cardinal priest of Saint Cecilia, is said to have made concerning Saint Cecilia’s, built upon the land of your monastery, insofar as it was made reasonably and without any impropriety and is contained in the authentic document of that cardinal. For the greater firmness of this apostolic confirmation, we have thought fit to insert verbatim into these letters the cardinal’s authentic instrument, which is as follows:

> “Peter, by the grace of God priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Cecilia, legate of the Apostolic See, to all the faithful in Christ: everlasting greeting. When we were at Parma and were discharging the office of legation, we learned that the parish of the church of Saint Gervasius had increased to such an extent that it was necessary for a new church to be erected, in which a portion of that people might receive the divine sacraments.
