## CCLXXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Denis. (Lateran, December 13.)

[D. FÉLIBIEN, *History of the Abbey of Saint-Denis*, Proofs, p. CXIV.]

[Col. 1188C]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son JOHN, almoner of St. Denis: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and bring to effective completion those requests which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, inclining to your prayers, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the house and wood of Berengarius and the other possessions which you have acquired through your diligence for the use of the almonry. We decree that you may freely and peacefully administer those possessions, and whatever you may hereafter be able to acquire there or elsewhere, God granting it, for as long as you live. [Col. 1188D] Yet after your death all those possessions must pass and devolve in full right to the almonry, as has been granted to you by our beloved sons H., abbot, and the convent of St. Denis, on account of the good and pious intention known to be yours toward the almonry, and as is contained in their authentic document.

Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation and constitution or rashly act contrary to it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the Ides of December, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

## CCLXXXVII *bis*. He confirms the possessions and privileges of the Church of Nicosia. (Lateran, December 13.)

[DE MAS-LATRIE, *History of the Island of Cyprus*, Part I, Documents, p. 601, from the cartulary of Santa Sophia, Venice, charter no. 8; cf. no. 9.  
Note: [Col. 1189D] No. 9 is a confirmation of the bull of Celestine III by Innocent III, dated 1 February 1201.]

[Col. 1189A]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother ALAN, archbishop of Nicosia, and to his successors canonically appointed in perpetuity.

Placed, by the Lord’s disposition, upon the exalted watchtower of the Apostolic See, we ought to love with fraternal charity our brother bishops both near at hand and far away, and provide with paternal solicitude for the churches entrusted to them by God. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, archbishop, we graciously grant your just requests; we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Nicosia, over which, by the Lord’s authority, you are known to preside; and we fortify it with the privilege of this present writing. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now lawfully and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, God granting it, shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. Among these, we have decided to specify the following by their proper names:

The site itself on which the aforesaid Church of Nicosia [Col. 1189C] is situated, with all its appurtenances; likewise, the endowment of that church, namely the two villages granted and assigned to it by our dearest son in Christ, Aimery, illustrious king of Cyprus: Ornithia  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Ornithi, southeast of Nicosia.]  
and Ascendia  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Second text: *Affendia*. This is Aphendia, near Ornithi.];

moreover, the tithes of the following districts of Cyprus which, by constitution of the Apostolic See, belong to the Church of Nicosia itself: namely, Nicosia with its appurtenances; la Solie  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Solia, in the valley of that name.];  
la Thomasie  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Location unknown.];  
la Tremetossie  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Tremethoussia, in the Mesaoria.];  
le Quit  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Chiti, near Larnaca.];  
la Quercherie  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Better in the second text: *la Quitrie*, Kythrea, east of Nicosia.];  
Cherin  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Xéri, south of Nicosia.];  
Lapiton  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Second text: *Lapizon*, Lapithos.];  
Melyas  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Perhaps Milia, at the eastern end of the Mesaoria, toward Karpas.];  
Maratha  
[Note: [Col. 1189D] Maratha, in the Mesaoria, northwest [Col. 1190D] of Famagusta.];  
Syvorie  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Sygouri or Sivori, in the Mesaoria.];  
Cambi  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Second text: *Cambyn*. Location uncertain.];  
Xindas  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Synta, in the Mesaoria.];  
and the fief of Briem  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Unknown.];  
and Asquia  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Aschia or Pacha-Keui, in the centre of the Mesaoria.];  
and Pigui  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Pighi, northeast of the Mesaoria.];  
and Prastrove  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Prastone or Prastove appears to be Peristerona, near Pighi, in the Mesaoria; but perhaps one should read *Prastione*, more likely Prastio or Prastion tou Sygouri, also in the Mesaoria.].

We confirm all these to you and your successors by apostolic authority.

We further decree that the bishoprics listed below—Paphos, Limassol, and Famagusta—shall henceforth be subject to you [Col. 1190A] and your successors by metropolitan right.

Likewise, out of regard for charity, we grant to you and your successors the use of the pallium, to be used on the days specified below: the Nativity of the Lord; the feast of the protomartyr Stephen; the Circumcision of the Lord; Epiphany; Hypapante  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] The Purification of the Virgin.];  
Palm Sunday  
[Note: [Col. 1190D] Palm Sunday.];  
the Lord’s Supper; Holy Saturday; Easter; Easter Monday; Ascension; Pentecost; the Nativity of St. John the Baptist; the three feasts of Blessed Mary; the commemoration of All Saints; the solemnities of all apostles; dedications of churches; consecrations of bishops; ordinations of clerics; the principal [Col. 1190B] feasts of your church; and the anniversary of your consecration.

It is therefore fitting that you provide more diligently how the honor of this vestment is to be preserved through the modest vitality of your conduct; that the ornaments of your morals may correspond to it; and that, by the Lord’s help, you may be conspicuous in both respects. Bound by the office of pastoral care, you should be found to show affection to the brethren, so that even those who are adversaries may, because of the Lord’s commandment, be joined to you in affection for you. Pursue peace with all; devote yourself to pious works; abound in virtues. Let the breastplate of judgment shine upon your breast, joined with the action-symbolizing ephod, so that you may proceed before God and in the eyes of men in such a way as to offer the flock entrusted to you an example of virtue; and so that adversaries themselves, seeing [Col. 1190C] your good works, may glorify your Father who is in heaven. Let a word of edification be on your tongue; let fervor of zeal be in your mind; and, beyond all these things, perform with moderation whatever belongs to your office, so that you may be seen frequently to embrace what the dignity of the pallium requires and may be able to acquire everlasting glory in heaven.

We also strictly forbid by this decree that anyone possess church cemeteries or ecclesiastical benefices by hereditary right. If anyone should attempt to do so, let him be restrained by ecclesiastical censure. Furthermore, lest the rights of you or your successors be able in any way to perish in the future, we prohibit monks in your province from holding chaplaincies or usurping the office or benefice of a priest or chaplain without pontifical authority; [Col. 1190D] rather, everything belonging to the right of the chaplaincy shall be kept intact [Col. 1191A] for priest-chaplains.

We further decree that no cleric of any order shall make subject to rent, or transfer into anyone’s power, churches granted to him only for his lifetime and belonging to the archbishop’s right, without the knowledge or consent of you and your successors; and, if this is done, it shall be deemed void.  
[Note: [Col. 1191D] It was not intended that clerics to whom churches or benefices dependent upon the archbishopric had been granted should be able to transfer them, or lease out their goods to anyone, without the metropolitan’s knowledge and express authorization.]

We further forbid anyone to admit persons interdicted or excommunicated by you to the divine office or ecclesiastical communion without the knowledge or consent of you or your successors, or to presume to act contrary to a sentence canonically pronounced by you, unless danger should perhaps be imminent and, because your presence cannot be obtained, it is necessary for a person bound by the sentence to be absolved by another according to the form of the Church, after prior satisfaction has been made. [Col. 1191B] We moreover grant you permission to have the cross, that is, the Lord’s banner, borne before you throughout your diocese and the bishoprics named above. By apostolic authority we further forbid anyone within the boundaries of your diocese to presume to build a new church or oratory without the assent of you or your successors, saving the privileges of the Roman pontiffs. Upon the death of you, the present archbishop of that place, or of any of your successors, no one may be set over that church through any artifice of fraud or violence, except one whom the canons of that place, with the advice of the suffragans, shall canonically provide to be elected.

We therefore decree that absolutely no one may rashly disturb the aforesaid Church of Nicosia, [Col. 1191C] or take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations whatsoever; but that all be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to make amends for the offence by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, acknowledge himself or herself answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, [Col. 1191D] and be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. [Col. 1192A] I, Melior, cardinal priest of the title of Pammachius, of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor [Note: [Col. 1191D] In the Palforis manuscript.], have subscribed. I, John, of the title of Clement, bishop of Saint Intluensis [Note: [Col. 1191D] The manuscript is erroneous here. Cardinal John subscribed other bulls as follows: “I, John, bishop of Tuscania and Viterbo, cardinal priest of St Clement, have subscribed.” (Paoli, *Cod. dipl.*, vol. I, p. 314.) “I, John, cardinal of the title of St Clement, bishop of Tuscania, have subscribed.” (Paris, Archives of the Empire, Historical Section, L. 235, 1)] and Tuscania, have subscribed. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Mary in Trastevere, of the title of Callistus, have subscribed. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of Saint Martin, of the title of Equitius, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, cardinal priest of Saint Praxedes, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca, [Col. 1192B] have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Berrard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro, have subscribed. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed. I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Bobo, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore, [Col. 1192C] have subscribed.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, on the Ides of December, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1196 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of Pope Celestine.

## YEAR 1196–1197

### CCLXXXVIII. To the dean and chapter of Rouen.—Concerning the annual revenues of prebends. (Lateran, 27 November.)

[Mansi, *Concilia*, XXII, 619.]

CELESTINE, etc., to his beloved sons the dean and chapter [Col. 1192D] of Rouen, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When a request is made of us which is recognized to accord with religion and propriety, we ought gladly to grant it and afford suitable support to the wishes of the petitioners. Therefore, beloved in the Lord, moved by your just prayers, we confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen with the protection of the present writing, the ancient custom of your Church concerning the annual revenues of the prebends of deceased canons, confirmed by the consent of the archbishop [Col. 1193A] and the entire chapter, as appears in their authentic instruments: namely, that upon the death of any canon, all the revenues of the prebend for the year in which he died should be distributed to pious uses according to the reasonable disposition of the deceased, or, if no disposition had been made, according to the judgment of the chapter. Therefore let no one, etc.

Given at Tours [read: at the Lateran], 27 November 1196.

## YEAR 1196–1197

### CCLXXXIX. He directs the abbot and convent of Saint John in the Vines not to receive more than ninety brethren in their church, nor anyone who has not reached his fifteenth year. (Lateran.)

[*History of the Abbey of Saint-Jean-des-Vignes*, Proofs, 305.]

[Col. 1193B]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the abbot and convent of Saint John in the Vines, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It has indeed been made known to us by letters presented to our apostolic office that, because your predecessors showed themselves excessively favourable to powerful and eminent persons, they were often accustomed to receive so many as brethren that the dormitory or refectory of your church could by no means accommodate them conveniently, nor could the church’s revenues suffice to supply necessities for their maintenance. [Col. 1193C] Thus, sometimes at the urgent request of those same powerful magnates, certain persons were placed in your church while still too young to observe the discipline of the regular order. On all these matters you have had recourse to the counsel and aid of the Apostolic See, humbly and with complete devotion requesting that it be established by apostolic authority for the future that no persons beyond the number of ninety, and no boy below the fifteenth year, should be received or admitted into your community. We therefore, assenting to your petitions, decree by the authority of the present letters that no more than ninety brethren are to be admitted in your church, nor is any boy to be received [Col. 1193D] into your church who is not known to have reached his fifteenth year.

Given at the Lateran, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

### CCXC. He confirms the judgment rendered by Archbishop O[berto] of Milan between Master Matth[ew] and the lay brethren of the hospital of Saint Simplician.

(*Decretals of Gregory*, book V, title 40, chapter 15.)

“Concerning matters which contain ambiguity.” And below: It came to the knowledge of our apostolic office that, when a dispute concerning the same hospital was being litigated between Master M. and the lay brethren of the hospital of Saint Simplician in the presence of the archbishop of Milan, [Col. 1194A] the archbishop, after hearing the case, did not employ in pronouncing judgment such words as, “I condemn such a party,” or “I absolve such a party”; rather, he pronounced as follows: “I establish and command.” And below: Considering, therefore, that this word, “I establish,” signifies a completed act and is understood as effectual, not merely verbal; likewise, according to Gregory, what is prescribed is commanded, and what is commanded must be done, and sometimes, if it is not done, it incurs a penalty; and considering nevertheless that one ought not to consider words but intention, since words ought to serve intention, not intention words, we interpret, in the presence of the procurators of both parties, and determine that the words of the aforesaid archbishop, pronounced in such form, possess the force of a judgment [Col. 1194B] valid in perpetuity.

## YEAR 1197

### CCXC bis. At the request of the chapter of that Church, he sends the pallium to Alan, elected archbishop of Nicosia. (Lateran, 3 January.)

[De Mas-Latrie, *History of the Island of Cyprus*, Part I, *Documents*, p. 605, from the cartulary of Venetian Saint Sophia, charter no. 1. Cf. nos. 3, 4, 5, 6, [Note: [Col. 1193D] Documents nos. 3, 4, 5, and 6 are repetitions or confirmations of this bull. We have made use of various corrections which they supplied [Col. 1194D] in order to improve the copy of text no. 1, which is the first document transcribed in the cartulary.].]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren the bishops of Paphos, Limassol, and [Col. 1194C] Famagusta, and to his beloved sons all prelates of churches and other clerics established throughout the diocese of Nicosia, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The unfathomable depth of the divine counsel, by whose will things earthly and heavenly are ordered, ordained that the foundation of the Church should be upon the rock [Note: [Col. 1194D] The manuscript has *statum*; document no. 3 has *statuit*, “ordained.”]; and he willed that blessed Peter, whom he appointed the vicar and teacher of that Church, though previously called Simon, should be called Peter after his name was changed, so that he who was known to be appointed over the Church whose foundation is upon the rock, which is Christ, should, by the Lord’s command, hold the office of teacher. He was called Peter, so that he might establish the people firmly in the foundation [Col. 1194D] of faith and possess full power of binding and loosing. But our Lord and Redeemer, who inspires and disposes all things when and as he wills, deigned in our time to recall to the bosom of the Roman Church—the Church which by divine dispensation is known to be the universal mother—the island of Cyprus, which for a long time past had been estranged from the mistress, the Apostolic See. He inspired our dearest son in Christ A., illustrious king of Cyprus, to request from us by envoy and letter that, on that [Col. 1195A] island, one church serving as a metropolitan see and three episcopal sees should be established by authority of the Apostolic See; he proposed to assign them suitable endowments, and that such prelates be instituted in them as would feed the people of God with the word of salvation and instruct them by constant preaching. Commending this pious purpose in the Lord, we assented to his request with the common counsel of our brethren; and, while A[lan], then chancellor of the aforesaid king and now archbishop of Nicosia, and you, brother bishop of Paphos, then archdeacon of Laodicea [Note: [Col. 1195D] Nothing is known of this prelate, who, after having been archdeacon of Laodicea in Syria, was then bishop of Paphos.], were carrying out the office of legation on that island, we granted you full authority, according to God, to organize churches and receive the endowments which the aforesaid king was to assign to those churches. [Col. 1195B] Furthermore, when the chapter of Nicosia canonically proceeded to celebrate the election of an archbishop, they unanimously postulated that same chancellor as their archbishop; and afterwards, by virtue of the authority of legation which he exercised together with you, brother bishop of Paphos, as the Apostolic See had granted you, the gift of consecration was bestowed upon him by our venerable brethren the archbishop of Nazareth and the bishops of Bethlehem and Acre. Since the chapter of Nicosia also humbly requested that the pallium [Note: [Col. 1195D] The pallium was a band of white woollen cloth decorated with crosses, which the prelate wore around his neck and upon his shoulders, allowing its ends to hang down, one in front and the other behind. [Col. 1196D] It is the highest sign of episcopal dignity. The pope granted it only very exceptionally to bishops; it was reserved for patriarchs and archbishops and was worn only on certain specified great feasts. The pope alone could—and still can, since its use has not entirely disappeared—wear it whenever he judged it fitting.] be granted and sent by the Apostolic See to the said archbishop of Nicosia, we, yielding to their request, have decided to send the pallium to that archbishop, primarily through you, brother bishop of Paphos, and secondarily [Col. 1195C] through our beloved sons Leonard and Ralph, canons of Nicosia. Wherefore, by apostolic letters we command all of you to show him due obedience and reverence in all things, to receive his salutary admonitions and commands, setting aside every objection, and to observe them steadfastly.

Given at the Lateran, 2 January, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

### CCXCI. He confirms the liberties and immunities of the monastery of Sorø. (Lateran, 19 January.)

[Shum, *History of Denmark*, VIII, 706.]

[Col. 1195D]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons . . . . abbot and convent of Sorø, greeting and apostolic blessing.

By the duty of our pastoral office, we are bound to give effective hearing to those who make just requests, especially where their wishes are supported by piety and the clear truth of right permits no refusal. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, granting favourable assent to your just petitions, [Col. 1196A] we confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen with the protection of the present writing, for you and through you for your monastery, the liberties and immunities granted to the settlers of your monastery and to your religious house by our dearest son in Christ Knut, illustrious king of the Danes, and by his father, the late Valdemar of illustrious memory: namely, that they should be free and exempt from every royal service, as is contained in the authentic writings of those same kings and of our venerable brother A., archbishop of Lund and legate of the Apostolic See.

We decree that absolutely no person may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God [Col. 1196B] and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, 19 January.

### CCXCII. He receives the monastery of Capelle under his protection and confirms its goods and rights. (Lateran, 26 January.)

[Wenck, *Hessian Regional History*, vol. III, p. 125.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons NICHOLAS, abbot of Capelle, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

It is fitting that apostolic protection should be at hand for those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an attack of any rash person either turn them back from their resolve or—God forbid—weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church of Capelle, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it with the privilege of this writing. First, we establish that the canonical order which is known to have been instituted in that place according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, and the institution of the brethren of Prémontré, [Col. 1196C] shall be observed there inviolably for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, by God’s favour, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and undiminished to you and your successors. Among these we have considered the following worthy of express specification:

The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; the estate at Everstorff with the whole holding of Albrechteroth, and Hougeren with all its appurtenances; Buchholz, Egendorf, and Luminesvelt with all their appurtenances; [Col. 1197A] Ludenrot, Wichten, Weldesbere, Solnhusen, another Solnhusen, and Landershusen with all their appurtenances; Alboldesberc and Bezingen with their holdings; the estate at Wirne with its whole holding; the estate at Grimeldesdorf; the estate at Engilgis; and the estate at Utershusen, with all their appurtenances. At Leigenbach, revenues of fourteen solidi; at Wolrshusen, fifty solidi; at Wirahin, eighteen solidi; at Rikershusen, thirty-four solidi; at Bidenbach, fourteen solidi; at Grimelderoth, four and a half solidi; at Gerlahesdorf, ten solidi; at Bubenhusem, eighteen solidi; at Geifridesdorf, nineteen solidi; at Hermannesdorf, three solidi; at Egendorf, five solidi; at Deidenhusen, thirty-four [Col. 1197B] solidi; at Grimoldesdorf and Frilngendorf, two talents and seventeen solidi; at Solnhusen, two talents and eight solidi; at Rohenroth, twelve and a half solidi; at Wegebach, two solidi; at Holzmanneshusen, twenty-seven solidi; at Aldendorf, four solidi; at Sigozeshusen, six solidi; at Bisopheshusen, twelve solidi; at Limpach, five solidi; at Eichen, two and a half solidi; at Lenterscheit, sixteen solidi; at Malzneltem, four and a half solidi; at Slachtersroth, six and a half solidi; at Husteden, thirty solidi; at Bucholz, four solidi; at Salzbuden, seven solidi; at Virne, five solidi; at Aldendorf, twenty-four solidi; at Megenharderoth, eight solidi; at Engilgis, fifteen and a half solidi; [Col. 1197C] at Urfa, three solidi; a mill at Virne; at Holzhusen, twelve solidi in Cologne currency; at Eppehagen, one solidus; at Herwigeshagen, four solidi; at Rukershusen, ten solidi; at Bunebach, nine solidi; at Belferoth, twelve solidi; at Wildingen, three solidi; at Wikardesdorf, two solidi; at Wichte, two talents and fourteen solidi; at Paleblaz, Domzelar, Heidelbach, Elbach, and Hegenebach, thirty-three and a half solidi; at Seilpach, thirty solidi; at Milsungen, eight solidi; at Holzhusen, eight solidi; at Unshusen, four solidi; at Sachsenhusen, seven solidi; at Dielichen, seven solidi; at Scastebach, seven solidi; at Rudolveshagene, seven solidi; at Gerstefe, [Col. 1197D] six solidi; at E[ch]agene, fourteen and a half solidi; at Jazbach, eight and a half solidi; at Monusebach, two solidi; at Schnegelbiz, three solidi; at Drumershusen and Steincile, one holding; at Bettenhusen, twenty-two solidi; at Munstre, fourteen solidi; at Frowenroth, six solidi; and at Verse, five solidi.

Furthermore, no one may presume to demand or extort from you tithes on your newly cultivated land which is cultivated by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the fodder of your animals. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a low voice. You may also receive into conversion clerics and laymen, free persons and those released from the world [Col. 1198A] who flee to you, and retain them without any objection. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your church, from leaving that place without the permission of his abbot, except perhaps for the sake of embracing a stricter religious life; nor may anyone dare retain one who has departed without letters of authorization from the community. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of clerics to be raised to holy orders, from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic and in communion with the most holy Roman See; otherwise, you may approach any Catholic bishop you choose who enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and who, relying upon our authority, shall grant you what you request. [Col. 1198B] We also decree that the burial place of the said house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last wishes of those who resolve to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; yet the rights of the churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken are preserved. Moreover, by our authority you have free power to redeem and lawfully free from the hands of laymen the tithes and possessions belonging by right to your church which they hold, and to restore them to your church. Upon the death of yourself, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any craft of intrigue or force, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the greater and more prudent part [Col. 1198C] of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations whatsoever; but that all be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, and, having been warned a second or third time, should fail to correct the offence by suitable satisfaction, [Col. 1198D] let that person be deprived of the dignity of power and honour, acknowledge himself or herself answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed, be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer, and be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Peter, [bishop] of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. [Col. 1199A] I, John, cardinal of Saint Clement, bishop of Viterbo and Tuscania. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of Saint Martin, of the title of Equitius. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Soffredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. I, Bernard, cardinal priest of Saint Peter in Chains, of the title of Saint Eudoxia. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. [Col. 1199B] I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory at the Golden Veil.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, 26 January, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1196 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Celestine III.

### CCXCIII. He receives the Church of Saint Exuperius of Corbeil under protection and confirms its possessions; he also confirms the agreement between the abbot and Maurice, bishop of Paris, “concerning the procuration to be paid to bishops in the Church of Paris.” (Lateran, 1 February.)

[Jean Bocquet, *Life of St Spire and St Leu*, p. 52. Paris, 1627, octavo.]

[Col. 1199C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot, and the canons of the Church of Saint Exuperius of Corbeil, present and future, to be canonically appointed, in perpetuity.

Both the force of equity and the order of reason require that just requests be granted effect, especially when piety supports the petitioners’ wish and truth permits no refusal. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid Church of Saint Exuperius of Corbeil, in which you are devoted to divine service; and strengthen it by the privilege of the present writing. We establish that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, by God’s favour, through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and undiminished for you and your successors. [Col. 1199D] Among these we have considered the following worthy of express specification:

The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; the cloister together with the tenants dwelling in that cloister; the village of Balecurtis; the tenants of Fonteneto with cultivated and uncultivated lands; the tenants with cultivated and uncultivated lands whom you possess at Chevanes; the tenants with cultivated and uncultivated lands whom you possess at Soisiacum; the village of Villadudone with its lands, meadows, and woods; everything which you possess at Euriacum, Vilarcel, and Castras; mills, meadows, vineyards, and all other things which you possess in the territory of Corbeil and in other territories; and the modius of grain which you possess in the greater tithe of Soisiacum, by gift of Paganus and his wife M.; the fairs which you hold at Corbeil on the feasts of Saint Exuperius and Saint Giles; and the prebend for the use of your church which you, son abbot, with the consent of our dearest daughter in Christ A., illustrious queen of the Franks, granted by charitable intention and devout resolution. [Col. 1200B] We also confirm by the present privilege the agreement amicably made between you and Maurice, bishop of Paris of blessed memory, concerning the procurations thereafter to be paid to the bishops holding office from time to time in the Church of Paris, just as it was prudently concluded, accepted by both parties, and hitherto observed, and as it is fully contained in the written instrument drawn up on the matter. Moreover, we hold valid the liberties and immunities granted to your church by prelates of churches, kings, and princes, as well as the ancient and reasonable customs hitherto observed, and decree that they shall remain unimpaired in future times.

We therefore decree that absolutely no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, [Col. 1200C] take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations whatsoever; but that all be preserved intact for the use and benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in the future, etc.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Conrad, archbishop of Mainz. I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina. I, John, cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, bishop of Viterbo [Col. 1200D] and Tusculum. I, Melior, cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Cecilia. I, Jordan, cardinal priest of Saint Pudentiana, of the title of Pastor. I, Guido, cardinal priest of Saint Mary in Trastevere, of the title of Callistus. I, Hugh, cardinal priest of Saint Martin, of the title of Equitius. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Stephen on the Caelian Hill. I, Cinthius, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Lawrence in Lucina. I, Soffredus, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Praxedes. [Col. 1201A] I, Bernard, cardinal priest of Saint Peter in Chains, of the title of Saint Eudoxia. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Prisca. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of Saint Adrian. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Aquiro. I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil. I, Lothair, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. [Col. 1201B] I, Nicholas, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Bobo, cardinal deacon of Saint Theodore.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope, on 1 February, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1196 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the sixth year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Celestine III.

### CCXCIV. He grants Gerald, bishop of Cahors, the right to receive from the Church of Saint Amator the expenses necessary for journeys to the Apostolic See and for other matters pertaining to his Church. (Lateran, 1 February.)

[*Series of the Bishops of Cahors*, 76.]

[Col. 1201C]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GERALD, bishop of Cahors, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just petitions of our brother fellow-bishops and advance their pious wishes in the Lord. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, assenting to your just requests, we give, grant, confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen with the protection of the present writing, to you and your successors, those things which, by the testimony of many bishops, abbots, and others, we have learned that you possess in the Church of Blessed Mary of Rocamadour: namely, the expenses necessary for you, your household, and your guests, whether you are present or absent, and expenses and mounts for the journey to the Apostolic See and for other matters to be carried out for your church, just as we have learned that you have hitherto possessed them peacefully. [Col. 1201D] We further grant that you and your successors may take all the aforesaid things, either yourselves or through your agents, from that church, should those who preside in that church delay to supply them.

We decree, therefore, that no person may infringe this page of our concession and confirmation or rashly presume to oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, 1 February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

### CCXCV–VI. He commands the bishop of Bobbio [Otto] to exhort the bishop of Pavia [Lanfranc] not to deprive the canons of Piacenza of the tithes from the territory of Porto Albarea. (Lateran, 10 February.)

[Campi, *History of Piacenza*, II, 375.]

[Col. 1202A]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop of Bobbio, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved sons, the canons of Piacenza, have informed us that, since they had long possessed tithes in the territory of Porto Albarea, a dispute concerning them formerly arose between themselves and Alfanus, late bishop of Pavia. V., a cardinal of the Roman Church of blessed memory and then legate of the Apostolic See, carefully examined that controversy and issued judgment for the said canons; this judgment was subsequently confirmed by the Apostolic See. While the same canons possessed those tithes under the authority of that judgment, a new dispute was raised concerning certain tithes of the same place between the archpriest of that place and the said canons of Piacenza. The dispute having been committed by apostolic delegation to our venerable brother the bishop and also to the provost of Lodi, [Col. 1202B] they examined the arguments of both parties with care and, after taking counsel with prudent men, took care to adjudge the said tithes to the aforesaid canons. In the course [Col. 1202C] of time, however, our venerable brother L., now bishop of Pavia, without making any mention that those tithes belonged to the same canons, obtained from the Apostolic See a grant that he should be bound to render tithes to no one from his own labours; and thus, carrying on cultivation at his own expense in the aforesaid place or territory, he seeks under such a pretext to despoil those canons of the tithes and of their right.

Therefore, by apostolic letters we command your brotherhood, if you find the matter to stand thus, not to fail to compel the aforesaid bishop, by our authority and without appeal, as shall be just, not to deprive the aforesaid canons of those tithes under pretext of that indulgence, since we do not wish it to cause any prejudice to their right or to diminish the tithes customarily due to them. [Col. 1202D]

Given at the Lateran, 10 February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

### CCXCVII. He confirms to the chapter of Ansbach the archdeaconry of Rangau. (Lateran, 27 February.)

[Ussermann, *Bishopric of Würzburg*, Proofs, 54.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the chapter of Ansbach, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just wishes of petitioners and bring to effective completion wishes that do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, favourably acceding to your just [Col. 1203A] requests, we confirm by apostolic authority, and strengthen with the protection of the present writing, for that church the archdeaconry of Rangau with all its appurtenances, just as your church is known to have possessed it lawfully and without dispute for fifty years.

We decree, therefore, that absolutely no person may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, 27 February, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

### CCXCVIII. He grants the sisters of Saint Mary of Soissons that, notwithstanding an oath formerly made, with the consent of the abbesses or prelates, they may receive any suitable nuns. (Lateran, 1 March.)

[D. Germain, *History of Notre-Dame of Soissons*, p. 445.]

[Col. 1203B]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess and convent of the monastery of Saint Mary of Soissons, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The duty of the apostolic office calls upon us, and the common obligation of charity requires, to lay the hand of our provision upon places dedicated to God in such a way that they may not in any respect be disturbed by the violence of any persons, but may, with His help, receive the desired increase, both temporal and spiritual, to the praise and glory of the name of Jesus Christ.

Now it has come to the hearing of our apostolate that in times past many nuns from neighboring places flocked to your abbey. Since at length, because of their number, they were unable to obtain from the resources of the monastery the sustenance they required, your predecessors confirmed among themselves by oath that from that time onward they would receive no nun from another church. But now, since few of those who confirmed the oath remain, and your church is deprived of its proper service—both because there are few resident sisters, and because they are old and infirm, while some [Col. 1203D] are of very tender age and cannot observe the discipline of the regular order—you have judged it necessary to have recourse, concerning all these matters, to the counsel and aid of the Apostolic See, humbly and with every devotion requesting that it be established by apostolic authority that henceforth you may lawfully receive suitable nuns from neighboring churches.

We therefore, assenting to your requests, have thought fit by the authority of these present letters to grant you that, notwithstanding the aforesaid oath, with the consent of their abbesses or superiors, you may receive any suitable nuns.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may be permitted to infringe this page of our grant and indulgence, or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the Kalends of March, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

CCXCVIII bis. He takes under protection the church of St Mary and St John the Evangelist at Cappenberg and confirms its goods and possessions. (Lateran, March 7.)

[NIESERT, *Münsterische Urkund.*, III, 294.]

COELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HERIMANN, abbot of the church of Saint Mary and Saint John the Apostle at Cappenberg, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

It is fitting that those who choose the religious life should have apostolic protection, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness either draw them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following the example of Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church of Saint Mary and Saint John the Apostle, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we establish that the canonical order which is known to have been instituted in that church according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, and the institution [Col. 1204C] of the brethren of Prémontré, shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; the church at Alen and the church at Werne, which Werner, bishop of Münster of good memory, either granted to your church together with their deaneries and parishes, or which the successors of that bishop afterwards confirmed to you; the church at Burk, which our venerable brother Herimann, bishop of Münster, granted to your church by prudent deliberation; the estate at Lohusen, which Frederick, count of Altena, conveyed to you by title of sale; and the fields adjoining that estate, which the nobles of Erperode sold to you.

Furthermore, with respect to the produce of your labors, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, whether from your gardens, shrubs, fisheries, or the increase of your animals, let no one presume to demand or extort tithes from you. We also decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken nevertheless being preserved.

Moreover, by our authority you shall have free power to redeem and lawfully free from the hands of laymen the tithes and possessions belonging by right to your churches which are held by laymen, and to restore them to the churches to which they belong.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let all things be preserved intact for the benefit in every way of those for whose government and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in future, etc. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, etc.

I, Celestine, bishop of the Catholic Church.  
I, Octavian, bishop of Ostia and Velletri.  
I, Peter, bishop of Porto and Santa Rufina.  
I, Hugh, cardinal priest of St Martin, title of Equitius.  
I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St Stephen on the Caelian Hill.  
I, Carth., cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina.  
I, Soffredo, cardinal priest of the title of St Praxedes.  
I, Bernard, cardinal priest of St Peter in Chains, title of Eudoxia.  
I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of St Cecilia.  
I, Jordan, cardinal priest of St Pudentiana, title of Pastor.  
I, John, cardinal of the title of St Clement, bishop of Viterbo and Tuscany.  
I, Guido, cardinal priest of St Mary in Trastevere, title of St Callixtus.  
I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian.  
I, Gerard, cardinal deacon of St Adrian.  
I, George, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Portico.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St Mary in Aquiro.  
I, Gregory, cardinal deacon of St George at the Golden Veil.  
I, Lothair, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus.

I, Bobo, cardinal deacon of St Theodore.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orthea, chamberlain of the lord pope; on the Nones of March, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1196 of the Lord’s Incarnation [Col. 1206A], and in the sixth year of the pontificate of the lord Pope Celestine III.

(L. S.)

A lead seal is appended on silk cords of yellow and red.

CCXCIX. To the chapter of Langres—concerning the residence of canons. (Lateran, March 12.)

[MANSI, *Concil.*, XXII, 623.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the dean and chapter of Langres: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When something just and honorable is requested from us, both the force of equity and the order of reason require [Col. 1206B] that through the diligence of our office it should be brought to its due effect. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, moved by your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority and fortify by the protection of this present writing the regulation made in the Church of Langres by P., formerly bishop of Tusculum, of good memory, afterwards renewed by the delegated judges, the abbots of Clairvaux and Lougivadi, and confirmed by the common oath of all the canons: namely, that no one shall presume to receive the income of a prebend unless each year he has remained in the church for sixteen weeks, continuously or intermittently, so as to be present at the office of one of the principal hours—Matins, High Mass, or Vespers—while preserving, however, the custom of the church concerning students and the attendants of the bishop and dean travelling to the Apostolic See.

We decree, therefore, that no one, etc.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Ides of March, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

CCC. At the request of Sifrid, count and castellan of Brandenburg, he grants the provost of Brandenburg the use of the mitre, ring, gloves, and sandals. (Lateran, March 18.)

[RIEDEL, *Codex diplomaticus Brandenburgensis*, vol. I, part VIII, p. 122.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son, the provost of Brandenburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1206D] Although the seed of the divine word, uttered by whomever it may be, is precious, and attention ought to be directed not to the garb worn by the preacher but to what he preaches, nevertheless, because in the eyes of men the adornment of garments and speech is regarded, insignia of dignities have been established in the Church of God, to be used in divine offices and in the propagation of the divine word only by those to whom they have been granted through apostolic kindness.

Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, in assent to your petitions—you who are placed in the midst of a wicked and perverse people, that is, among Slavs and enemies of the Christian name, and who ask to be adorned with certain insignia, so that the nourishment of saving doctrine and the word of faith which you instill into their hearts by constant preaching may be received by them the more gratefully and readily the more insignia they see you [Col. 1207A] bearing—we grant to your person, by the authority of these present letters, at the request of the nobleman Sifrid, count and castellan at Brandenburg, the use within your church, only on solemn days when you undertake to expound the word of preaching, of the mitre, ring, gloves, and sandals in the solemnities of Mass.

Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our grant or rashly to oppose it. If anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of April, in the sixth year of our pontificate.

CCCI. He confirms to the chapter of St Peter at Mainz the gift of the church at Altavilla. (Lateran, March 29.)

[WURDTWEIN, *Dioeces. Mogunt.*, II, 344.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons of the chapter of St Peter at Mainz: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners and bring to fulfillment, by a corresponding effect, vows which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, giving favorable assent to your just petitions, we confirm to you by apostolic authority and fortify by the protection of this present document the church at Altavilla, which Sifrid of Eppinstein, your provost, with the consent of our venerable brother, the archbishop of Mainz, bishop of Sabina, [Col. 1207C] granted to you as a supplement to your stipends: namely, that you shall appoint a priest in that church and assign him an adequate prebend from its revenues, while whatever remains is to accrue to your benefit.

Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

CCCII. He permits the monks of St Blasius in the Black Forest to sing “Glory to God in the highest, and the Sequence” on certain feast days. (Lateran, April 8.)

[GERBERT, *Historia Nigrae Silvae*, vol. III, p. 113.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the abbot and convent of St Blasius, situated in the diocese of Constance: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although we ought every day to render to the Lord a song of rejoicing, the institution of the holy Fathers, by prudent deliberation, ordained that on feast days we should sing with fuller melodies, and by a wonderful ordering established what should be sung by the faithful at solemnities [Col. 1208A] and what should at certain times be kept silent.

But in this we greatly commend your devotion in the Lord: that you have humbly requested from the Apostolic See, in which, by the Lord’s ordering, the fullness of power resides, a grant allowing you, when the feasts of the Annunciation and Purification of the Blessed Virgin and the feast of St Blasius occur within Septuagesima, to sing at Mass *Gloria in excelsis Deo*—“Glory to God in the highest”—and the Sequence.

We therefore, assenting to your petitions, grant you by the authority of these present letters that on the aforesaid feasts you may sing *Gloria in excelsis Deo* and the Sequence in the solemnities of Mass, earnestly admonishing your devotion that, as you desire by your voice to share in the angelic song, so you should show yourselves such in deed that, by the Lord’s working, you may attain fellowship with the angels in the eternal homeland.

Given at the Lateran, on the sixth day before the Ides of April, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

CCCIII. He confirms the rights and possessions of the monastery of Wadegozen. (Lateran, April 18.)

[HUGO, *Annales Praemonstr.*, vol. II, proofs, p. 623.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GODEFRID, abbot of Wadegozen, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1208C] It is fitting that those who choose the religious life should have apostolic protection, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness either draw them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid church, in which you are devoted to divine service; we fortify it by the privilege of this present document, establishing that whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grants of popes, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The right of patronage and the cure of souls of the church of St Michael at Buckenheim; the right of patronage of the church of St Martin in the same village, with all its appurtenances; the church of St Mary at Ramspach, with its tithes, offerings, and other appurtenances; the cell at Marceto, with fields, meadows, vineyards, mills, tithes, offerings, and other appurtenances; the church of Willari in its entirety; the church of Raldingen, with tithes and its other appurtenances; and, at Marceto, a fishery and a mill.

Likewise, at Marceto, Hardinge, Bute, and Fremestori, one hundred and twenty *diurnales* [day-measures of land]; the estate at Hustad; the demesne land of Ceppenberg [Col. 1209A] and what it possessed at Bestente; the allod at Burgalben; the church of St Adolf in the same village, with tithes, advocatial rights, and its other appurtenances; another fourth part which you acquired from the Templars; the allod at Singescheit; the allod at Borbach and half a *mansus* at Nove; a fourth part of a *mansus*; an eighth part of the wood called Putzernualt; one *mansus* at Pize; and all the goods which you possess at Siswilre.

Furthermore, with respect to your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or the increase of your animals, let no one presume to demand or extort tithes from you. You may also receive for conversion clerics or laymen, free and released from the world, who flee from secular life, and retain them without any opposition.

Moreover, we forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in the same church, to leave that place except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and let no one dare retain one who has departed without letters of the community certifying the matter. We further prohibit any bishop or others from demanding or receiving from you more for your tithes than has been demanded by their predecessors down to the present time.

When a general interdict is imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and those under interdict, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of your canons or clerics who are to be promoted to holy orders, from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any abuse. Otherwise, you may approach whichever bishop you prefer who enjoys the favor and communion of the Apostolic See; supported by our authority, he shall provide you with what you request.

Moreover, we forbid anyone within the bounds of your parish to dare build a new chapel or oratory without the consent of the diocesan bishop and ourselves, saving the privileges of the Roman pontiffs. To this end, we wholly prohibit new and unlawful exactions from being imposed by archbishops, bishops, archdeacons, deans, or any other ecclesiastical [Col. 1209D] or secular persons.

Furthermore, we decree that the burial ground of that place shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict; the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken nevertheless being preserved. Moreover, you shall have free power by our authority to redeem and lawfully free from the hands of laymen the tithes and possessions belonging by right to your churches which are held by laymen, and to restore them to the churches to which they belong.

Upon the death of you, now abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any device of fraud, cunning, or violence, except one whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, shall provide to be elected according to the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, remove its possessions, retain what has been removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but let them remain unshaken and unimpaired for the benefit in every way of those for whose government and support they were granted, saving the canonical right of the diocesan bishop.

If, therefore, in future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt to act against it, after a second or third admonition, unless he corrects his presumption by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him recognize that he is guilty before the divine judgment of the iniquity he has committed, be cut off from the most holy body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, and be subject to strict vengeance at the final judgment. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the supreme Judge, the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at the Lateran, through the hand of Cencius, cardinal deacon of Saint Lucy in Orchea, chamberlain of the lord pope, on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of May, in the fifteenth indiction, in the year 1197 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the seventh year of Pope Celestine III’s pontificate.

CCCIV. To all the faithful established in the kingdom of Denmark who give money to build the church of Aarhus with a stone wall, he grants forty days’ remission from penances imposed for their offenses. (Lateran, April 23.)

[LANGEBEK, *Script. rerum Dan.*, vol. VI, p. 387.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all Christ’s faithful established in the kingdom of Denmark, and to those approaching or passing through the church of Aarhus: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1210C] Amid the various conditions of human frailty, it is not easy for those dwelling upon the earth to escape incursions of sins. Works of piety have therefore been set forth as a remedy for our salvation, by which we may be able to have the Lord all the more propitious as we exercise them more devoutly in our neighbors’ necessities.

Now our venerable brother Peter, bishop of Aarhus, with a view to eternal recompense and for the honor of God and the laudable benefit of the clergy and people entrusted to his care, has resolved to construct in stone the cathedral church which in the time of his predecessors was built only of wood. Since this cannot be done in your land without heavy labor and expense, we ask, admonish, and earnestly exhort your whole community; we command you by apostolic letters and enjoin it upon you for the remission of sins, that, out of love of God and for the sake of the common benefit, you should provide grateful and generous assistance of charity from the goods bestowed upon you by God [Col. 1211A] for the completion of so pious and laudable a work. Thus, with your support, that church may be built more quickly and well; and through this and the other good works which, by the Lord’s inspiration, you shall perform, you may attain the glory of eternity.

To those who lend a hand of charity to the aforesaid work in accordance with the means granted them by the Lord, trusting in the mercy of the Creator’s clemency, we grant forty days’ remission from the penances imposed for their offenses.

Given at the Lateran, on the ninth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

CCCV. He confirms for the canons of Aarhus six prebends conferred by Bishop Peter. (Lateran, April 23.)

[Ibid.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother PETER, bishop of Aarhus: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The obligation of our office and rightly ordered charity require that acts laudably performed by our brethren and fellow bishops should obtain unshaken firmness through the protection of our authority, and should give greater confidence for future action. As has been reported to us on your behalf, venerable brother in Christ, you have prudently established six prebends to be assigned to canons who ought to serve the same church, from your patrimonial goods and other goods which you have reasonably acquired, and from those which the church entrusted [Col. 1211C] to you had previously possessed.

We therefore commend this statute with worthy praise in the Lord and, so that it may be firmly observed for all future time, as it was carefully and prudently made and as is more expressly contained in the authenticated document of our venerable brother Asger, archbishop of Lund and legate of the Apostolic See, we confirm it by apostolic authority and fortify it by the protection of this present writing.

Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles [Col. 1211D] Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, on the ninth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

CCCVI. He announces to all the faithful established throughout the province of Bordeaux that Gerald, founder of the monastery of La Sauve-Majeure, has been enrolled among the Saints. (Lateran, April 27.)

[MABILLON, *Acta SS. ord. S. Bened.*, century VI, pt. II, p. 874.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all Christ’s faithful established throughout the province of Bordeaux: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1212A] Just as golden bowls of incense, filled with the prayers of the saints before the presence of the Most High, give forth a sweet fragrance for the cleansing of the corruption of our sins, so we believe that it is of the greatest benefit to our salvation if we keep their memory celebrated upon earth, recalling their merits in solemn praises, whose constant intercessions in heaven we hope will aid us.

Now when our beloved sons G. and P., monks of La Sauve-Majeure, came to the Apostolic See and fully informed us, both through the letters of our venerable brethren the archbishop of Bordeaux and his suffragans, and through those of others—namely abbots and nobles—concerning the holy manner of life, conduct, and merits of blessed Gerald, founder of that monastery, [Col. 1212B] and had offered to us and our brethren many certain proofs; and when we had been made more certain through our venerable brethren the archbishop of Rouen, the bishop of Châlons, and certain others, who had more fully learned the miracles which the Lord works through the merits of that holy man; having also heard the outstanding reports of his virtue and miracles, and that among the carnal he had maintained a spiritual manner of life, and indeed an angelic one among men, we canonized him, who, released from the body, deserved to be with Christ. For we might seem in some manner to detract from the honor and glory due to him if we allowed one sanctified by the Lord to remain any longer without the veneration of human devotion. We decreed that he should be numbered in the catalogue of the saints.

Therefore, since his lamp so burned in this world that, through God’s grace, it deserved to be placed not under a bushel but upon a lampstand—burning in itself through works of charity and shining upon others by example—we ask, admonish, and command by the authority we exercise that, devoutly and profitably stirred to his veneration, you should honor him every year with a solemn feast on the appointed day, so that, invoked by supplicatory prayers, he may intercede for us before the Lord.

Given at the Lateran, on the fifth day before the Kalends of May, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

CCCVII. He permits [Gerard], bishop of Bologna, to excommunicate those who seize the goods of the Church. (Lateran, May 2.)

[SAVIOLI, *Ann. Bol.*, II, II, 200.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother, bishop of Bologna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The duty of our office requires, and the sincerity of your devotion strongly urges and induces us, to show apostolic favor to your petitions. Therefore, venerable brother in Christ, giving favorable assent to your petitions, we grant you by apostolic authority free power, without obstacle of appeal, to strike with a sentence of excommunication invaders and unlawful holders of possessions of the Church of Bologna, and to absolve, after satisfaction has been received, those whom you find bound by excommunication [Col. 1213A] for the aforesaid cause.

Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this page of our grant or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at the Lateran, in the year 1197 of the Lord’s Incarnation, on the sixth day before the Nones of May, in the seventh year of our pontificate.

CCCVIII. He enumerates and confirms the estates and privileges of the abbey of La Sauve-Majeure. (Lateran, May 10.)

[*Gallia Christiana nova*, II, *Instrum.*, 316.]

CELESTINE, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons PETER, abbot of the monastery of Saint Mary of La Sauve-Majeure, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Whenever something is requested of us which is known to accord with religion and uprightness, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and afford appropriate support to the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just requests; and, following the example of Lucius, our predecessor of happy memory, [Col. 1213C] we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and our own the aforesaid monastery, in which you are devoted to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present writing. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in the same monastery according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1213D] The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; in the same village, the churches of St Peter and St John; the granges belonging to that monastery, namely Malforat, with the land of Bunasse; the grange of Daignac and that of Carensac, with the church of Nérigean; the granges of Fontgraveuse, St Nicholas of Génissac, and Montfaitol, with their appurtenances; the tithes, mills, and tenants which belong specifically to your monastery; likewise the priories of Senon [Note: Col. 1213: *Senon*], Saint-Loup [Note: Col. 1213: *S. Loubez*], Castellet [Note: Col. 1213: *de Castellen*], Avaron [Note: Col. 1213: *de Daron*], Croignon, and Foncanbalada [Note: Col. 1213: *Foncambalas*], Madirac, Loupiac, Berabat, Baignaus, Old Benalgia, Gribon and Aguillac, Ardenas, and Daignac [Note: Col. 1213: *la Daux Renaugo vieille*], with all the appurtenances of those priories; also the churches of Épiet [Note: Col. 1213: *Espiet*], Caniac, Saint-Leon, Montinac, Corbillac, Saint-Sidoine [Note: Col. 1213: *S. Sidoin*], Dlassac, and Saint-Germain-de-Campet; likewise the priories of St Andrew of the Name of the Lord [Note: Col. 1213: *S. Andras*], Puy-Dodon [Note: Col. 1213: *Puy Dodon*], with its churches of St Christopher and St Severinus; the priory of St Martin and St Saturninus of Boens, and St Vincent of Portets [Note: Col. 1213: *Portets*], and St Lawrence of Escures, with all their appurtenances; and whatever you have at Brojas and Jalam.

In the diocese of Saintes, the priory of St. Nicholas of [Col. 1214B] Royan, with its church of St. Mary of the Isle, which is in Arvert, and its possessions in Oléron and Pratfornel. In the diocese of Bazas, the church [Note: [Col. 1213] of Branc. Ruch.] of Brana, with your other possessions; the priories of St. John of Blaignac and St. Peter of Castet, with its church of Siurac; the priories of Ruffio, of [Note: [Col. 1213] Soursac. Sescas.] Sorsac, of Coirac, of Fistals, of la Gardera, of Niac, [Note: [Col. 1213] Langon.] of Langon, with all their appurtenances; and of [Note: [Col. 1213] Belfont.] Bellefont, with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Périgueux, the priories of St. Martin [Note: [Col. 1213] Camp-Martin.] of Camp-Martin, and [Note: [Col. 1213] Escaurnac.] of Scaurniac, of Pison, and of St. Ulric and St. Nicholas of Gorson, [Note: [Col. 1213] Loupehac de Villefranche.] of Loupehac, with its church of Minzac; the priory of St. Saturninus [Note: [Col. 1213] de Puch.] of Puy, with its churches of St. Mary of Belpojet and [Col. 1214C] of Lonas; the priory [Note: [Col. 1213] de Verdhs.] of la Vernia, with its churches of St. Martin of Combis and [Note: [Col. 1213] Creisse.] of Crossia; the priory [Note: [Col. 1213] S. Pastour.] of St. Pastor, with the churches belonging to it; and the priories of [Note: [Col. 1213] de Cadetes et Tenac.] Atenac and [Note: [Col. 1213] les Nauses.] Nauses, with all their appurtenances, and of Siorac, with its appurtenances.

In the diocese of Agen, the priory of St. Antony and that of Runauld, with the church of St. Rufina and that of Maureliac, and St. Mary of Cultures; the priories of St. Sylvester of Pena and [Note: [Col. 1213] de Gontaut de Nogaret.] St. Peter of Gontauld of Escassefort, with their churches and other appurtenances; likewise the priories of Monthurt, Culezun, St. Caprasius of Lavardac, St. Mary [Note: [Col. 1213] la Hite.] of la Fite, [Note: [Col. 1213] Cabeouse.] of Caubeosa, with its church of St. Andrew, with all their appurtenances. In the diocese of Cahors, the nunnery, namely [Note: [Col. 1213] la Pomarede.] Pomaret, [Col. 1214D] with its priories, churches, and other possessions; the safe-conduct of Blanquefort. In the diocese of Auch, the priory [Note: [Col. 1213] de Bavarret.] of Gavarret, with the tithe and rent of the whole town, ovens, and its other possessions; the priories of Lucader, Mauvaisin, [Note: [Col. 1213] du Gel.] Gilo, [Note: [Col. 1213] Perqueier.] Perquerio, and [Note: [Col. 1213] Bougue.] Boga-del-Mont-de-Canens. In the diocese of Aragon, the priories of [Note: [Col. 1213] Reusta.] Rosta, Pintano, [Note: [Col. 1213] un Castille.] Unocastello, [Note: [Col. 1213] Exac.] Exea, Pratella, and Alcalá, with their churches, tithes, and other possessions [lacuna].

In the diocese of Lincoln in England, [Col. 1215A] the priory of [Note: [Col. 1215] Beroelle.] Proella, with its appurtenances. In the diocese of Cambrai, the abbey of St. [Note: [Col. 1215] St. Denis in Brogueraye near Mons in Hainaut.] Denis of Brocares, with its churches, tithes, and other appurtenances. In the diocese of Soissons, the priories of [Note: [Col. 1215] St. Leodegar.] St. Leodegar, [Note: [Col. 1215] St. Paul in the Woods.] St. Paul of the Wood, and Bellevallis. In the diocese of Laon, the priories of Gesy, St. Proba, and Lapion. In the diocese of Reims, the priory [Note: [Col. 1215] Nauvy.] of Noveii. In the diocese of Châlons, the priory of Chentry. In the diocese of Sens, the priory of Néronville. In the diocese of Orléans, the priory of St. Bartholomew [Note: [Col. 1215] Semois.] of Sede-Meri, with the churches of St. John of [Note: [Col. 1215] Cureys.] Curcy and St. Symphorian of Complens.

[Note: [Col. 1215] Add to these benefices: the priories of St. Anne of Artoleia; St. Catherine of the Desert; St. John of Champagne; and St. Lawrence of Obscures: in the diocese of Bordeaux. In the diocese of Bazas, the priory of St. Martin of Coyrac. Parish churches in the diocese of Bordeaux: St. Romanus of Targon with its dependent chapel; St. Genesius of Totigac; St. Denis of Climat, commonly called St. Denys; St. Mary of Credonio, commonly called Creon; St. Peter of Bat. In the diocese of Bazas, the parish church of Blessed Mary of Boleson. In the diocese of Agen, the priory of St. Antony of Agen; the parish churches of St. Hilary of Verdegas; St. Pardulphus; and St. Gemma, St. Albinus, and St. Stephen of Preignac.]

Indeed, no one shall presume to demand or [Col. 1215B] extort tithes from you for your newly cleared lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the increase of your animals. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen who are free and unbound, and who flee from the world, and retain them without any opposition. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices behind closed doors, after excommunicated and interdicted persons have been expelled, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. In the parish churches which you possess, you may choose priests and present them to the diocesan bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust the care of souls to them, so that they are accountable to him in spiritual matters, but to you in temporal matters.
