Book One, 21. Book Two, 85. Book Three, 157. Book Four, 207. Book Five, 289. Book Six, 351. Book Seven, 437. Book Eight, 539. Book Nine, 609. Book Ten, 655. Book Eleven, 725. Book Twelve, 793.

## CELESTINE III, ROMAN PONTIFF

Historical notice, 863. Diplomatic notice, 865.

## LETTERS AND PRIVILEGES ARRANGED IN CHRONOLOGICAL ORDER

### YEAR 1191

I.—Confirms to the Church of Porto a grant made by the abbot of St John at Ravenna, 867.  
II.—Takes the Church of St John of Rastorf under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 867.  
III.—Announces to archbishops, bishops, abbots, priors, and the other prelates of churches that Peter, formerly archbishop of Tarentaise, has been enrolled among the saints, 869.  
IV.—Informs the abbot and convent of Bellevaux that Peter, formerly archbishop of Tarentaise, has been placed among the saints, 871.  
V.—Promises Geoffrey, archbishop-elect of York, that Hugh, bishop of Durham, will be subject to him after receiving consecration, 872.  
VI.—Takes under protection the monastery of St Mary and St John the Evangelist [Col. 1292] at Lübeck, and confirms its goods, 872.  
VII.—Takes under protection the monastery of St Mary and St John the Evangelist at Cismar, and confirms its privileges, 873.  
VIII.—Orders Reginald, bishop of Bath, and the abbots of Reading and Waltham to restore what Archbishop Baldwin took away from the monks of Canterbury, 874.  
IX.—Restores to the prior and convent of Christ Church, Canterbury, privileges taken away by the late Archbishop Baldwin, 875.  
X.—Takes the Church of St Lawrence at Florence under protection and confirms its goods and rights, 876.  
XI.—Takes the monastery of Nonantola under patronage and confirms its privileges and possessions, 878.  
XII.—Orders Opizo, subdeacon of Parma, and Master John of Bergamo to settle the controversy between the canons of the cathedral church of Reggio and the clergy of St Prosper, 878.  
XIII.—Takes the Church of St Sigismund under protection and confirms its goods and possessions, 879.  
XIV.—Takes the monastery of St Peter at Pescara under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, 881.  
XV.—Grants various privileges to the prior and convent of Canterbury, 884.  
XVI.—Confirms for the prior and brethren of Camaldoli the parochial right of the church of St Margaret, 885.  
XVII.—Takes the monastery of St Anastasius near the Acquae Salviae under protection and confirms its possessions and goods, 886.  
XVIII.—To the chapter of Narbonne.—Confirms the transfer of Berengar, bishop of Lleida, to the metropolitan see of Narbonne, 886.  
XIX.—Takes the monastery of St Ghislain under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, 887.  
XX.—Confirms to the monastery of Cluny the monastery of Baume, 890.  
XXI.—Privilege for Henry the Lion and his sons: that they may not be excommunicated by any person except the supreme pontiff or his legate *a latere*, 892.  
XXII.—Takes the monastery of St Ragnibert in the Jura under protection and confirms its discipline and possessions, 893.  
XXIII.—Confirms the privilege of the provost and brethren of the church of St Nicholas at Stendal: if the diocesan bishop refuses to confer the ecclesiastical sacraments, they may receive them from any bishop, 895.  
XXIV.—Forbids a synod to be held in the church of St Nicholas at Stendal against the will of the brethren, or that it be placed under interdict.—Confirms to the provost and brethren of St Nicholas at Stendal the privilege concerning the care of souls, granted by Lucius III, 895.  
XXV.—Takes the Church of St Nicholas at Stendal under protection, 895.  
XXVI.—Takes the Church of St Mary and St John the Evangelist at Schwerin under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, 896.  
XXVII.—Grants Humbert, archbishop of Arles, authority to restrain by ecclesiastical censures disorders that have arisen in Provence, 897.  
XXVIII.—Confirms the agreement made between the churches of St Mary and Holy Cross at Étampes, 898.  
XXIX.—Bull which first establishes that the Order of St Benedict shall be observed in perpetuity on Mount Cruzenberg; then that its goods shall remain perpetually inviolate; and specifies: Erctestedt, Saverhausen, Dsthaimb, Bolthaimb, Heit-Zelle, Ingelmarstadt, Rapuldis, houses belonging to it, other properties at Hersfeld, and revenues from salt at Salzungen. Furthermore, by general decree it grants the right to celebrate divine offices subject to the stated conditions, and likewise the right to elect an abbot according to the Rule of St Benedict, 898.  
XXX.—Under penalty of excommunication orders the monks of Clus to return to the monks of Savigny their charters, which they have long withheld, 898.  
XXXI.—To the prelates of England.—On behalf of William, bishop of Ely, 899.  
XXXII.—Takes the monastery of St Peter at Savigny under protection and confirms its possessions, 900.  
XXXIII.—Confirms certain possessions to Hugh, bishop of Coventry, 902.  
XXXIV.—Confirms to the clergy of Cardona the church of Liemon, 903.  
XXXV.—Confirms to the archbishop of Esztergom the right to crown the king of Hungary and “to bind the provosts of officials of the royal household with the bond of anathema and to judge in spiritual causes,” 903.  
XXXVI.—Confirms the liberty of the Church of the Transylvanian Germans, made a provostship, in letters addressed to the archbishop of Esztergom, 903.  
XXXVII.—Confirms the goods and privileges of William, lord of Montpellier, 903.  
XXXVIII.—Confirms to Theobald, bishop of Chiusi, and to his Church all goods and rights, 904.  
XXXIX.—Orders Stenar, bishop of Växjö, not to encroach upon the possessions at Kolon belonging to the bishop of Linköping, 906.  
XL.—Orders C[inthius], cardinal priest of the title of St Lawrence in Lucina and legate of the Apostolic See, Peter, archbishop of Uppsala, and Jerpulf, [bishop] of Skara, to determine the dispute between C[olonis], bishop of Linköping, and Stenar, bishop of Växjö, concerning the boundary of their dioceses, 906.  
XLI.—Grants the monks of St Augustine at Canterbury “that they may celebrate divine offices during a general interdict,” 907.  
XLII.—Confirms the privilege of the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury concerning the blessing of its abbot, 907.  
XLIII.—Confirms to the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury the church of Northbourne with chapels for the use of its almonry, 907.  
XLIV.—Confirms to the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury the prebend of Gustone for the monks’ clothing, 907.  
XLV.—Orders R[oger], abbot of St Augustine at Canterbury, to see “that none of the clerics assign the church entrusted to him to anyone at farm.” (Fragment.) 907.  
XLVI.—Permits Roger, abbot of St Augustine at Canterbury, “if anyone who has obtained an ecclesiastical benefice from the monastery should disdain to render the customary oath of fealty, to suspend him from receiving the benefice.” (Fragment.) 907.  
XLVII.—Confirms the privileges of the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury, 908.  
XLVIII.—Informs Sueno, bishop of Aarhus, that he has permitted Absalon, archbishop of Lund, to grant him leave to resign the episcopate, 908.  
XLIX.—Writes correspondingly to Absalon, archbishop of Lund, concerning the preceding letter, 908.

### YEAR 1191–1192

L.—Orders certain bishops to release R., wife of Canute, king of the Swabians, from a vow of continence undertaken on account of illness, 909.

### YEAR 1192

LI.—Confirms the goods of the Liberian basilica at Palestrina, 910.  
LII.—Takes under protection the Church of St Thomas at Halberstadt, founded by Bishop Theodoric and entrusted to Premonstratensian monks, 911.  
LIII.—Confirms the goods and privileges of the monastery of Marbach, 911.  
LIV.—Takes the monastery of the Valley of St Mary at Helmstedt under protection and confirms its possessions, 912.  
LV.—Confirms to the chapter of Genoa the authorization granted by Joscius, archbishop of Tyre, for establishing a chapel in the city of Tyre, 913.  
LVI.—Confirms to Ubaldo, archbishop of Pisa, the primacy of Sardinia, 913.  
LVII.—Takes the monastery of Goldbach under protection and confirms its goods and rights, 913.  
LVIII.—Grants the patriarch of Grado the tithes of the Church of St Archidan at Constantinople, and permits him to exercise conventual right in the chapels of that church, 915.  
LIX.—Informs John, archbishop of Lyons, and his suffragans that he has granted the monks of Cluny “that it shall be lawful for them, if the bishops and prelates of churches of all wrongdoers against them and their men who are from the province of Lyons, after having been three times asked by the brethren, do not see fit to compel them to make suitable satisfaction, to subject those wrongdoers, with candles lighted, to a sentence of excommunication and interdict,” 916.  
LX.—At the request of Bishop Bentivolo, confirms the possessions of the Church of Gubbio, 917.  
LXI.—Confirms certain churches to the monastery of Cluny, 918.  
LXII.—To Bishop Bentivolo and the clergy of Gubbio.—Concerning the canonization of St Ubaldo, 918.  
LXIII.—Takes the Church of Scala under protection and confirms its goods, 919.  
LXIV.—To William, king of the Scots.—Confirms the liberties of the Scottish Church, 921.  
LXV.—Grants the abbot of the monastery of St Sixtus at Piacenza the use of the ring, 922.  
LXVI.—Takes under protection the convent of St Peter at Florence and confirms its goods, 923.  
LXVII.—Orders Aymar, archbishop of Vienne, and his suffragans not to permit their parishioners to be hindered from bestowing goods upon the Carthusian Order, 924.  
LXVIII.—Takes the monastery of St Justina under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, imposing upon the monks an annual rent of one bezant, 924.  
LXIX.—Grants William, bishop of Lucca, power to confer benefices even under lay patronage, if no other person has been presented by the patrons within a fixed period, 927.  
LXX.—Takes the monastery of St Mary at Lodi under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, 927.  
LXXI.—To the dean and chapter of Rouen.—Permits them, during an interdict, to celebrate divine offices without solemnity, 930.  
LXXII.—At the request of Bishop William, takes the Church of Lucca under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, 931.  
LXXIII.—Confirms to the convent of Ulcia the chapel of Holy Cross in Auvergne, situated in the territory of Camalaria, 934.  
LXXIV.—Appoints the bishop of Castello and the bishop of Clogne as judges between Wolcancus, bishop-elect of Trieste, and the patriarch of Aquileia, 934.  
LXXV.—Privilege for the abbey of Le Boschet or Vallis Lucida, by which the supreme pontiff takes the said monastery under the protection of St Peter and his own, establishing that the monastic order, recognized as instituted there according to God, the Rule of St Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian Order, shall be observed there inviolate for all time. (Fragment.) 934.  
LXXVI.—Takes the monastery of St Arnulf at Metz under protection and confirms its goods and possessions, 935.  
LXXVII.—Takes the monastery of St Vincent at Metz under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, 938.  
LXXVIII.—Orders [Seffrid], bishop of Chichester, and the abbots of Reading and Waltham “to absolve the clerics of Lamhee from the oath of observing the new chapel which they had sworn to [Baldwin], the late archbishop of Canterbury,” 941.  
LXXIX.—Grants the abbot of the monastery of St Denis “that, notwithstanding a frivolous appeal, he may freely perform the duty of his office in correcting monks and lay brothers,” 942.  
LXXX.—Takes the monastery of St Mary at Plumine under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, 943.  
LXXXI.—Takes the Church of Saints Andrew and Nicholas at Empoli under protection and confirms the possessions and privileges of its canons, 944.  
LXXXII.—Confirms to the canons of the Church of Saints Peter and Andrew at Paderborn the estate of Helmgeldere and the privileges concerning the election of provosts and bishops, 947.  
LXXXIII.—1. Ordains Albert, bishop-elect of Liège, deacon “on the Saturday of the solemn fast of the Ember Days celebrated at Pentecost.” 2. Orders Bruno, archbishop of Cologne, to confer consecration upon Albert, bishop-elect of Liège. 3. Writes to William, archbishop of Reims, “that if the archbishop of Cologne should refuse to carry out the apostolic command concerning the consecration of Albert, bishop-elect of Liège, through fear of imperial power, the archbishop of Reims shall nevertheless carry it out.” 4. Orders and strictly commands, under peril to each person’s rank, all clergy and people, and all ecclesiastical and lay persons of every dignity and office throughout the whole bishopric of Liège, that all obey Albert of Louvain; and that, released from the allegiance and oath they had made to the provost of Bonn, whom the emperor had intruded, they make an oath and pledge of subjection and obedience to Albert, whose election he approves, 948.  
LXXXIV.—Takes the convent of St Cosmas at Taliacot under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 948.  
LXXXV.—Takes the monastery of Altorf in Alsace under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 950.  
LXXXVI.—Ratifies Sifrid, provost-elect of St Martin at Worms, and establishes “that this provostship shall never thereafter be assigned to the bishop of Worms, but that its care and administration shall always be exercised through its own provost,” 952.  
LXXXVII.—Grants all Carthusian priors and brethren “that no prior or brother may be permitted to appeal without the consent and will of the chapter of his house, or of its greater and sounder part,” 952.  
LXXXVIII.—Confirms the possessions and rights of the canons of the Church of St Mary at Savona, 953.  
LXXXIX.—Takes the Carthusian house under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 954.  
XC.—Confirms certain privileges of the prior and brethren of the Carthusians, 957.  
XCI.—Takes the monastery of St Mary at Pomposa under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 958.  
XCII.—Confirms to the abbot and convent of Cîteaux the church of Schardeburg, granted by Richard, king of England, 961.  
XCIII.—Confirms the goods of the Roman churches of St Mary, Lady of the Rose, and Blessed Lawrence, situated in the Castle of Gold, 962.  
XCIV.—At the request of Bishop Mark, confirms the liberty, privileges, and possessions of the Church of Venice, 965.  
XCV.—Grants Conrad, bishop of Regensburg, authority to absolve those who, while fighting for the Church of Regensburg, committed acts of arson, 965.  
XCVI.—Approves the foundation of the Church of St Peter at Marchtal, 966.  
XCVII.—Confirms to the prior and brethren of the Hospital of Jerusalem the church of Reichartsroden, 968.  
XCVIII.—Sends letters to all bishops, abbots, provosts, and other clergy established throughout the kingdom of Denmark, 968.  
XCIX.—To the bishops of Lincoln and Rochester.—Concerning the invalidity of a sentence against the bishop of Durham, nullly pronounced by the archbishop of York, 969.  
C.—To the abbot and convent of Lire.—Concerning burials, 969.

### YEAR 1193

CI.—Bull for the canonization of St Bernward, bishop of Hildesheim, 970.  
CII.—Writes to the archbishops and bishops established throughout England that the armies which set out for the East did not fulfill expectations because of dissensions. He wishes the princes to be admonished, once discord has been calmed, to bring aid to the Holy Land, 970.  
CIII.—Forbids Berno, bishop, and the chapter of Hildesheim either rashly to diminish the body of St Bernward without the authorization of the abbot and brethren of St Michael, or to allow it to be diminished by others; and forbids them to permit the offerings of the faithful to be disturbed, 973.  
CIV.—Takes the monastery of St Michael at Hildesheim under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 973.  
CV.—At the request of Bishop Omer, confirms certain possessions of the Church of Ribe, 973.  
CVI.—Forbids the successors of Peter, bishop of Roskilde, to alienate the castle of Copenhagen, which is to come to the Church of Roskilde after the death of Absalon, archbishop of Lund, 974.  
CVII.—Privilege granted to the abbot and monks of Fécamp, 974.  
CVIII.—Confirms to Omer, bishop of Ribe, “every due of royal right which country-dwellers call *Querset*, while townspeople call it *Skot* and *Quersem*, and half of every royal due which in the city of Ribe is ascribed to royal authority, except these three: *Forban*, *Strandwerc*, and cases involving forty marks; all of which Sweyn Grathe, king of the Danes, remitted to all colonists of the Church, both townsmen and countrymen,” 975.  
CIX.—Takes the monastery of St Benedict at Ringsted under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 975.  
CX.—To the abbot and convent of Fécamp.—That they may lawfully remove from their benefice persons who do not serve their churches in person, 977.  
CXI.—Takes the monastery of St Mary of Ferraria (diocese of Teano) under protection and confirms its goods and privileges, 978.  
CXII.—Takes the monastery of St Mary at Esrom under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, 980.  
CXIII.—Confirms to Absalon, archbishop of Lund, that after his death the castle of Copenhagen is to come to the Church of Roskilde, 983.  
CXIV.—Orders the rights of the bishop of Lucca and the prior of Camaldoli concerning the Church of St Jucunda to be preserved, 985.  
CXV.—Bull for the monastery of Fécamp.—Forbids churches subject to the monastery of Fécamp to be placed under interdict, 985.  
CXVI.—Confirms the substitution of Premonstratensians for the monks of St Vincent at Wrocław, 986.  
CXVII.—Bull confirming the goods granted to the monastery of St Vincent at Wrocław, 987.  
CXVIII.—Confirms the privileges of the citizens of Pisa, established by Guy, formerly king of Jerusalem, Sibylla his wife, Richard king of England, and Conrad, formerly marquis of Montferrat, 988.  
CXIX.—Takes the monastery of St Benignus at Dijon under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 989.  
CXX.—Privilege for the Church of Genoa, 992.  
CXXI.—Congratulates Meinhard, bishop of the Livonian people, on the progress of the preaching he has undertaken, 995.  
CXXII.—Grants John, dean, and the chapter of Rouen “that, when there is a general interdict upon the land, they may celebrate offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice,” 996.  
CXXIII.—Takes the Church of Blessed Peter at Guastalla under protection and confirms its goods and rights, 997.  
CXXIV.—Takes the monastery of St Mary and St Rumon at Tavistock under protection and confirms its goods and rights, 999.  
CXXV.—Takes the convent of Sixena under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges, 1001.  
CXXVI.—Takes the monastery of St Peter on the Mountain at Heisterbach under protection and confirms its goods and rights, 1003.  
CXXVII.—Answers the questions of Walter, archbishop of Rouen, concerning appeals, 1007.  
CXXVIII.—Confirms the rights of the hospice before the greater church of Siena, 1010.  
CXXIX.—Confirms the constitution of Boleslaus, bishop of Vác, made with the approval of Job, archbishop of Esztergom, concerning a synod to be celebrated yearly on the Nativity of Blessed Mary (8 September), 1011.  
CXXX.—At the request of Bishop William, takes the Church of Melfi under protection and confirms its goods and rights, 1011.  
CXXXI.—Confirms the possessions and privileges of the Church of Bath, 1012.  
CXXXII.—At the request of Bishop Theodinus, confirms the boundaries of the diocese of Teano, and the possessions and privileges of its bishops, 1013.  
CXXXIII.—Informs the abbot and convent of Vallombrosa that John Gualbert, founder of the Vallombrosan congregation, at the request of the abbot and convent of Passignano, has been enrolled among the saints, 1018.  
CXXXIV.—Takes the Church of St John at Calcinaia under protection and confirms its possessions and rights, 1019.  
CXXXV.—Grants William, archbishop of Ravenna, authority to convey certain goods to the people of Argenta by emphyteutic tenure, 1022.  
CXXXVI.—Orders the provost of Mount St Walburga, G., cantor of St Gereon, and the scholasticus of St Mary ad Gradus at Cologne, to require the inhabitants of the village of Winsae to pay a certain tithe to the monastery of Deutz, 1022.  
CXXXVII.—To William, archbishop of Ravenna, 1022.  
CXXXVIII.—To Sicard, bishop of Cremona, 1023.  
CXXXIX.—To the bishop of Bitonto, concerning tithes, 1023.  
CXL.—To the abbot of Vézelay, concerning divorces, 1023.  
[Col. 1297] CXLI.—To someone, concerning excommunication, 1024.  
CXLII.—To the bishop of Ancona.—Concerning a sentence of excommunication, 1024.  
CXLIII.—To the prior and chapter of Dehum, 1025.  
CXLIV–CXLV.—Grants the monastery of St Augustine at Canterbury that no one may presume to burden its abbot or monks with any sentence unless he has been sent from the side of the Roman pontiff. (Fragment.) 1025.  
CXLVI.—Forbids Hubert, archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, to demand obedience from the abbot and monks of St Augustine, 1025.  
CXLVII.—Informs Roger, abbot of St Augustine at Canterbury, concerning the preceding letter; he is forbidden to render obedience to Archbishop Hubert, 1026.

### YEAR 1193?

CXLVIII.—To Canute, king of the Danes, 1026.  
CXLIX.—Bull in favour of St James at Provins, 1026.

### YEAR 1194
CL.---To Adalbert, Archbishop of Salzburg, he grants the office of apostolic legate. 1027  
CLI.---He confirms to the monastery of Steingaden the property bestowed by Duke Welf. 1028  
CLII.---He receives the monastery of St. Lawrence of Aversa under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1029  
CLIII.---To the chapter of Modena. 1031  
CLIV.---He removes the priory of Bromholm from the jurisdiction of the monks of Acre. 1031  
CLV.---Bull for the reform of the monastery of St. Caesarius at Arles. 1032  
CLVI.---He directs the bishops [Francis] of Arezzo, [Bono] of Siena, and of Pistoia, when requested by the abbot and monks of Passignano, to “raise the body of St. John Gualbert from the place where it lies, and beneficially stir the devotion of the faithful to venerate him.” 1033  
CLVII.---To the dean and archdeacons of the church of Lincoln.---Against Geoffrey, Archbishop of York. 1034  
CLVIII.---He directs Arpinus, bishop of Polymniacum, and William, bishop of Cuperzano, to assemble at the monastery of St. Benedict at Cuperzano, once abundant but now in the greatest poverty through the fault of its prelates, and to arrange for the election of a suitable abbot. 1034  
CLIX.---He directs Michael, archbishop, and M., archdeacon of Sens, to judge between the chapter of Chartres and the Countess of Chartres. 1035  
CLX.---He directs Adelard, Bishop of Verona, to receive an oath from the Duke of Austria. 1036  
CLXI.---To the Bishop of Lincoln.---He orders an inquiry into the misdeeds of the Archbishop of York. 1037  
CLXII.---He takes the church of Nidaros under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1039  
CLXIII.---He takes the church of St. Peter at York under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1042  
CLXIV.---He orders the chapter of Tarragona to declare William Raimund, who had cruelly murdered Archbishop Berengar in the city of Girona, anathematized and to place his land under interdict. Moreover, under penalty of excommunication and interdict, they are to urge the King and Queen of Aragon to banish William and his accomplices from the whole kingdom, to restore the property taken from the church of Tarragona, and to make satisfaction for the injuries. 1045  
CLXV.---He takes the church of Halle, called “at the New Work,” under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1048  
CLXVI.---He takes the convent of St. Mary at Hainsberg under protection and confirms its possessions. 1050  
CLXVII.---1. To John, abbot of the monastery of Saints Facundus and Primitivus at Sahagún, and his successors, he grants “that, provided they are priests, they may give solemn and pontifical blessing in the monastery itself and in its other churches, and, without appeal, bind or loose both clerics and laypeople dwelling in the borough, the precinct, and the other exempt churches.” He adds other privileges.---2. To John, abbot, and the convent of the monastery of Saints Facundus and Primitivus at Sahagún, he grants “that no person whatsoever, apart from the Roman pontiff or a cardinal legate of the Apostolic See, may pronounce a sentence of excommunication, suspension, or interdict against their monks wherever they reside.” He attaches other privileges.---3. To the same persons he confirms that the monastery was founded by Berengar of Medina. 1051  
CLXVIII.---He grants Roger, abbot of the monastery of St. Severinus at Naples, the use of a ring. 1051  
CLXIX.---He takes the monastery of Bonne-Espérance under protection [Col. 1298] and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1051  
CLXX.---He takes the monastery of Holy Cross at Donawerth under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1056  
CLXXI.---He orders the Bishop of Lincoln not to hinder the monks of St. Neot in their possession of the churches of Eynesbury and Thorney. 1058  
CLXXII.---He takes the Scottish monastery of St. James at Regensburg under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1059  
CLXXIII.---He directs the Bishop of Forlì to ensure that the church of St. Mary of the Port remains in the possession of the church of St. John in Marmorato, granted to it by the canons of Ravenna. 1059  
CLXXIV.---He takes the church of St. Reparata at Lucca under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1060  
CLXXV.---He receives the monastery of St. Prosper at Reggio under the protection of the Holy Roman Church and confirms its possessions and rights. 1062  
CLXXVI.---He replies to Gilbert, Bishop of Clermont, “that he ought in no way to observe an interdict imposed upon any church by one or more of its canons without his consent.” 1064  

ANNO 1195.

CLXXVII.---He permits Bernard, Bishop of Faenza, to restore the monastery of Gamondo, without his order subjected by its prior to the monastery of Acceglio, to its former status. 1064  
CLXXVIII.---He confirms certain possessions of the canons of Maurienne. 1065  
CLXXIX.---He confirms the settlement made between the abbot of St. Benedict at Piacenza and Martin, abbot of St. Mary of Vallombrosa, concerning the right and establishment of the monastery of St. James at Turin. 1065  
CLXXX.---He orders the Bishop of Castello (Venice) to grant the church of St. Bartholomew to the canons of St. Saviour. 1066  
CLXXXI.---He grants Peter, Archbishop of Compostela, “that, since human law provides that no prescription has force in tribute and public duties, and since the offerings which King Ramiro decreed should be paid annually to God and Blessed James in Spain are, as it were, tributes, any prescription pleaded against them shall have neither place nor force.” 1067  
CLXXXII.---He permits the chapter of Bremen to deprive beneficed brethren of their benefices if they have not paid to the chapter the customary dues at the appointed time. 1067  
CLXXXIII.---He directs the bishops [Hermann] of Münster and [Gerhard] of Osnabrück to anathematize certain ministeriales of the church of Bremen if they do not restore the goods unjustly taken from that church. 1067  
CLXXXIV.---He grants the chapter of Bremen that the security for the church’s indemnity furnished by Archbishop Hartwig “at the time of the agreement” shall remain inviolate. 1068  
CLXXXV.---He confirms to the church of St. Donatian at Bruges the legacy established in the will of Margaret, formerly Countess of Flanders. 1069  
CLXXXVI.---At the request of Sifrid, cardinal-priest of the title of St. Praxedes, he grants privileges to the church of St. Praxedes. 1069  
CLXXXVII.---He writes to [Adolf], archbishop, and to the dean of the cathedral church and the provost of St. Andrew at Cologne concerning the dispute between Adolf, Count of Schauenburg, and Hartwig, Archbishop of Hamburg. One of them, having occupied the castle of Stade and the county of Stade, had built Harburg Castle to the great detriment of the church of Hamburg; the other is said previously to have invaded the lands of the count, who had departed for Jerusalem. The bishops of Münster and Osnabrück had been directed to excommunicate the count unless he repaired the damage inflicted on the archbishop. If they do not obey the order, they themselves are to declare both the count excommunicated and the bishops deprived of their dignities. 1070  
CLXXXVIII.---He confirms to the monastery of Raitenhaslach the chapel of Zeidlern. 1072  
CLXXXIX.---He takes the monastery of St. Zeno at Reichenhall under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1073  
CXC.---To Hubert, Archbishop of Canterbury.---He entrusts him with the legation of the Apostolic See. 1074  
CXCI.---To all the bishops of England.---Concerning the reverence to be shown to Hubert, Archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the Apostolic See. 1075  
CXCII.---He directs Anselm, Bishop of Foligno, to recall the abbot of St. Sylvester at Ospello to obedience to the prior of Camaldoli. 1076  
CXCIII.---He praises Adalbert, Archbishop of Salzburg, [Col. 1299] “because, at the death of Leopold, former Duke of Austria, he compelled Leopold’s son, together with the leading men of the land, to swear to make satisfaction for his transgressions and to restore intact what he had improperly received for the ransom of the illustrious King of England.” 1076  
CXCIV.---He takes the church of St. Mary on Usedom under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1077  
CXCV.---To the canons of Urgell.---Concerning the election of a bishop to be carried out. 1077  
CXCVI.---He informs the archpriest and primicerius of Lucca of the free burial granted to the monastery of St. Peter at Pozzuoli. 1078  
CXCVII.---He directs P., abbot of St. Peter, and Master Rudolph, dean of Salzburg, to compel Rapoto of Stein and Count Eberhard of Dornbach, who while serving under the Duke of Austria had harassed the monastery of Baumburg by fire and plunder, to repair the damage. 1078  
CXCVIII.---He confirms to the monastery of Baumburg the estate of Anegatterberg, donated by Elizabeth of Ortenberg and her sons Rapoto and Henry. 1079  
CXCIX.---He grants free burial to the monastery of St. Peter at Pozzuoli, so that no one may hinder the devotion and last will of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict. 1079  
CC.---He takes the Scottish monastery at Würzburg under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1080  
CCI.---To Walter, Bishop of Autun, and Garnier, Bishop of Troyes.---Concerning the dissolution of the marriage of Gaucher of Salins and Lady M. of Bourbon. 1080  
CCII.---He takes the monastery of St. Alexander at Parma under protection and confirms its possessions. 1081  
CCIII.---He grants the abbot of the monastery of St. Denis authority to correct his monks and lay brothers, notwithstanding their appeal. 1083  
CCIV.---He confirms to the monastery of St. Alexander at Parma the church of St. Cecilia. 1084  
CCV.---Privilege for the church of St. Genesius. 1085  
CCVI.---To the provost and canons of St. George of Ganaceto in the diocese of Modena.---He confirms all their goods and privileges. 1087  
CCVII.---He praises the purpose of Henry, King of the Romans, in procuring peace, sending aid to the land of Jerusalem, and advancing for the better the common good of the Christian people. He commends his envoys. 1089  
CCVIII.---Privilege for the monastery at Lučenec (diocese of Olomouc). 1091  
CCIX.---He confirms the settlement made between Henry, provost of Hadmersleben, “and the nobleman Gardulf concerning the site of the church of St. Stephen, through the intervention of C[onrad], Archbishop of Mainz and Bishop of Sabina.” 1091  
CCX.---He takes the monastery of Ranshofen under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1091  
CCXI.---He takes the convent at Vilich under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1093  
CCXII.---He writes to [Michael], Archbishop of Sens, that he is grieved that King [Philip], without consulting the Roman See, had divorced I[ngeborg], sister of Canute, King of the Danes, and had received Cent., his subdeacon and notary, and his letters with too little respect. He annuls and quashes that sentence of divorce. He directs that, if “while she lives the king should wish to bring in another wife, he is to take firm care to prevent this.” 1095  
CCXIII.---He directs William, Archbishop of Reims, cardinal of St. Sabina, legate of the Apostolic See, and his suffragans, to do the same as was directed in the preceding letter to the Archbishop of Sens. 1098  
CCXIV.---He informs Philip, King of the Franks, that “that sentence of divorce [made with Ingeborg] has been rendered void and quashed by him.” He urges him to “receive his wife and treat her with marital affection.” 1098  
CCXV.---Confirmation of the sentences of excommunication and interdict issued by the authority of Archbishop Walter against the citizens of Rouen. 1098  
CCXVI.---He grants and confirms to the abbots of St. Chrysogonus the faculty, obtained from his predecessors, of using pontifical insignia. 1100  
CCXVII.---He forbids the privileges of the chapter of Chartres to be infringed. 1101  
CCXVIII.---He directs the canons of St. Quentin not to injure the privilege granted by him to the canons of St. Péchin. 1101  
CCXIX.---He directs Michael, archbishop, and the archdeacon of Sens not to allow certain privileges of the chapter of Chartres to be infringed. 1102  
CCXX.---He decrees that no canon is to be brought before a secular court except on account of a fief. 1103  
CCXXI.---He confirms the judgment delivered between Taon, abbot [Col. 1300] of Fontaine-Taon, and the parish priest Massarius. 1103  
CCXXII.---He grants the church of St. Mary and St. Theobald at Metz privileges of indulgences. 1106  
CCXXIII.---He grants the archdeacon, archpriest, and primicerius of the church of Siponto the use of mitre, buskin, and ring. 1107  
CCXXIV.---He directs H[ubert], Archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the Apostolic See, and his suffragans to exhort people to provide aid for the land of Jerusalem. He wishes King Richard to be admonished to send there “well-equipped knights and foot-soldiers.” 1107  
CCXXV.---At the request of Bishop Odo, he confirms two castles to the church of Penne. 1110  
CCXXVI.---He directs archbishops, bishops, and other prelates of churches established throughout Alemannia and Germany to induce the people “to assist the region of Jerusalem in persons and property, according to the just disposition of P[eter], cardinal-priest of St. Cecilia, and J[ohn], cardinal-priest of the title of St. Stephen on the Caelian Hill.” 1110  
CCXXVII.---By letters to the chapter of Blessed Martin at Tours, he forbids any rent or lease of church property for more than ten pounds to be granted without security; he then decrees that canons absent from their duties are to lose the six denarii which they received daily from the common fund. 1110  
CCXXVIII.---He takes the church of Auch under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1111  
CCXXIX.---To the bishops of Bayeux, Avranches, Séez, and Coutances.---Concerning the sedition raised by the citizens of Rouen against the canons, and the satisfaction to be made to them. 1116  
CCXXX.---To the citizens of Rouen.---On the same subject. 1117  
CCXXX bis.---He takes the church of St. Mary of Newcastle under protection and confirms its donations, possessions, and property. 1119  
CCXXXI.---Privilege for the monastery of Bec. 1120  
CCXXXII.---He takes the monastery of St. Mary at Germerode under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1123  
CCXXXIII.---To Simon, dean of York.---Concerning the administration of that diocese. 1125  
CCXXXIV.---To the clergy of York.---On the same subject. 1125  
CCXXXV.---To the Bishop of Lincoln.---On the same subject. 1127  
CCXXXVI.---He confirms the judgment delivered by Michael, Archbishop of Sens, and M., archdeacon of Sens, between the chapter of Chartres and Adela, Countess of Blois. 1131  
CCXXXVII.---He takes the monastery of St. Mary at Deuil under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1133  

ANNO 1196.

CCXXXVIII.---To Hubert, Archbishop of Canterbury.---Concerning the affairs of the Holy Land. 1135  
CCXXXIX.---To Walter, Archbishop of Rouen.---That he should restrain those who despised ecclesiastical censures. 1136  
CCXL.---He directs Albert, Bishop of Vercelli, and the abbot of Locedio, under penalty of anathema, to forbid the monks of St. Just from administering ecclesiastical sacraments to the townsmen of Susa contrary to the privilege of the canons of Oulx. 1136  
CXLI.---He grants Gerard, Bishop of Bologna, that, if priests of churches in the city or diocese of Bologna should die, he may have authority to entrust their office to others. 1136  
CCXLII.---He takes the monastery of St. Mary at Baumgarten under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1137  
CCXLIII.---He grants the abbot of Longpont “that no one may demand procurations in the granges belonging to the monastery or exact homage from its servants.” 1141  
CCXLIV.---He confirms to Aegidius, Bishop of Modena, the right of appointing canons in the churches of his bishopric. 1142  
CCXLV.---Privilege for the church of the Holy Sepulchre at Jerusalem. 1142  
CCXLVI.---He confirms the exchange of “the estate of Bocharn,” made by the provost and chapter of the church of Reichenau with C[onrad], bishop, and the canons of Regensburg. 1147  
CCXLVI bis.---To the clergy, magnates, and people of Cyprus.---He declares that, at the request of King Amalric, he had delegated the Archdeacon of Laodicea and Alan, Chancellor of Cyprus, to regulate in that island, hitherto schismatic, whatever concerned the conferral of endowments upon [Col. 1301] the Church, notwithstanding the obstacle of appeal. 1147  
CCXLVII.---He takes the church of St. Alban at Basel under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1148  
CCXLVIII.---He takes the monastery of St. Peter at Aldenburg under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1150  
CCXLIX.---He takes the convent of St. Mary at Kluaynard under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1152  
CCL.---To the master and brethren of the Knights Templar.---Concerning tithes. 1154  
CCLI.---He urges the Count of Toulouse to repair the damage inflicted on the monastery of St. Giles; otherwise, he declares that he will be excommunicated by the archbishops of Bourges, Narbonne, Arles, and Aix. 1155  
CCLII.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Lawrence at Wedinghausen. 1156  
CCLIII.---To the chapter of Nidaros.---He forbids any layperson in the diocese of Nidaros to exercise ecclesiastical jurisdiction. 1159  
CCLIV.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Maurice at Agaune. 1159  
CCLV.---He grants William, abbot of St. Maurice at Agaune, the use of mitre and ring. 1159  
CCLVI.---He confirms to Berard, elected Archbishop of Messina, the entire tithe of the River Dionysius. 1160  
CCLVII.---He decrees that Greek and Latin abbots shall provide necessities for Berard, Archbishop of Messina, while he visits his parishes. 1160  
CCLVIII.---To William, Bishop of Maguelonne. 1160  
CCLIX.---To William, bishop, and the chapter of the church of Maguelonne. 1161  
CCLX.---He forbids the prior and monks of St. Pancras of Lewes to pay certain pensions or to promise churches to anyone before they are vacant. 1162  
CCLXI.---He confirms the bridge of Litia, together with its chapel, to the chapter of Parma. 1162  
CCLXII.---Bull for the convent of Crisenon. 1163  
CCLXIII.---He directs Hubert, Archbishop of Canterbury, to give the monks of Thorney opportunity to appoint a successor in place of their deposed abbot. 1165  
CCLXIV.---He takes the church of St. Mary of the Port at Ravenna under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1165  
CCLXV.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the church of Paris. 1168  
CCLXVI.---He confirms the customs of the chapter of Mâcon. 1169  
CCLXVII.---He decrees upon whom, among the clergy of Modena, the burden of expenses is to fall upon the arrival or passage of legates of the Holy See and of the metropolitan. 1170  
CCLXVIII.---He directs S[icard], Bishop of Cremona, not to allow the church of Holy Cross at Cremona to suffer injury to the detriment of the administration of the monastery of Nonantola from its patrons and neighbours. 1171  
CCLXIX.---Confirmation of the settlement between the archbishop and clergy of Split. 1171  
CCLXX.---To the Bishops of Skradin and Knin. 1173  
CCLXXI.---He enlarges the privileges and possessions of the monastery of the Holy Trinity at Fécamp, subject only to the Roman pontiff. 1173  
CCLXXII.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of St. Mary at Vendôme. 1176  
CCLXXIII.---He directs Albert, Bishop of Vercelli, and Peter, abbot of Locedio, to make peace between Archbishop Boniface and the canons of Genoa. 1178  
CCLXXIV.---He permits Hugh, abbot of Cluny, “to correct, in the abbeys belonging to the monastery of Cluny, those things which appear to require correction according to God, the Rule of Blessed Benedict, and the statutes of the order.” 1179  
CCLXXV.---He directs [Michael], Archbishop of Sens, and the abbot of St. Columba to compel the Count of Nevers to restore the house of Colanges to the priory of La Charité. 1180  
CCLXXVI.---He confirms to the canons of the Venetian church of St. Saviour the church of St. Bartholomew, granted by Bishop Mark. 1181  
CCLXXVII.---He directs archbishops, bishops, abbots, deans, and other prelates of churches to excommunicate lay plunderers and harassers of the brethren of Cluny, and to remove clerics from their offices. 1181  
CCLXXVIII.---He directs Master Leo, procurator at Constantinople, to compel the heirs to pay the Bishop of Castello (Venice) tithes from the goods of John Canalo Lupi. 1182 [Col. 1302]  
CCLXXIX.---He confirms the “constitutions concerning the life of the monks and monasteries subject to his abbey, concerning the property possessed by the brethren themselves, and concerning their number,” of Abbot Joachim of Fiore. 1183  
CCLXXX.---He permits Aegidius, Bishop of Modena, to punish the disobedience of certain clerics. 1183  
CCLXXXI.---He directs the Archbishop of Ravenna and his suffragans, under penalty of excommunication, to admonish the citizens of Modena to restore what they had taken from the monastery of Nonantola. 1184  
CCLXXXII.---He directs the Bishop of Arras, the abbot of St. Victor, and the prior of St. Martin-des-Champs at Paris to subject the church of Calais to the church of Paris. 1184  
CCLXXXIII.---By letters to Odo, Bishop of Penne, he confirms “the sentence of deposition issued against the clerics of Arsita.” 1186  
CCLXXXIV.---Bull for the nuns of St. Julian at Auxerre. 1187  
CCLXXXV.---He directs the abbots of St. Peter at Salzburg and Ebersberg, and the provost of St. Andrew at Freising, to protect the brethren of Garsten against Count C. of Medeling. 1188  
CCLXXXVI.---He directs the abbot of Hemmerode and the scholasticus of the cathedral church of Trier to judge between the brethren of St. Peter at Mainz and their provost Sifrid of Eppenstein. 1188  
CCLXXXVII.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Denis. 1188  
CCLXXXVII bis.---He confirms the possessions and privileges of the church of Nicosia. 1189  

ANNO 1191–1197.

CCXXXVIII.---To the dean and chapter of Rouen.---Concerning the registers of prebends. 1192  

ANNO 1196–1197.

CCLXXXIX.---He prescribes to the abbot and convent of St. John in the Vineyards that no more than ninety brethren are to be admitted into their church, nor anyone who has not reached his fifteenth year. 1193  
CCXC.---He confirms the judgment delivered by Oberto, Archbishop of Milan, between Master Matthew and the lay brothers of the hospital of St. Simplician. 1193  

ANNO 1197.

CCXC bis.---At the request of the chapter of that church, he sends the pallium to Alan, elected Archbishop of Nicosia. 1194  
CCXCI.---He confirms the liberties and immunities of the monastery of Sorø. 1195  
CCXCII.---He takes the monastery of La Chapelle under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1196  
CCXCIII.---He takes the church of St. Exuperius at Corbeil under protection and confirms its possessions; moreover, he confirms the settlement between the abbot and Maurice, Bishop of Paris, “concerning the procuration to be paid to bishops in the church of Paris.” 1199  
CCXCIV.---He grants Gerald, Bishop of Cahors, that he may receive from the church of St. Amator the expenses necessary for a journey to the Apostolic See and for other matters concerning his church. 1201  
CCXCV–VI.---He directs Otto, Bishop of Bobbio, to urge Lanfranc, Bishop of Pavia, not to deprive the canons of Piacenza of the tithes from the territory of Porto Albare. 1202  
CCXCVII.---He confirms to the chapter of Ansbach the archdeaconry of Rangau. 1202  
CCXCVIII.---He grants the sisters of St. Mary at Soissons, notwithstanding an oath previously made, that with the consent of the abbesses or female superiors they may receive any suitable women as nuns. 1203  
CCXCVIII bis.---He takes the church of St. Mary and St. John the Evangelist at Coppenberg under protection and confirms its goods and possessions. 1204  
CCXCIX.---To the chapter of Langres.---Concerning the residence of canons. 1206  
CCC.---At the request of Sifrid, Count and Castellan of Brandenburg, he grants the provost of Brandenburg the use of mitre, ring, gloves, and sandals. 1206  
CCCI.---He confirms the donation of the church at Hauteville to the chapter of St. Peter at Mainz. 1207  
CCCII.---He permits the monks of St. Blasius in the Black Forest to sing on certain feast days: “Glory to God in the highest,” and the Sequence. 1207  
CCCIII.---He confirms the rights and possessions of the monastery of Wedinghausen. 1208  
CCCIV.---To all the faithful established in the kingdom of Denmark who give money for the construction of a stone wall for the church of Aarhus, [Col. 1303] he remits forty days of the penances imposed for their offences. 1210  
CCCV.---He confirms to the canons of Aarhus six prebends conferred by Bishop Peter. 1211  
CCCVI.---He announces to all the faithful throughout the province of Bordeaux that Gerald, founder of the monastery of La Sauve-Majeure, has been enrolled among the saints. 1211  
CCCVII.---He permits Gerard, Bishop of Bologna, to excommunicate those who have occupied the goods of the Church. 1212  
CCCVIII.---He enumerates and confirms the estates and privileges of the monastery of La Sauve-Majeure. 1213  
CCCIX.---He takes the canonry of St. Mary at Pesaro under protection and confirms its possessions. 1217  
CCCX.---He confirms the agreements made between the abbess of St. Alexander and Hugh, canon of the church of Parma and archpriest of the parish church of St. Pancras. 1219  
CCCXI.---He confirms to the monastery of St. Denis the patronage of the church of Blessed Mary of Medonta, granted by Philip, King of the Franks. 1220  
CCCXII.---He confirms the judgment delivered by Burchard, abbot of Ebersberg, and Conrad, provost of St. Andrew at Freising, between the Garsten brethren and the provost of Ovens. 1221  
CCCXIII.---He forbids the abbot and monks of Fécamp to provide the archdeacon of Calais with an annual procuration. 1223  
CCCXIV.---He warns the monks of Nonantola not to retain an improper custom in assigning the monastery’s possessions. 1223  
CCCXV.---He grants Hugh, abbot, and the brethren of St. Denis that no one may dare to pronounce against them a sentence of excommunication. 1224  
CCCXVI.---To the Archbishop of Rouen.---What punishment is to be imposed upon plunderers, invaders, or burners of churches. 1225  
CCCXVII.---He takes the monastery of Amelungsborn under protection and confirms its possessions, rights, and privileges. 1226  
CCCXVIII.---He confirms to the monastery of Steingaden the church of Widergeltingen. 1229  
CCCXIX.---Privilege for the monastery of Tepl. 1229  
CCCXX.---He takes the church of St. Mary of Arzilla at Fano under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges. 1230  
CCCXXI.---He confirms to the canons of St. Mary at Ronce the tithes of the newly cultivated lands of Ronce and Stampes. 1232  
CCCXXII.---He confirms the donations, foundations, and endowments made by Guy, lord of Salins, for the establishment of canons in the church of Blessed Mary at Salins. 1232  
CCCXXIII.---He writes to the brethren of Marmoutier concerning the repair of a certain chapel. 1233  
CCCXXIV.---He directs [Raynald], Bishop of Mâcon, [Robert], Bishop of Chalon, and the dean of Lons to compel Raynald, lord of Château-Raynald (diocese of Chalon), and Giles of Belfort (diocese of Besançon), to restore the goods taken from the priory of Louhans, belonging to the monastery of Tournus. 1233  
CCCXXV.---He appoints the Bishop of Lodi judge between the Bishop of Pavia and the canons of Piacenza. 1234  
CCCXXVI.---He confirms to Leontius of the monastery of St. Saviour at Messina and its monks the tithes granted by William, Archbishop of Reggio. 1234  
CCCXXVII.---To the Archbishop of Canterbury.---For restoring monks to the church of Coventry. 1234  
CCCXXVIII.---He takes the monastery of Cison under protection and confirms its discipline and possessions. 1236  

ANNO 1191–1198.

CCCXXIX.---He takes the church of St. Thomas of the Paraclete at Ebelholt under protection and confirms its possessions and rights. 1238  
CCCXXX.---He takes the monastery of Lieu-Dieu under protection and confirms its possessions. 1240  
CCCXXXI.---He takes the leper-house in the valley of Bugnes under protection and confirms to it “a portion of the forest of Cantastra, exempt from every exaction.” 1240  

SPURIOUS.

I.---Privilege for the monastery of Murbach. 1241  
II.---Privilege for the monastery of St. Modestus at Benevento. 1243  
III.---He replies to Philip, Bishop of Beauvais, that he deservedly suffers adversity because “he had stripped off the peaceful prelate and put on the warlike soldier”; and because, with his assistance, [Col. 1304] “the King of France, who was bound to the King of England by a bodily oath sworn to observe the inviolability of towns and lands, had shamelessly acted against faith and oath, violently occupied the king’s towns, and cruelly ravaged his land with a hostile hand.”---“At last, when returning from captivity, the King of England had met the King of France courageously; and on that account had fought humility against pride, law and equity against injury, moderation and restraint against arrogance and intemperance.” He adds that “he had sent supplicatory letters to the King of England on his behalf.” 1246  
IV.---To those who visit the altar of St. Mary in the church of St. Stephen at Bologna and lend helping hands for the condition and preservation of that church, he remits sins. 1247  

DECREES OF CELESTINE III.

I. — He replies to the bishop of Ambule that the Templars, Hospitallers, and others who have oratories in their houses are not permitted to install bells there or ring them publicly. 1247

II. — He commands the bishop of Abien to restore to the priest I. what has been taken from him. 1248

III. — He grants to Ralph, bishop of Angers, that those who cannot attain the rank of priest because of the impediment of age, if he finds that this alone stands in their way, may be tolerated until such time as he has established that they are fit to undertake the burden of the priesthood. 1249

IV. — He exhorts the patriarch of Aquileia to take care that provosts and others to whom, according to the custom of the land, the power is known to have been assigned of appointing persons to prebends in the place of deceased persons, do not substitute for the deceased their own sons, whom they have begotten while constituted in sacred orders. 1249

V. — He forbids all judges of Benevento that any of them should presume to act as advocate except in his own cause, or perhaps if he is bound to provide advocacy for some church or by reason of an obligation arising from someone’s benefaction. 1249

VI. — He replies to the chapter of Bisiuco that, if a layman, at the command of an abbot in whose service he resides, has presumed to lay rash hands upon a cleric, monk, or convert, both abbot and layman are to be regarded as excommunicated until they come to the Apostolic See. 1249

VII. — He replies to the bishop of Brugna [Brugnatensis]: first, that one who claims to have incurred a sentence of automatic excommunication can obtain the benefit of absolution only through the Apostolic See; secondly, that bigamous priests and husbands of widows are not to be admitted to the celebration of divine offices, whether their wives are living or dead. 1249

VIII. — He replies to the [arch]bishop of Brindisi concerning those who have taken an oath unwillingly in order to preserve their lives and property. 1249

IX. — He replies to the bishop of Saragossa that, when a prebend is vacant and several of those enrolled there raise an appeal, if they have not pursued the appeal within forty days, a canonical election is to proceed. 1249

X. — He replies to the archbishop of Canterbury that the appeal of one whom his adversary is prepared immediately to prove despoiled him, after the appeal had been lawfully lodged, is not to be deferred to. 1249

XI. — He replies to the archbishop of Canterbury that, if a criminal issue is litigated in a matrimonial case, the matter should be determined not through an intermediary person but through the principal matrimonial cause itself. 1249

XII. — He replies to a certain inquirer through W., dean of Cathalaven, that a woman who, believing her husband dead, has assumed the religious habit and, upon his return, has been removed from the monastery, is not to be compelled against her will, after her husband’s death, to observe the rule. 1249

XIII. — He informs the bishop of Le Mans that he has confirmed the elected abbot of Pelicea. 1249

XIV. — He commands certain persons to compel the archbishop to restore what he has taken from the monastery of Dol. 1250

XV. — He commands certain persons to compel a certain knight to pay B., archdeacon of Leun., tithes from the revenues of a mill. 1250

XVI. — He commands certain persons to order that tithes of hay from certain lands be paid to B., archdeacon of Dol. 1250

XVII. — He replies to the archbishop of York concerning a certain marriage. 1250

XVIII. — He commands the bishop of Exeter to annul leases of ecclesiastical estates made by canons. 1250

XIX. — He grants the abbot of St. Facundus that, whenever he is required to produce his privilege or any indulgence whatsoever [Col. 1305], the instrument is to be read aloud only by the judge himself, in the hearing of the opposing party; and the privilege is in no way to be handed over for copying. 1250

XX. — He replies to the bishop of Vam that trial by combat is not to be tolerated either in cases concerning the presentation to churches or in other cases. 1250

XXI. — He grants the bishop of Faenza that he may restore to its former state the monastery of Granden., which the prior had, without his authorization, subjected to the monastery of Cerat. 1250

XXII. — He commands all the oblates of the monastery of St. Peter of Fertum to obey the abbot. 1250

XXIII. — He writes to the archbishop of Otranto concerning John, who was ordained priest by a Greek bishop not at one of the four Ember seasons: “We do not wish henceforth that mixtures and customs of rites be observed in ordinations.” 1250

XXIV. — He commands the bishop of Lincoln and the abbots of Thaniae and Labrire to compel G. Bochis to restore a church to a certain priest. 1250

XXV. — He commands the bishop of Lincoln and Abbot T. to declare Lucy, widow, the legitimate daughter of G. and A. 1250

XXVI. — He commands the bishop of Lincoln, the prior of Fractoponte, and the archdeacon of Marin. to compel G[alfrid], archbishop of York, to restore money received from R., the provost. 1250

XXVII. — He replies to the chapter of Lucca that the clerics of Bari who, having been suspended by Bishop Vigilius, obtained ecclesiastical benefices are to be deprived of those benefices. 1250

XXVIII. — He replies to the chapter of Magdeburg that, since N., archdeacon of Le Mans, although dean of their church, has nevertheless chosen his residence rather in the regions of France, and their church has been unable to have his presence for the space of ten years, they are to elect a new dean unless he returns when summoned. 1250

XXIX. — He replies to certain persons that the son of the knight C., whom his father made assume the monastic habit while he was by no means of years of discretion, in a monastery of the province of Mainz, is not to be compelled to retain that habit if he does not wish to do so. 1250

XXX. — He commands the archbishop of Vidros [Nidaros] to refrain from communion with one who, through sacrilegious laying on of hands, has incurred the sentence of excommunication, even though he has not been publicly denounced. 1251

XXXI. — He commands the [canons of Poitiers] fully to receive as brother and canon Hugh of Le Mans, subdeacon, whom Jordan, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Pudentiana, has appointed a canon of their church, and to assign him a stall in choir and a place in chapter. 1251

XXXII. — He writes to the prior and canons of St. Ranierius that they should not doubt that an oath sworn concerning a fixed number of canons may be altered by the authority of the Apostolic See. 1251

XXXIII. — He commands certain persons to excommunicate I. de Malafrena, I., son of Cavalca, and their companions, who violently broke into the church of Miliaton and other churches of the diocese of Reggio. 1251

XXXIV. — He replies to [Walter], archbishop of Rouen, that those who have incurred excommunication for laying hands upon clerics or other religious persons are to be regarded as absolved when they have been absolved for the time being by cardinal legates sent from the side of the Roman pontiff, even though those legates do not show him an express mandate concerning these matters. 1251

XXXV. — He writes to [Walter], archbishop of Rouen, concerning the right of collegiate churches to present prelates. 1251

XXXVI. — He writes to [Walter, archbishop of Rouen?] concerning James the priest, who is not to be regarded as excommunicated. 1251

XXXVII. — He replies to the dean of Rouen, who consults him on various matters. 1252

XXXVIII. — He writes to the suffragans and dean of Rouen as follows: “Through forgers recently discovered in the City, certain letters have been sent out which we fear may be accepted by some as genuine. We therefore command that, if you can discover any such letters—which you will be able to recognize by comparison of the bull and by the character of the style—you have them seized and kept under close guard until this has been reported to us.” 1252

XXXIX. — He commands certain persons that, since Jews occupy a large part of the parish of St. Laud, unless the Jews living in the city of Rouen arrange annually to compensate the church of St. Laud, and the other churches whose parishes they hold occupied, for the tithes and all other revenues which they would receive from faithful parishioners if the faithful parishioners lived there, they are to bind with the bond of anathema all those marked with the character of Christ who may attempt to render service to Jews, borrow something from them, repay what has already been borrowed, conclude sales or leases with them, enter into any other contract, greet them, or hold conversation with them. [Col. 1306] 1252

XL. — He grants the bishop of Senigallia that, when an appeal has been made from his subjects to the Apostolic See, he may compel the appellant to set out for the Apostolic See within twenty days after the appeal has been lodged. 1252

XLI. — He replies to the bishop of Teramo that the marriage of C. is not to be dissolved: after swearing that he would take the daughter of V. as his wife, he changed his mind and married another. 1252

XLII. — He grants the abbot and convent of Vercelli that, if archbishops, archdeacons, archpriests, and deans, when visiting their churches, should presume to exceed the prescribed number of mounts and persons established at the Lateran Council, and demand procuration for them, the abbot and convent may refuse it. 1252

XLIII. — He commands the faithful established in the province of Vienne [Viennensis?] that, before deducting expenses from all goods collected, they are to pay tithes in their full due amount to the churches, without prejudice to the privileges of the Roman Church. 1253

XLIV. — He annuls this custom [of certain churches]: when the election of a prelate is to be confirmed, the convent names two persons, to be communicated secretly into the ears of the patriarch or prince, so that they may have the power either to elect one of them or to annul the whole election entirely. 1253

XLV. — He replies to a certain archbishop that it does not appear fitting for him to lend his pallium to another, since the pallium does not pass from one person to another. 1253

XLVI. — He replies to a certain archbishop concerning presentations. 1253

XLVII. — He replies to a certain bishop concerning persons who, absolved from excommunication by more distant judges, remain in an unlawful union of consanguinity. 1253

XLVIII. — He writes to a certain bishop that, on the pretext of an oath sworn not to alienate the property of the church, he should not neglect to provide beneficially for a needy people in the furnishing of basilicas. 1253

XLIX. — He replies to a certain bishop concerning the marriage of G. 1253

L. — He replies to a certain bishop that Henry, a priest, although he did not himself fight in a duel but someone fought on his behalf, ought not to minister in sacred orders. 1254

LI. — He commands a certain bishop to permit V., a deacon, to enjoy a certain benefice. 1254

LII. — He replies to a certain bishop concerning B., a cleric who, after betrothing a certain girl, was promoted to become a canon. 1254

LIII. — He grants a certain bishop that the illegitimate son of a certain knight may be promoted to sacred orders. 1254

LIV. — He commands a certain bishop to have W., a subdeacon, avoided by everyone as excommunicated until he dismisses a woman from his companionship. 1254

LV. — He replies to Master Columbo concerning delegated cases. 1254

LVI. — He replies to a certain person concerning the kind of incapacity meant by the clause often inserted in letters: namely, that if two, three, or even more persons to whom letters are directed cannot all be present together for their execution, one or more of them may nevertheless execute them. 1254

LVII. — He replies to a certain person that, if he had proved nothing against R. before the bishop of Dulmen and his co-judges, the sentence nevertheless had to stand unless R. showed that it should be annulled. 1254

LVIII. — He commands a certain person to order that a certain church be restored to D., a priest. 1254

LIX. — He replies to a certain person concerning an indulgence of Pope Adrian, of blessed memory, then bishop of Albano and legate in Norway, by which all persons of that land were permitted to marry within the sixth degree. 1254

LX. — In answer to someone’s questions, he replies concerning spiritual kinship. 1255

LXI. — He writes to a certain person that a merchant who has entered into the religious habit can neither cast off the habit nor marry any woman. 1259

LXII. — He commands certain persons that, if clerics residing in Paris have any secular lawsuits, they are to decide them according to canon law and are not to permit custom to prevail over written law. 1259

LXIII. — He replies to a certain person that he is not to allow B., a woman abandoned by A., to be harassed by the knight Peter concerning a certain house. 1259

LXIV. — He replies to a certain person concerning clerics caught in theft, homicide, or perjury. 1259

[Col. 1307]

LXV. — He replies to a certain person concerning a certain cell that wished to be exempted from the subjection owed to its mother church. 1259

LXVI. — He replies to a certain person concerning appointed judges. 1260

LXVII. — He replies to a certain person concerning appeals. 1260

LXVIII. — He replies to a certain person concerning testimonies. 1260

LXIX. — He replies to a certain person concerning public witnesses. 1260

LXX. — He replies to certain persons concerning P., an acolyte, who took up arms with certain men in order to resist robbers. 1261

## LETTERS OF VARIOUS PERSONS TO CELESTINE III

I. — Guarinus, abbot of St. Victor, to Celestine. — He congratulates him upon his promotion and commends to him the church of St. Victor. 1261

II. — Eleanor, queen of the English, to Celestine. — She implores the pontiff’s aid for the release of Richard, king of the English, her son. [Col. 1308] 1262

III. — Another letter from the same. — Of similar subject matter. 1265

IV. — A third letter from the same. — Of similar subject matter. 1268

V. — Deed of renunciation made by Peter Latro and Nepos to Lord Pope Celestine III. 1272

VI. — Charter of renunciation made to Pope Celestine III concerning the city of Castello by the sisters Constance and Sibyl, and Hyacinth, Peter Deus vos salvet, and the brothers Nicholas and Octavian. 1275

VII. — Ingeborg, queen of the French, to Celestine. — Because, while she herself was neglected, the king attached himself to the daughter of the duke of Merania. 1277

VIII. — Philip, bishop of Beauvais, to Celestine. — Concerning his capture. 1278

**INDEX TO THOMAS OF CÎTEAUX.** 1279

**INDEX TO JOHN ALGRIN.** 1289

[Col. 1307]

**END OF THE TWO HUNDRED AND SIXTH VOLUME.**
